ResponsesInList.Title: Turnitin Similarity Reports Missing for Quiz Essay Questions after Upgrading to Moodle 5.0 (with latest Turnitin plugin 2025070201)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello everyone, I’m reaching out regarding an issue with Turnitin plagiarism detection in Moodle quiz essay questions after upgrading from Moodle 4.2.2+ (Build: 20230822) to Moodle 5.0 (Build: 20240624) . 🔍 Context In Moodle 4.2.2+ , Turnitin plagiarism checking worked perfectly inside quiz essay questions . After students submitted a quiz, each essay response was sent to Turnitin automatically, generating a Turnitin ID (for example, `2400266315` ) and displaying a similarity percentage below the answer. Instructors could click the pencil icon to open the Similarity Report. However, after upgrading to Moodle 5.0 , this functionality stopped working entirely: Essay responses are no longer submitted to Turnitin. No Turnitin IDs or similarity scores are generated. The “Enable Turnitin for Quiz” setting is still available and turned ON. Turnitin continues to work correctly for Assignments, Forums, and Workshops — the issue is specific to Quiz essays. ⚙️ Current Environment Component Version Moodle version 5.0 (Build: 20240624) Turnitin Plagiarism Plugin 2025070201 (released July 2, 2025) PHP version 8.2.18 Database MariaDB 10.11.6 Web server Nginx 1.24.0 Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS Feedback Studio Not in use (Similarity Check only license) 🧩 Observation In Moodle 4.2.2+, the Turnitin plugin relied on the following event observer: 
```text
\mod_quiz\event\attempt_submitted
```
 In Moodle 5.0, this event appears to have been deprecated or refactored . The quiz module now triggers different events such as `core_question_answered` and `mod_quiz_attempt_reviewed` , which the current Turnitin plugin does not listen to. As a result, the plugin no longer detects quiz submissions and therefore doesn’t send essay responses to the Turnitin API. No errors appear in the Moodle logs or the Turnitin diagnostic logs — the event simply never fires. 📉 Result Moodle Version Status Behavior 4.2.2+ ✅ Working Turnitin IDs generated for quiz essays 4.3.x ⚠️ Intermittent Some partial compatibility 5.0 ❌ Not working No API call triggered, no report Plugin v2025070201 ❌ Not resolved Still no event observer for quiz ❓ Questions for the Development Team Has official support for quiz essay questions been intentionally deprecated in the latest Turnitin plugin (2025070201)? If not, is there a plan to restore this feature in the upcoming Moodle 5.1+ compatible plugin release? Are there any recommended workarounds (e.g., custom local plugin or event observer using `core_question_answered` ) to re-enable quiz essay submissions to Turnitin? Has anyone successfully tested this with Moodle 5.1 and confirmed whether the issue is fixed? 🧠 Additional Notes Our instructors regularly use essay-type questions in quizzes for reflective or short analytical writing, and they rely on Turnitin similarity checking for academic integrity. Moving all essays to separate Turnitin Assignment activities is pedagogically inconvenient. We would prefer to maintain quiz-based workflows if this feature can be re-enabled or patched. Any confirmation, patch, or insight from the Turnitin or Moodle HQ developers would be greatly appreciated. I can provide detailed logs, screenshots, or test results from both environments (4.2.2+ where it worked, and 5.0 where it stopped) if needed. Thanks in advance for your time and support. Best regards, Yunus Akarsu Educational Technologies Specialist Kadir Has University – Istanbul, Türkiye

ResponsesInList.Title: How to expand the width of rubric marking tables (solution) / improvement
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I was going crazy about the width of my rubrics (Boost theme), so I turned to the Moodle community and found this forum post - Moodle in English: How to expand the width of rubric marking tables (solution) | Moodle.org Thank you, Eoin Campbell, for this! I just put 90% instead of "none" (Discussion locked so I cannot reply to it directly) However, I was still not entirely satisfied, so I combined it with another bit of code I came across during Moodle Moot Francophone 2024 in Marseille! Sorry I can't credit the person who shared because I don't have access to the discussion anymore. So it goes (Raw SCSS): /* Grading for rubrics  - make the KDSC marking rubric table wide for tutors to use */ .path-mod-assign .fullwidth[data-region="grade-panel"] [data-region="grade"] { max-width:90%;} /* Narrow the description part of the rubric table */ .gradingform_rubric .criterion .description {width: 20%;} It's not yet perfect, but much better, let me show you 😌 Original display of the rubric (big screen) Only with Eoin's code and 90% width (big screen) Combined with the other code from Moodle Moot Francophone 2024 (big screen) And the same thing on a smaller screen You can see it's still not perfect on a bigger screen, so if anyone has any idea to improve it, it would be great! Thanks again to Eoin and the other person who shared their workaround!

Does your page have these? As you've probably determined the Assignment activity's `module.js` contains the `init_tree` definition. If this isn't loaded it's no surprise that there's an error. You can set up an assignment on the sandbox site to compare this with your site. You'll see the `mod/assign/view.php?id=<ID>` page contains the above `<script>` elements and `module.js` is loaded for the page. We need to determine what's preventing this from happening on your site. If your site isn't using the default Boost theme, try switching to this and see if the problem still occurs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignment Notification Emails: Links No Longer Direct to Student Submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I’m reaching out to check if others are experiencing an issue with assignment submission email notifications in Moodle 4.5 LTS. Background: Previously: In earlier versions of Moodle, when a student submitted an assignment, the email notification sent to graders included a link that would take them directly to the specific student’s submission for grading. Current Issue: After upgrading to Moodle 4.5 LTS, these notification links now take graders to the assignment’s general assignment grading summary page instead of directly opening the individual student’s submission. Testing Notes: I tested an older notification email (from before the update), and it now also redirects to the general submission box instead of the specific submission. This behavior persists for all new assignment notifications as well. Questions: Has anyone else encountered this change in behavior in Moodle 4.5 LTS? Is this an intentional change in Moodle’s core functionality (e.g., for security reasons or standardization)? Are there any settings, workarounds, or customizations available to restore the previous functionality, where links go directly to the student’s submission? Additional Info: We don’t have any plugins that modify assignment notifications. Our Moodle admin believes this might be a change to Moodle’s core functionality but wasn’t able to confirm. Any insights, guidance, or experiences would be greatly appreciated! Thanks in advance, Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: PDF annotation - disk size
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the question more relates how long these artefacts are necessary to hold on to, or if there is a better way to handle these cases. Displaying a blank PDF for a case where there is not feasible way to create a valid PDF does seem like a waste of resources and processing. Detecting that a blank PDF is the output (or technical no valid inputs), and then displaying a relevant message & disabling the annotate PDF option would give better feedback. You could argue that the generation of the "Blank" PDF allows for some arbitrary feedback file creation, but this doesn't really entirely hold up, as you're limited to one single page, so it's not a "full" creator option. Finally if in cases where it's "known" that there's going to be no more processing (or lets say "immediate" need) for the intermediary files, then may be they should be cleaned up and re-generated when actually needed, rather than being kept "in case" they're needed. One example of this would be if the " context freezing" feature ( https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Context_freezing ) is in use (yes I know it's experimental), but other functions like it being after the course end date, or the submission has been graded.

The core issues is HOW we are producing the PDF's.  For what I consider really bad reasons (fears about malicious links, there are comments in tracker outlining this) every page is flattened to an image.  That's the core problem, PDFs are orders of magnitude bigger than they need to be, not that they exist.  This is in addition to the processing overhead this causes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Improvement suggestion: Hide assign submissions page columns by default
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey E.T - the first few "Identity" columns are controlled by the Site Admin setting for Users - User Policies - Show User Identity (unchecking Email address there would then hide it, but it would hide it *everywhere* else as well such as gradebooks, Participants/Enrolled Users page, reports, etc....); however, because these columns are added by that setting it will include a special CSS class which makes it certainly easy to hide via CSS. For example, the Email Address column gets a class of "email", so it can be hidden for example with code such as #page-mod-assign-grading .header.c3.email, #page-mod-assign-grading .cell.c3.email { display: none; } You'd have to check your browser tools to make sure it's "column 3 (c3)" but that is an example how you can hide one of the Identity columns by default on the assignment quick grading page

Inside the 'MORE' menu, you see 'Grant attempt' which on single student selection is 'allow another attempt' Inside the 'MORE' menu, you see ' Upload feedback'. Which could also be an option for a single user to avoid going to the grading screen So you see, there's a lot of inconsistency in this user interface. ResponsesInList.Title: Deleting uploaded files without deleting the grade
ResponsesInList.Text: Question: The video file student submit ... was/is there a requirement for the filename of the video?   Like student George Jones has to use gjones-intro.mp4 when submitted? Reason asked ... A file uploaded to moodle goes into /moodledata/filedir/ by the contenthash value seen in a DB query of mdl_files table. Looks like: zzy9zzy9abunchoflowercasecharacters and is located in moodledata/filedir/zz/y9/ by the of the contenthash value. One could do a query of mdl_files table for filename,filesize,contenthash (maybe other columns) to find the specific video file in moodledata/filedir/xx/xx/xxxxetc. and then replace it with a 0 byte file by the same name. The DB reference doesn't change .... meta data would still show a link to an .mp4 video by whatever name, but the file itself isn't anything ... thus, am thinking, everything in gradebook/feedback is the same. Top of head idea ... could change future assignment to a video that students have in their 'outside of moodle space' ... YouTube? Google Drive?, other such thing. Students then just provide a link to the video - no space issues with your moodle then. Comment: in a 'forever course' like that, should you decide to change the assignment and use something else and then delete the old assignment with all those video's, strongly suggest setting the recyclebin time to retain to 1 second.   That would hurry along the assignment videos to moodledata/trashdir/ where one can manually erase files. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Turnitin Grade Me mark up not displaying with anon sumbissions on
ResponsesInList.Text: When anonymous submissions is turned on in an assignment and grades released (ether partially or fully) students cannot see their Grade Me Turnitin feedback until identities are revealed for all. T here is no pencil next to the TII report in the submission window in student view (to see the Grade Me markup) The students can see the grade and the similarity score, but not Grade Me annotations or comments. Students cannot see the pencil/ Grade Me mark up until student identities are revealed. Anon identites revealed and grades released the pencil is there. I suspect the issue is a conflict between Moodle anon workflow and TII anon workflow. ResponsesInList.Text: `Cookie: {cookieStuff}` Getting an undefined error is one thing. But getting logged out as a result? That's very strange. And in your Response Headers screenshot is `Set-Cookie: MoodleSession=f4r8...` . That looks to me like Moodle logging you out, and indeed that's what's happening to you. But Moodle shouldn't do this just because there's an error. When you log in Moodle sends a new MoodleSession cookie value. Then every browser request contains that cookie, until you log out when Moodle sends `Set-Cookie: MoodleSession=...` with a new value. When you click Grade with Network Monitor open in your browser tools so that the error occurs work back from `r.php/api/rest/v2/user/current/preferences` and check the Request Headers and Response Headers. The Request Headers should all contain `Cookie: MoodleSession=` and this should be the same value. The Response Headers should not contain `Set-Cookie: MoodleSession=` . Is this the case?, i.e. is `r.php/api/rest/v2/user/current/preferences` the first request containing `Set-Cookie: MoodleSession=` ? I realise there's a lot of technical debugging here but I'm struggling to imagine what might be causing this. ModSec could be involved, but the fact you're seeing error/You do not have permission to edit this preference – which is sent by Moodle – makes me doubt this, unless ModSec is altering the browser's request for some reason. I think Ken knows ModSec better than me so maybe he's got ideas of places to look.

ResponsesInList.Text: To stop the cron from the looping, add this line to config.php $CFG->cron_keepalive='0'; Do you have your cron setup with the 'la-la-land' redirect? You could change that redirect to a log file that is constantly overwritten and be able to watch the log file in realtime with tail -f /var/log/moodle-cron.log How to: touch /var/log/moodle-cron.log chown apache:apache /var/log/moodle-cron.log Then in setup of the cron job .... > /var/log/moodle-cron.log You could do that for all your moodles ... only to different log files. I have a server with multiple moodles running. /var/log//mdlandcli-cron.log /var/log/mdlsamples-cron.log /var/log/m44sb-cron.log Can watch those logs via: tail -f /var/log/m44sb-cron.log When it runs for the m44sb instance, I see what it is doing in realtime. Leave setup of cron to run once every minute .... yes, with multiple instances of moodle that will spike memory usage but not for long. I do multiple moodle sites using a bash shell script that has 3 one liners ... each line runs different moodle instance. In the setup of cron job, I point to that script ... they each run, 1 at a time. Not all task in cron will run at same time ... so some runs of cron job are actually less than other runs.   Obviously, the moodle that is used will have more to do and your sandbox instances will have less. ResponsesInList.Title: Do they receive notifications of these comments?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ricardo, For Assignments, there is a difference "Submission Comments" and "Feedback" (see this thread: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=312090 ). There are no notifications when a user leaves/receives Submission Comments. However, there are [Notifications] if a user receives Feedback on an assignment, but that needs to be enabled in the user menu and when the teacher Leaves the feedback, they must check the "Notify Student" box. It might be useful to add a test Student account into your course (with a working email address) and submit to the assignment as a test, then login as the teacher and leave the feedback for the test submission and then see how the test student account receives the feedback.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preserve clickable hyperlinks in assignment converted to PDF
ResponsesInList.Text: The issue is that the document conversion process, to allow for the inline-annotation converts the student submission into a PDF, and the unstitches the PDF into separate pages. Each page is actually created as an image to allow the Moodle annotator to display it in your web browser, so by this point there is no information about the "text" or the URL , you're basically looking at a picture of the students page. When your annotations get saved however, their positions on top of the image of each page are then used to write the annotations into a "real" PDF, based on the original converted work, which is why the the annotated PDF the student gets in their feedback files has all the text selectable. At the moment there's no way to access / display the converted PDF file in your browser, which would allow your browser's PDF capabilities to open the web links in the content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing the color of the Assignment activity
ResponsesInList.Text: I do this by adding in CSS - note, it isn't possible to target just the assignment icon, you have to target all of the 'assessment' icons (e.g. Quiz and a few others). (change the XXXXXX to the color code you want. /*Changes the background colour of assessment activity icons*/ .activityiconcontainer.assessment{ background-color: #XXXXXX; } If you need to change others, then they are: .activityiconcontainer.collaboration .activityiconcontainer.communication .activityiconcontainer.content .activityiconcontainer.other .activityiconcontainer.administration Some themes having settings built in to allow you to do the same, without having to add in CSS. If you have any third party activities which don't have up to date icons, then you may need this code as well: /*Inverts the colour (e.g. makes black svg into white) for the 3rd party activity plugins*/ .activityiconcontainer.other .activityicon, .activityiconcontainer.other .icon { filter: brightness(0) invert(1); }

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: notifications to teachers/graders not being received for Assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I know, if teachers have the capability moodle/site:accessallgroups, they should receive all notifications, regardless if a user is in multiple groups. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: notifications to teachers/graders not being received for Assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Correct - backing up what Helen has posted - there are two permissions you need to check here: mod/assign:receivegradernotifications - if this is not set to allow, they won't get emails. moodle/site:accessallgroups - by default for teacher and non-editing teacher this will be set to allow, but (and I regularly do this) it may be set to 'Prevent' - if it is set to prevent then the person will only get an email if they are in the same group as the person submitting. remember you can change permissions at different levels - so if the site settings for 'accessallgroups' is set to prevent, you can always tweak the permissions for a single activity (assignment) to change this to allow.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can teacher deal with student submitted file & then, remove submission
ResponsesInList.Text: Well noted with thanks. My suggestion #1 is to delete "remove submission" button for assignment if possible. However, this button can be kept for the Submission settings with "Require students to click the submit button --> Yes". It is because with the default setting as "No" here, students can remove submission & Moodle allows NO files with "submitted for grading". If this setting is "Yes", student CANNOT remove submission without replacing file. However, with "NO", students can submit many times before the due or cut-off date. With "Yes", once students confirm the submission, they CANNOT submit anymore even the due or cut-off date is not finished yet. #2 is that Remove button can be kept in this default Submission setting. However, just like the case of "Yes", student CANNOT remove submission files without anything. #3 is that Remove button can be kept in this default Submission setting. However, if student removed submission, the submission status changed to "removed submission without anything" or simply "removed submission". This can make both teachers & students understand that the files had been removed by the students. Thank you very much!

ResponsesInList.Title: Gradebook 'Exclude empty grades' documentation error?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, hopefully someone can help me here - I'm not sure if I'm just not understanding something right, or whether there is an error in the documentation. I'm referring to Grade category settings>Aggregate only non-empty grades . It says: With "Exclude Empty Grades" enabled Any ungraded work is assumed to be a zero, which might be used to show students the impact of missing work on their overall grade. This can be a motivator for students to submit all assignments. With "Exclude Empty Grades" disabled Students’ averages are based only on the work they’ve completed and been graded for. This is often used to give students the benefit of the doubt until all grades are in, encouraging continuous participation without penalising them for grades that haven't been entered yet. However, my understanding is that when it is enabled, i.e. set to ignore ('exclude') empty grades, it will ignore ungraded work, and therefore only calculate an overall total based on what has already been graded - i.e. the second explanation above. It's puzzling me... I have been doing tests with a 'Drop the lowest' scenario (drop the two lowest grades out of five), and the behaviour when I enable 'Exclude empty grades' does not seem to be consistent with the above explanation in the documentation. Or maybe I'm just not seeing something obvious... And I've just noticed that above that, on the same page, it says this: If this option is enabled, Moodle will ignore any grade item that has no grade when calculating the category or course total. If it is disabled, Moodle will treat empty grades as zero when calculating averages or totals

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook 'Exclude empty grades' documentation error?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Julian! 😊 First, it's important to understand how the "Exclude empty grades" setting really works. When this option is enabled , Moodle ignores the assignments that have not yet been graded. This means that when calculating the average, only the grades that have already been assigned are considered. In other words, if you have a student who hasn't submitted some assignments, those assignments will not affect their average since Moodle does not consider them as zeros. On the other hand, when the option is disabled , Moodle assumes that the unsubmitted assignments are zeros, which can cause the student's average to drop. This approach is designed to encourage students to submit their work by showing the impact that missing submissions can have on their final grade. Regarding your question about the behavior during tests with "Drop the lowest grades," if the "Exclude empty grades" option is enabled, Moodle should indeed ignore the unassigned grades when calculating the total, maintaining the evaluations that have already been completed. If you notice that the logic is not applying correctly, it might be worthwhile to check if there are any additional settings influencing the expected behavior. Eduardo Kraus Professor and programmer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook 'Exclude empty grades' documentation error?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Eduardo - I understand how it works, and the testing I did supports what you are saying, but I think the explanation on the documentation is wrong. It says that when the option is enabled: Any ungraded work is assumed to be a zero , which might be used to show students the impact of missing work on their overall grade. i.e. it is not ignoring it. I think that there is an error in the documentation. Does that make sense?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Gradebook 'Exclude empty grades' documentation error?
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with you Julian, I think the explanations are the wrong way round so I've updated the docs accordingly. The Moodle Docs are a wiki that anyone can edit . Feel free to create an account and revise these further if my changes need further correction.

ResponsesInList.Title: Automatically send video to students who submitted their assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey, Simply, I want whenever a student submit his homework/assignment a video answering the homework become visible or is sent to the student .. Is there anyway to do something like this or something close to it ? Thanks in advance

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatically send video to students who submitted their assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: There may be several ways to do this. I'll suggest one way. Create a URL resource, and "restrict access" on it for the assignment to be "marked as complete." In other words, hide the video's URL until the assignment is marked as complete. I don't think you want to show this URL simply when someone submits because some students might immediately submit a bogus file so that they see the video, then later on, resubmit their correct file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatically send video to students who submitted their assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: A lot depends on what completion setting you want on the assignment. If you are happy for the assignment to be complete once a submission is made then what Rick has suggested would work - or you could use the filter codes plugin https://moodle.org/plugins/filter_filtercodes and have the desired video embedded inside the assignment description itself, but initially hidden with the {ifactivitycompleted id}{/ifactivitycompleted} tags. Once the user has submitted, the assignment would be marked as complete and the video would then be visible. The advantage of this is that it keep it all within a single item. However - if you want the assignment to only be considered complete, once the teacher has marked it and given it a pass score, then the video would only be visible once the tutor has marked it, not once the student has submitted it. The only way round this (which is a bit cack handed) is set the assignment as complete when work is submitted - this then releases the video, but then have a parallel pulse activity ( https://moodle.org/plugins/mod_pulse ) which you make available once they have achieved a certain score for the assignment (e.g. the pass score) - you can then track completion of this for your overall course level tracking.

ResponsesInList.Title: Automatically validating (and rejecting?) assignment submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: We currently require students to upload a zipfile as their assignment submission, which our human markers subsequently unzip and investigate. Is it feasible to run a custom check on those files as part of Moodle's assignment submission process such that the submission gets rejected if it doesn't meet some specified criteria (e.g., a known file of non-zero size within the zip)? Alternatively if that isn't possible — and as our custom checks get more complex (unpacking and running Python files from the zip in a sandbox) it feels like it's not reasonable for that to be within the Moodle's submission pipeline — is it possible to specify HTTP webhooks (instead of email) notifications? Those could trigger such a process to run separately whenever a submission is made. It feels like the sort of thing there might be a plugin for but I haven't found it. Is there anyone out there who is already doing something like this? A little more context : Although the Moodle assignment setup allows us to specify a maximum upload file size, there's no minimum, right? We've had students goof up and submit a zip file that only contains a Windows shortcut to the their local folder, and if we could specify a minimum upload size we could prevent those submissions — but obviously a better general case would be to run an arbitrarily complex check on the uploaded zip and accept/reject based on that. By the time we're doing that, it seems we could more usefully be running specific tests on the files within the zipfile, rather than the coarse "zip is infeasibly small"... which is why I'm asking if anyone else is doing this already. Thanks for any pointers!

An extra complication — which presumably is not that uncommon in big institutions — is that we don't run the Moodle instance ourselves, so anything we implement _before_ submission is going to be easier for us to manage than something we can wrangle onto the Moodle itself. Ideally I'd never have students submit code like this (it's Python) as a zip; a better solution is for them to be using a version control system (such as GitLab) to which we have access. This business of submitting a zip of source code already feels like something of an anachronism... but it's where we're at, at the moment. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manage Report: SQL Query
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume that you have configured each "exam" as an Assignment in your course. You should be able to use the course Gradebook setup to create 3 Categories: a parent category "Admin/Domain", and two child categories "Admin" and "Domain". Then move the grade item for each Assignment into one or other of the child categories. The category grade value will be the overall grade for each set of assignments (the sum or mean of all the grade item scores), and this will indicate whether a student has passed or not. If students are in 3 separate groups, then you can export a grade report for each group separately, and get the information you need.

ResponsesInList.Title: Setting Up Dual Marking Workflow
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Everyone, I'm currently facing a challenge in setting up an efficient dual marking system for assignments on Moodle and would like your thoughts and advice. We aim to ensure that two teachers evaluate each assignment to maintain a robust assessment process. The ideal workflow would involve the first marker being automatically assigned based on the student's group allocation (e.g., the teacher responsible for that particular group). Alternatively, having the capability for all teachers to view the assignments and then delegate via email who should mark which student's work could also work for us. However, we need help to establish a transparent and streamlined process. We attempted to utilise the marking allocation feature within Moodle, but it appears only to support the assignment of a single marker per submission . ResponsesInList.Title: Offline grading won't accept windows csv files
ResponsesInList.Text: We are having problems with offline grading, when using Windows and Excel. An error message about file type and delimiter type is shown whichever kind of CSV file exported to. For Mac OS we got it working with the instructions below, but can anyone tell how to make it work with Windows? MacOSX The assignment should be set to use Worksheets for offline grading under the Types of Feedback section Go to the task and select View all submissions In the Grading Action drop-down menu, select Download Grading Worksheet Now you have a csv file for the task. Open a new document in Excel, select Import and select the CSV file you just downloaded Complete the process to get the CSV file into the cells of the datasheet Enter grades and feedback in the Grade and Feedback comments columns Select Save as... and select the file format CSV UTF-8 (comma-separated values, .csv) Now you will upload the CSV file you just saved to transfer the grades to the assignment in Moodle Go to the task and select Show all submissions In the Grading Action drop-down menu, select Upload Grading Worksheet At the file upload, select your file and specify Semicolon as Separator! Even though it says "comma-separated" in the file type, it becomes a semicolon when the file is exported from Excel. Upload and check in the preview that it looks right, and then perform the grading.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Offline grading won't accept windows csv files
ResponsesInList.Text: See How to change Excel CSV delimiter to comma or semicolon : "What delimiter Excel uses for CSV files To handle .csv files, Microsoft Excel uses the List separator defined in Windows Regional settings . In North America and some other countries, the default list separator is a comma, so you get CSV comma delimited.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle group assignment locks 'grouping' setting
ResponsesInList.Text: If you have ABCDE in a grouping (chronologically in January) and this groupings is just called "Assignment Groups", this just governs who's working together. And this just governs the people working together for these groups (presumably they're not the same set of students as January?) ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing student submission date
ResponsesInList.Text:
I don't think this date can be changed within Moodle. I think it should be fine to change this in the database. Some notes: Always take a back up of the database before making changes such as this. Presumably the affected students have made only one attempt. If not you
may need to specify the attempt number in the UPDATE statement so that only the records with the correct `mdl_assign_submission.attemptnumber` are modified. Moodle stores date/times using the Unix epoch format . Make sure the values for the new date/times are correct for your timezone. The course and site logs will
show the events (for example, A submission has been submitted ) at their
original times. This won't create a problem in the database but may be
confusing if someone reviews the student's actions in the
future. When I tested this I used the following queries ( MySQL / MariaDB ): 1. Get the IDs for the affected students: 
```text
SELECT id FROM mdl_user WHERE username IN ('student1', 'student2');
```
 2. Get the mod_assign ID for the affected course activity: 
```text
SELECT instance FROM mdl_course_modules WHERE id = 123;
```
 3. Change the students' submissions' modified dates to 12:30 UTC today.: 
```text
UPDATE mdl_assign_submission


  SET timemodified = UNIX_TIMESTAMP('2024-03-17 12:30:00')


  WHERE assignment = 52


  AND  userid IN (9, 10);
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Revealing Moodle Assignment feedback before grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Is there any way to reveal Moodle assignment feedback to the students in advance of their grades?  As far as I can see, the expectation is that Moodle assignment grades and feedback will always be released together. There are two reasons for the enquiry: From an administrative point of view: At our institution, a QA statement requires that staff provides assignment feedback within 3 weeks and grades within 5 weeks.  Although staff could release both grades and feedback (together) within 3 weeks of submission (and still comply with the institutional QA statement), they frequently want to release the grades at the 5 week mark (which gives them extra time for moderation etc.) From a pedagogical point of view: There is an increasing interest in being able to give students their feedback in advance of their grades in order to encourage them to focus and respond to the feedback (rather than the end grade) - being able to deliver the two elements separately would be extremely helpful in this respect. We are currently using Moodle 4.1 - planning to move to 4.3 in August 2024. Many thanks, Lisa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Revealing Moodle Assignment feedback before grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lisa, I would say this depends on what the assignment entails. If it is some sort of writing assignment, such as an essay, this can be easily done with the Journal or Diary plugins, with Diary be MUCH more versatile. Both allow the teacher to provide feedback without giving a rating/grade. Diary has the added benefit of being able to give some automatic grading recommendations based on the activity settings. If it is some sort of file submission, you still might be able to do it with Journal or Diary. If you assignment is something else, all I can think of would be to use an email to provide the feedback, but this has the huge disadvantage of not being an actual part of the original assignment. Full disclosure. I maintain the Diary plugin and have plans to add more capability to it that would enhance it's automatic feedback/rating system. My problem is finding the time to do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Revealing Moodle Assignment feedback before grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lisa, This is where things get complicated in a Moodle world! Firstly the link between grade and feedback is set by the relevant *plugins*, not Moodle per se. However in the Moodle Gradebook, any feedback that is transcribe into it will be displayed at the same time and subject to the same view controls as the gradebook item. For the Assignment however, this is further complicated! If the grade item for the is set to hidden then neither grade nor feedback should be hidden. However *if* you have blind marking enabled, and you grade and feedback a student, the *grade* only will be hidden from the students (and is also not passed on to the gradebook) but the feedback comments *are* displayed (and it is for this reason that we tell all our staff to set grade items to hidden!) The grade item visibility in the gradebook is the thing that governs *both* being displayed... Arguably this is a bug in blind marking as it potentially leaks the results of the process to the student, but at the same time it does also set the visibility in the gradebook as the *master* switch on visibility of the item...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Revealing Moodle Assignment feedback before grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Michael. Some of our staff have been using blind marking as a way around this issue, but I'm slightly wary of recommending this approach at a wider institutional level given that it relies on what appears to be a bug. Having done a bit more digging, I've just spotted this: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-57006 - recently closed with a final comment that I think recognises some of those complexities that you mention. Unfortunately it sounds like we'll have to wait and hope that a wider review of feedback/grade release is on the agenda.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: All assignments complete -> attendance not required. Any ideas?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jennifer. I cannot think of a way to fully automate what you want to achieve here, but I can offer a slight alternative, which is to use the 'Pulse' plugin - I have written a blog post about this (includes a video) at https://davefoord.wordpress.com/2022/01/18/moodle-tricks-of-the-trade-course-completion-based-on-different-activities-for-different-people/ The basic approach would be to have a pulse item for each 'session' and the pulse is made available if the student has either completed the assignment or attended the session (yes you would need to turn activity completion on for this to work). You then set the pulse to itself be complete once available. Then when the tutor wants to check attendance they use the activity completion report, and look down the column for the session in question, and any missing ticks are the people that need chasing. It feels a bit like a hammer to crack a nut solution, but once set up, would make it very easy for the tutor to know who to chase. Dave Foord

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: All assignments complete -> attendance not required. Any ideas?
ResponsesInList.Text: Having worked & done development against both of these plugins, the short answer is "no". You're basically looking at a dependency / interaction between 2 completely separate plugins that have no awareness of each other (I'm assuming you're using mod_attendance and mod_assign). So: 1 & 2) No you'd need some process to be able to observe the completion change and do this. 3) No - there's no way to sync group memberships really, (well there is but it's really techie, and requires an enrolment method to trigger the group sync and it's quite convoluted) If you have technical development available it *could* be coded around, for instance you could have an assignment submission plugin that is (somehow) aware of a corresponding attendance activity, which then tries to set all future attendance at sessions to a specific value. But this would require that plugin to be written, and have an awareness of exactly what sessions it should mark and what value should be marked with, both of which are configured in a different plugin and (generally) by people, so could be inconsistent... But such an assignment submission plugin could in principle be created...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Different Grade Letters for Different Assignments within the same Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Each assignment has a defined "Marking Guide", with each question having an allocated number of marks. So, for example, an assignment has a maximum of 80 marks ... the tutor will go through the assignment and mark the assignment, at the end the learner will have a number of marks for the assignment ... so, for instance, if the marks the learner had ended up totalling say 54 out of 80 (that would equate to 67.5% of the total marks available) ... and if it was a pass only assignment, that would give a "Pass" grade (as it is over 60%), but if it was pass/merit/distinction assignment, the same mark would give a "Merit" (as it between 65% and 69.99%). I hope that clarifies enough for you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Different Grade Letters for Different Assignments within the same Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi hi! I think the feature you're looking for is called an " Outcome ". Here's the MoodleDoc for it . Outcomes will allow you to create a small grade item that has a text item associated it with it—such as "Resubmit", or "Pass".  You attach the Outcome to the Assignment, and then two items are displayed in the gradebook: one for the outcome, and one for the Assignment.  This will allow you to retain using score/marking guide grading on the Assignment, while also enabling you to create a kind of "grade letter" attached.  Instructors manually select the outcome for the item, and to make sure it's clear, you'll probably want to do some gradebook reorganization. Here's a basic idea of what that looks like: I believe you can define these at the course-level.

This means that students can share their test essays, including the writing prompt, with future classes. While writing prompts can be changed, the ability to download previous test materials creates a strong temptation for students to "help out" their friends. Sharing of previous test materials is seen by my institution as a form of academic dishonesty. Or is there another way to administer the assessment outside of using an assignment? Thank you for your ideas and support!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disallowing students from accessing past assignment submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: I have done something similar with other activities (e.g. once they have completed, you deny them access to it), and this should work with the assignment activity. Firstly set the assignment to be marked as complete on submission. We then use activity completion restriction to restrict access to the assignment - you have probably already worked out, that you cannot do this directly, e.g. the assignment itself won't appear within its own list of possible restrictions, but you can create a triangular relationship to do this as follows: I use either the checklist plugin or the pulse plugin: If using the checklist you set this to contain 1 item (the assignment) and mark it as complete if 100% of items are ticked off. So the checklist will mirror the assignment's completion status. You can then add the checklist as the restriction to the assignment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Submitting Video Assessments
ResponsesInList.Text: In addition to Emma's questions, one more ... What is the typical file size of a 10 minute video? Depending upon bitrate of a MP4 video (commonly used), those files could be between 400 MB to 775 MB.   If 10 students are submitting videos at the same time that's a lot of data headed to your server at one time. Large files will take time to transfer and load. Could be that your moodle server just can't handle the load - a factor is, of course, bandwidth (the 'wire' and how much data can be sent on that wire as well as server allowing or being able to handle that much data).   Hosting providers do have bandwidth limits. Something you need to keep an eye on is space.  400 MB X 10 students gets into Gigabyte ranges and your space in moodledata/filedir grows.   Server will begin to exhibit strange behavior.   And if your DB server and DB for moodle is on the same server, could result in not enough space for the DB. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Submitting Video Assessments
ResponsesInList.Text: I think it is probably that they are uploading large files and somewhere on the network (could be their wifi/3g/4g r) there is a timeout. Its also possible that your Site/Course/Activity upload size limit is too low. So you should check and if necessary adjust your upload file size limit: https://docs.moodle.org/402/en/File_upload_size A ten minute video file if recorded from a chrome web browser is not that big. But mobile phones with their super cameras make big files. There are settings usually on the phone to switch from HD to FD (or some similar setting) and that will reduce file size. But after they have already recorded, they will need to use some app to reduce the file size. It is probably too hard to get it across to students, but if they were to upload to Google Drive and share the link with you that would work too. Finally, if you do this video upload sort of thing often, you might look at the Cloud Poodll Assignment Submission. It allows you to accept video uploads into the assignment and manages the conversion and cloud storage of them. And I am the Poodll Guy, so I am biased.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Having Multiple Submissions in one Assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: In that case, here are some suggestions: Database activity - it is built in to Moodle, but you will have set up your own preset of the fields you want to use. I do remember a preset that was available at one time for something  like this. Each time the user needs to, they add a new entry. Journal - It used to be built in to Moodle but is now an activity plugin that you would need to install. The down side is, while students can come back and modify their entry, it is just a one page entry that gets longer and longer, each time they add to it, leading to the "scroll of death." Diary - I would recommend that you try this one, just note that I maintain it, so I am a little prejudiced. Diary is also a plugin you would need to install. It is based off the Journal plugin, with many, many, many additions. Some of the most notable are that users can make new, separate entries, add to old entries, or it can be set to have it work just like the Journal, etc. A rather recent addition is that you can set up time released writing prompts that tell the user what is NOW required. If you so desire there are a few things that can be set up to use for automatic grading: character count, word count, sentence count and paragraph count. You can also set up a glossary of common errors, that also get graded automatically. e.g. i instead of I, u instead of you, etc. You can create a student account and take a look at it here: https://m3x.drachels.com/course/view.php?id=4 Note send me an email and I can give you teacher access so you can try it "your" way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to setup multiple graders
ResponsesInList.Text: It's worth being clear about multiple-graders and what you're meaning: You can use Marking Workflow to describe the "state" of the grading for a submission, and Allocated Marker allows you to specify "who" is doing the grading. You cannot have 2 separate markers assign 2 separate grades and then reconcile them into a single final grade. There is one advanced grading method plugin ( https://moodle.org/plugins/gradingform_multigraders ) that implements a form of multiple-grading, but you'd need to be happy that it's reconcilation process (for getting the final grade) is acceptable to you. In this case, I believe the plugins makes the *first* grader the one who gets to decide, where most places (like my institution) expect the either *last* grader or a 3rd-party to deal with any disagreement.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignments, Groups & Teaching Assistants
ResponsesInList.Text: What you are describing Mary Beth is what I do regularly with the Moodles that I support. What I do, is for the standard role of 'Non-editing teacher' there is a permission called 'accessallgroups' which I change from allow to prevent. This means that someone with that role will only see students who are in the same group as them. This means they will only get submission notifications sent to them from their students and not other students. (and likewise will only see and get notifications from forums that are set to recognise groups). You then set the assignments to 'separate' groups, you don't need to force groups for this to work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Rubric, Grading Guide - Pass Fail option with Multiple Criterion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mary, if I am understanding your request correctly, then I think you want to be looking at Outcomes : https://docs.moodle.org/401/en/Outcomes Outcomes are a bit fiddly to get used to, and I would recommend testing and practising on a test site first, as once you have set them up, they are a pig to delete, so something you want to get right first time. You can set them up at site level or course level, I would suggest course level most likely - once added to the course, you then choose which outcomes are to be added to which assignment and what scale you are using to grade them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student sees "Expired" label on Assignment, cannot submit
ResponsesInList.Text: What seems to have happened here is that the assignment initially had a Due date and a Cut-off date. The student missed the cut-off date, and was granted an extension. However, the original cut-off date still applies to the extension and cannot be changed when granting the extension. So when granting an extension, it is possible to set a new due date that is after the cut-off date, which seems incorrect and misleading for lecturers. If the student attempts to submit before the extended due date, but after the cut-off date, then they can go into the assignment, but won't see the "Add submission" button. (As a side-effect in the "Adaptable" theme, the "Expired" label is displayed below the assignment link in the course page.) As this point I was called in and turned off the Cut-off date on the Assignment , thinking it would solve the problem, but this change didn't get applied to the cut-off date already set on the extension for the student, so they still couldn't submit. I can understand this, although it would be nice if any change to the cut-off date was automatically applied to any extensions too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student sees "Expired" label on Assignment, cannot submit
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a rather complicated (and confusing) set up around Assignment dates, extensions *and* user/group overrides. Overrides *can* change both due date and cut-off date...so seem like a second redundant (but better) implementation of the extension date. The Extension date which *doesn't* seems to be done on the basis that if the student fails to submit by their extension date, they can't be late (because the "original" cut-off date kicks in). The only thing I can think of is that this allows you to see if the student is "late" when compared to the "standing" dates for the assignment. Personally I'd like to see the extension grant feature deprecated in favour of overrides, which allow for *all* of there potential dates to be adjusted for a student, not just the due date...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: non enrolled students in turnitin
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you reusing email addresses? My organisation had issues with this, and was caused by the integration using email to uniquely identify the user ( LTI does this). When a user is allocated a recycled email account, the original user is added into the course Turnitin as a Non Enrolled Student. Worse, when the new student uploads a document, it is transferred to the original owner of the email address, preventing the submitter from seeing the report, feedback and grade. The only way we've been able to deal with this moving forward, is to allocate a new email address to the user.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: non enrolled students in turnitin
ResponsesInList.Text: Yup, we had this and stopped using the Assignment 2 plugin (TT). Now, we just use the plugin on Moodle Assignment module (PP). There are a few reasons for the non-enrolled students, one being not resetting the course page and the TII Assignment module before teaching begins for a new cohort. There is also an issue if the module and course dates are not kept current. You will find the that the non-enrolled status can impact those students if they are in 'current' cohorts on other course pages on the platform. It gets very, very messy. We were able to solve it (only occasionally) by doing an unlink then relink via the plugin admin, but generally it needs to be sorted via the admin account on the TII platform. Very time consuming.

ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, Laura, with your post and Eoin's I am understanding. Eoin offers the "Flexible sections format" solution, which seems to do what you desire. I do not see you mentioning which version of Moodle you are using, and Moodle 4 has changed a bit from Moodle 3, so I am unsure what ideas might make sense to you. I wonder if you are using Moodle's ability to "highlight" the current topic? This feature will help guide your students. Currently on Moodle 4.1 and we have document conversion "unoconv" enabled to allow for PDF markup during the grading process. For the most part it is working pretty well, however we have occasional submissions that cannot convert. The "adhoc" task logs give us a report of a failed conversion, but I can't figure out from the log which assignment has the failure. I can find the USER from the ID, but many users are in multiple classes with multiple assignments. Its needle-in-haystack hunting. Here is an example log error: Execute adhoc task: assignfeedback_editpdf\task\convert_submission Adhoc task id: 217334 Adhoc task custom data: {"submissionid":"246000","submissionattempt":"0"} ... started 09:11:12. Current memory use 35.9 MB. Debugging increased temporarily due to faildelay of 86400 Converting submission for user id 3244 ... used 43 dbqueries ... used 0.92600202560425 seconds Adhoc task failed: assignfeedback_editpdf\task\convert_submission,error/Could not find readonly pages for grade 227177 Backtrace:
* line 105 of /mod/assign/feedback/editpdf/classes/task/convert_submission.php: call to assignfeedback_editpdf\document_services::get_page_images_for_attempt() * line 359 of /lib/cronlib.php: call to assignfeedback_editpdf\task\convert_submission->execute() * line 198 of /lib/cronlib.php: call to cron_run_inner_adhoc_task() * line 76 of /lib/cronlib.php: call to cron_run_adhoc_tasks() * line 178 of /admin/cli/cron.php: call to cron_run() Is there any way to easily track down what exactly the student is submitting so I can address the issue? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Administration: Assignment Convert Submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: The "submissionid" in the error message will be the id of the relevant record in the database table mdl_ assign_submission. From that table, you can get the "userid" and "assignment" values. The userid will directly give you the user and "assignment" can be looked up in table mdl_assign, to give you the "course" value - the id of the course in question. If you need the specific activity, you would need to look this up in the mdl_course_modules table, which is a bit more fiddly - for more details, see: https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Course_module

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Role that allows a 'supervisor' to upload assignments on the behalf of *some* students
ResponsesInList.Text: The editothersubmission capability allows you to access the edit submission page if you're not the owner of the submission (not the student). The submission will still be "owned" by the student user, but you'll get some artefacts in the log that show the submission change associated with the user doing the editing (this of course is actually good as it shows the change was made not by the student). The limitation on which users can do this would be impacted by the context, so typically your role would be defining at the class level, so all students, but if you were to override the capability and enable it for a role *on an assignment activity* the it would be constrained (I'm pretty sure) to the students within that assignment (as limited by restrict access conditions etc). I'm sure you *can't* specify it along the lines of "Tutor A" can only amend "Students 1, 3, & 5" and "Tutor B" can only amend "Students 2,4 & 6", the context that the capability is checked in is the "assignment" (and then backwards up the chain ->course->site) and *not* the student.

ResponsesInList.Title: Removal of Assignment 2.2 from core code in Moodle LMS 4.2
ResponsesInList.Text: We would like to inform you that the Assignment 2.2 (mod_assignment) plugin was replaced in 2012 in Moodle LMS 2.3 by a new one called Assignment (mod_assign) . Since then, mod_assignment is disabled but kept to enable pre-2.2 backups to be restored. Because of that, the Moodle HQ team has now decided to remove Assignment 2.2 from core and make it available in the plugin repository. The only impact will be that from  Moodle LMS 1.9 downwards, the Assignment 2.2 backups will not be restored. This plugin will be removed once you upgrade to Moodle LMS 4.2. On the other hand, you can still use it, if needed, by installing it from the plugin repository .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to properly manual delete the remaining 'assignfeedback_editpdf' after uninstalling the AnnotatePDF plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi The scripts are too specific to our installation to share them, but I can tell you how I do it: First I get a list of the ids of all courses in the category, from which I want to purge all editpdf-files: moosh -n -p $moodlepath -c $catid | awk -F, '{ print $1 }' | tr -d \" >$tmpfile (You can use moosh -n category-list $category-name to find a categories id) Then I scan these courses for the editpdf-files: rm $editpdffiles 2>/dev/null i=0 while read -r cid; do i=$((i + 1)) [ $i -eq 1 ] && continue; moosh -n -p $moodlepath file-list course=$cid \ | grep -e "assignfeedback_editpdf" \ | grep -v -e ":stamps:" \ >>$editpdffiles done < $tmpfile This gives a list of all these files. Here a sample line: 1581580 0 .... f111716a9e35eea8aa735106e3cba13857eae832 Saturday, 10. April 2021, 10:13 77645:assignfeedback_editpdf:combined:40147 combined.pdf --- You can now purge all these files (or filter them before by date as I do) cat $editpdffiles | moosh -n -p $moodlepath file-delete -s Hope it helps a bit. But be careful and check all twice, so you not delete something wrong

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to properly manual delete the remaining 'assignfeedback_editpdf' after uninstalling the AnnotatePDF plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't have moosh installed, so my approach is different, although still using bash. It assumes that you have a separate DB Server to connect through ssh, but that can be changed easily. The select statement creates a deletelist shellscript which is then executed and removes the physical files. Afterwards the db entries in mdl_files are removed. mytime="1 YEAR" sql user"yourusername" sqlPW="yourpassword" #create deletelist script ssh user@yourserver " mysql -u$sqluser -p$sqlPW yourmoodle_db -e \"SELECT DISTINCT CONCAT('rm -f /path/to/moodledata/filedir/', LEFT(mdl_files.contenthash, 2),'/', MID (mdl_files.contenthash, 3, 2),'/', mdl_files.contenthash,';') AS shellscript FROM mdl_files WHERE component = 'assignfeedback_editpdf' AND timecreated < UNIX_TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(NOW(),INTERVAL $mytime));\"" > clear.sh; #modify and execute deletelist script sed -i '1d' clear.sh chmod +x clear.sh /path/to/clear.sh; #delete database entries ssh user@yourserver "mysql -u$sqluser -p$sqlPW yourmoodle_db -e \"DELETE FROM mdl_files WHERE component = 'assignfeedback_editpdf' AND timecreated < UNIX_TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(NOW(),INTERVAL $mytime));\"";

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment Add Submission Not Showing for Students
ResponsesInList.Text: The top one is not a normal Student view. it is the normal Teacher view because only Teachers can see the Grade and View all submissions button. In fact, the "Grade"/"View all submissions" button and the "Add assignment" should never show up for the same person. The first thing to verify is that the Student and Teacher role permissions are correct in Site admin > Users > Permissions > Capability overview. The following two capabilities should be set to 'Allow' for the Student and 'Not set' for Teacher (and all other standard roles): 1) Submit assignment mod/assign:submit 2) View own submission summary mod/assign:viewownsubmissionsummary The following two should be set to 'Allow' for Teacher (and Manager and Non-editing teacher) and 'Not set' for Student (and all other standard roles):: 3) View grades mod/assign:viewgrades 4) Grade assignment mod/assign:grade The following should be set to 'Allow' for Teacher (and Manager) but for Non-editing teacher and Student (and all other standard roles):: 5) Review grades mod/assign:reviewgrades If those are correct, then look for the issue where a user has more than one role in the course, or is inheriting a role from above, such as from a Category or the System level roles. Also verify that your Default role for all users is Authenticated user in Site admin > User > Permissions > User policies, just in case that may be causing problems.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Moodle Direct V2 -resetting turnitin activity
ResponsesInList.Text: When you add a Turnitin assignment to a Moodle course, Turnitin gets this information and creates a "course" and "assignment" within Turnitin's system linked to your Moodle course and assignment, then it finds all the students/users in your course and creates accounts/enrols them into the course on their end. This is definitely an issue on the Turnitin end - not Moodle's, but it's hard for them to fix on their end - you need to "break" the connection between your Moodle course, and the course Turnitin has created and mapped against your Moodle course. Turnitin (at least they used to last time I saw) charges you as an organisation per user per year and a lot of their internal processes expect that a "Turnitin" level course is only really used for 12 months and they mostly expect organisations to create a new course each year for the new cohort of students - they extended this on their end a little so it sounds like the upper limit is now 7 years. Historically getting a Moodle course to map to a "turnitin level" course has been quite problematic - us Moodlers use courses completely differently than the Turnitin engineers ever expected - roles/permissions/ enrolments etc... and so they've had to implement various workarounds to support this. It's been quite a while since I've used the mod_turnitintool plugin myself - but sometimes deleting the assignment activity itself in your course and creating a new one in the course may trigger the process to create a "new" course in Turnitin's system associated with the Moodle course - alternatively there are various options in the admin level settings of the plugin that I think allow you to manage this.... but really, Turnitin support should be helping you to understand how to fix this on the Moodle side.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Moodle Direct V2 -resetting turnitin activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Finally in terms of actually answering your questions, in our set up, we automatically run a class reset each year against most of the Moodle Courses in our server, but we've hit this issue with courses that haven't been reset and carried forward. This is basically the equivalent of creating a new TII class linked to the *same* Moodle Class ID each year. If you only have 1 Moodle class and do this, then the previous TII Class will now not be linked to your Moodle Class any more. Every year you get a new 0year old TII class: Case 1. Case 2 the TII class and the Moodle class don't change, but the individual TII assignments get changed. This may hit the term limit eventually as the TII class would now be in its "2nd year", then 3rd ...etc. At somepoint you'll need to "reset" the class, by creating a new Turnitin class. However the "age" of the Moodle Class Site is completely irrelevant, and as far as I can see Moodle does not impose this limitation, nor can I see any good reason as to why it should be a hard limit either.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Moodle Direct V2 -resetting turnitin activity
ResponsesInList.Text: My understanding of the TII reset code is that when it is set to "Create duplicates, New Turnitin Class", what happens is: the TII Class ID held in Moodle and linked to your class is wiped out (deletes from {turnitintooltwo_courses} table. Calls TII Service to create a new TII Class. Joins the instructor to the new TII class. This new TII Class Site's ID gets stashed locally in your moodle, linked to your Moodle Class ID For each of the TII 2 activities in your moodle class it generates a new TII activity using all of the Moodle settings (effectively) "duplicating" the previous version of that activity from the "old" TII Class. You can see what it's doing in the turnitintooltwo/lib.php file in the turnitintooltwo_duplicate_recycle function. This function is called by the moodle reset_userdata() framework when you do a course reset. Yes basically (although we use the plagiarism plugin, rather that TIITool2, but it's the same principle) we have a script that sets up the "right" moodle reset data (that you'd do via the UI) and then automatically runs if for every class that we want reset.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to deal with "Grade to pass" if I'm using a competence scale?
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I'm aware, you are only required to enter a "Grade to pass" if the activity completion settings have the "Require passing grade" option ticked. If you don't have that completion criteria, then you can just leave the "Grade to pass" as blank. If you really need to have the "Require passing grade" criteria, then you can can probably enter a number that relates to the scale - i.e. 1.0 = review prior knowledge; 2.0 = work on this; 3.0 = level up. So, if you require a student to receive a grade of "Level up!" to pass, then setting the "Grade to pass" to "3.0" should work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Blind Marking - Participant ID Changes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi folks, I deliver eLearning and Moodle support for Robert Gordon University and have come across a blind marking query I can't get my head around. The examiner has downloaded all the papers that students have submitted for offline marking, all of which are distinguished by their blind marking IDs. When he comes to bulk- upload them back into Moodle, however, he finds that some of the Participant IDs don't match. Very strange. In most cases, the participant IDs increase by 1 but there are some cases of students' participant IDs increasing by 30+ in this dropbox. I guess this is Moodle searching for the next available participant ID in the sequence? At first I thought this was perhaps because the students had reuploaded their papers and therefore gained a new participant ID but the logs reveal none of the students have uploaded papers a second time. Has anybody encountered this problem before? Any advice on how to prevent the participant IDs changing in future dropboxes?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blind Marking - Participant ID Changes
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes! If I recall correctly there is a potential for a race condition that leads to there being 2 Blind participant IDs for the same user. Both IDs should work to tie back to the same user but it's disconcerting and only 1 of the IDs is displayed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blind Marking - Participant ID Changes
ResponsesInList.Text: I *think* what can happen is that, when a blind ID is needed for the first time (e.g. generating the 1st user in the grading table for the assignment for the first time), allocated_unique_ids() gets run to generate *all* of the unique ids. However there's no locking that goes on to prevent a 2nd request also asking for a blind id or a user, and if that user is different to ^^ or ^^ hasn't been generated yet, then it will also generate a unique ID for all of the unallocated users, which could also be "all" of the users. So now when both requests finish allocate_unique_ids() has been called twice. But it's also a very small timing window, but I think it really comes from the fact that the initial unique ids are only generated when they are first needed (as far as I can tell on a "view" of assignment pages), rather than being generated as early as possible (so for instance when the activity is saved).

It lists Participant 14391 14 but, when the examiner clicks Grade and when he downloads the submissions, he gets 14391 10 . Uploading his feedback into Moodle as 14391 10 doesn't seem to be matching with the 14391 14 participant either. Participant_1439146 has become 1439174 Participant_1439110 has become 1439114 Participant_1439079 has become 1439080 Does this number increase sequentially for the next number in the queue or is it random? Since it's a blind marking dropbox, the examiner is worried he has given feedback to the wrong students if the participant IDs can change. The IDs wouldn't change once generated, would they?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blind Marking - Participant ID Changes
ResponsesInList.Text: The IDs aren't changing, but it seems that there end up being 2 ids pointing to the same user and there's an inconsistency as to which one is pulled out (probably because it didn't expect to ever end up with more than 1 record per user per assignment).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blind Marking - Participant ID Changes
ResponsesInList.Text: The participant number is sequential, in that it is just the primary key of the table, so it's guaranteed unique, but 2 processes adding records to the table at the same time could end up being interleaved.

ResponsesInList.Title: Unwanted file upload by students through atto

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignments submitted by member of "Default" group
ResponsesInList.Text: First, I am sorry but I cannot tell which version of Moodle I am using as the site administrator appears to have removed all links to that information. I hope it is not relevant to my question. My question is about the behavior of assignments submitted by a student in the Default group who is later placed in a named group. Do they continue to "belong" to the Default group, or to the "new" group the submitter is placed in, or to both? Before anyone aims a criticism my way for not setting "Require group to make submissions" to Yes, that is my normal procedure, but on one occasion I forgot to do so, and a student (say, A) who was never placed in a group ended up with a certain named group's (G01) submission attached to his name. I am trying to determine if this situation could have come about because a member of group G01submitted his report while still in the Default group, i.e., before being placed in the named group. Student A was the only student left in the Default group by the time I became aware of the situation. Thank you for any help you can provide on this question.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignments submitted by member of "Default" group
ResponsesInList.Text: You can answer this yourself. If the assignment is now also attached to G01 and still to default then that is how it works. I suspect however, that the assignment is probably only attached to the group that the submitter was joined to at the time of submission.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignments submitted by member of "Default" group
ResponsesInList.Text: I can't really answer this myself without moving a student currently in a named group into the Default group, and I'm a bit nervous about doing that, even temporarily, since I don't know whether the effects of doing that are 100% reversible. If you are correct, that the assignment is only attached to the group to which the submitter belonged at the time of submission, then the student in the Default group somehow obtained the report and submitted it dishonestly. That is what I am trying to determine. The report is definitely attached to G01, but the question is whether it is ALSO attached to the Default group. If it is, then the student in the Default group is likely innocent and I do not want to accuse him of cheating without knowing whether it is possible that the report was originally submitted before the submitter was moved into G01. But thank you for your reply. Initially I had difficulty posting this because when I tried to edit a minor typo, the system said my post had been blocked as possibly containing spam . So I wasn't certain whether it was visible to anyone else.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignments submitted by member of "Default" group
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I think I understand now. When I switched my own role temporarily to Student, I saw that I was in the Default group and the submission was shown as my own submission (i.e., that of my group). So this submission is definitely attached to the Default group. However, although it is identical to this submission, the file attached to G01 was submitted *separately*, a day later, according to the timestamps. Also, looking back at my email exchange with G01's student representative, it appears that the student informed me of his group membership at 3:53 pm, and then per the timestamp, the Default group submission was made 2 minutes later, at 3:55. I did not move his G01 group into the grouping for that assignment until 7:30pm on the same day. So my guess is that the same student submitted the report immediately without waiting for my reply (which except for my error he could not have done), and that you are correct, that the original submission remained attached to the Default group. The student likely found the next day that his file was no longer in the submission box, and submitted it again. Thus, the one remaining student still in the Default group is almost certainly innocent of any academic dishonesty in this matter. In a previous thread, someone opined that the "Require group to make submissions" setting is a design flaw. I agree. At the very least, its default setting should NOT be "no", once one has set "Students submit in groups" to "yes", unless that setting has very different semantics than it does now. I cannot imagine a situation where it would be desirable for a submission by a student who is not a member of a named group to be attached to ALL students who are not members of a named group. And my experience here shows, I think, how easy it is with the current semantics to accidentally bring about a situation where the actual history of submissions is very difficult to trace, and might even make it appear that an innocent student has cheated. I could not have figured this out without the emails between myself and the G01 student, since there is ( AFAIK ) no timestamp telling when a group was moved into a grouping.

ResponsesInList.Title: Auto assign a grade for simply submitting a file
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all We have a number of courses that require file submissions which will not be looked at or assessed by a person. However, there is a mark allocated for simply submitting the file (usually a very low percentage of the course final grade). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Auto assign a grade for simply submitting a file
ResponsesInList.Text: The Checklist module could work here! Set your assignment to not be worth any points (by setting the grade type to None), and set the Activity Completion for it to "Student must submit to this activity to complete it" -- then you can allow the Checklist activity to do the rest of the work for you. Add a Checklist activity into the same section of the course as the assignment. Set "Show course modules in checklist" to "Current section" and assign the activity grade to be whatever the assignment was set to. Once you save it, that checklist activity will include "all" activities that within that current section, so you then click "Edit Checklist" and omit items you don't need included. Course page: Then, once the students submits something to the Assignment, the Checklist Activity auto "completes" and assigns the grade into the gradebook

ResponsesInList.Title: What to whitelist for email notifications

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What to whitelist for email notifications
ResponsesInList.Text: A little deeper iceburg is involved me thinks. Do you have your Moodle set up to relay mail via SMTP service? If not, then your moodle is using the built-in phpmailer which can't pass muster on systems bent on protecting 'customers' - and there are more of those than just gmail.com. A good SMTP relay setup will pass muster with Google checks ... those checks are SPF, DKIM, valid no-reply address, etc. - multiple. Ask those students to check their spam .   Also, if they had previously gotten something from your Moodle, ask them to look at the 'Show Original' of that message.   That will show the full header of the email message which shows the mail servers that message ran through to get to their inbox. The 'Receivied' lines in that header are the important ones. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What to whitelist for email notifications

ResponsesInList.Text: We can set the default file type restriction as a moodle Admin, but a Teacher can delete that value when creating an Assignment, enabling Student submission of any file type.
