ResponsesInList.Title: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, in 2014 there was a discussion here in the forum on the same topic: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=257428 Unfortunately the discussion has been closed, so I have to open a new thread. The scenario described in the discussion cited above is this: - Have your students hand in group solutions for an assignment no. 1. - For assignment no. 2 students change the group and hand in a solution with their new group The problem here is: If a student is in Group A and receives a grade for Assignment 1 and
then moves to Group B, the student will suddenly have Group B's grade for
Assignment 1 if Assignment 1 is re-graded. The proposed solutions were to either a) use a new grouping for each assignment or b) not to -re-grade Assignment 1 anymore once Assignment 2 allows the handing in of solutions. Imo neither of this is a real solution. Solution a) makes the organisation of assignments especially in large groups (>500 students) very uncomfortable and unnecessarily complicated. The problem here is that it is not enough to create new groupings for each assignment, you also have to create new groups. This puts a lot of workload on the teachers which seems all the more unnecessary as in our scenario not all students  change the group but only those whose partners left the course or want to join a different group because they don't get along well with each other. And this happens quite frequently at the beginning of a course. What makes it more complicated is the fact that in our scenario students can choose their group. So creating new groups and having the students choose a new group each and every time extends the process a lot, especially as some students tend to forget things and will not choose a new group which means a lot of additional support for the teachers. Solution b) also is not really a solution as it is not safe and it is very hard to tell all the teachers using assignments at a university not to re-grade assignments if groups have changed. What is more, with assignments in large courses and on a weekly basis it is not possible to (finally!) grade the whole assignment before the next one starts, even with a dozen of tutors. So my question here is: Is there any other, clean and preferably technical solution to this? Kind regards Harald

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a general problem with the assignment module which either wasn't considered when the module was designed or it was deferred as there do exist workarounds. But as Harald says we can't use these workarounds. In my opinion this is a bug and should be fixed in the core. Would anything speak against that? The problem is this: For each group submission the groupid is stored. If the submissions are graded, then a student switches from one group to another and then his grade is changed again, Moodle checks which group he's currently in, who else is currently in his group and updates the grade for all of them. Instead we'd need to have separate DB tables like "assign_submission_groups" and "assign_submission_groups_members" where we would store group info and group membership at the time of submission. It could look like this: assign_submission_groups id assignment idnumber name description descriptionformat picture hidepicture 1 1 g1 Group 1 1 0 0 2 1 g2 Group 2 1 0 0 3 1 g3 Group 3 1 0 0 4 2 g1 Group 1 1 0 0 5 2 g2 Group 2 1 0 0 assign_submission_groups_members id assignsubmissiongroupid userid 1 1 2 2 1 3 3 1 6 4 1 11 5 2 4 6 2 7 7 2 8 8 2 10 9 3 1 10 3 5 11 3 9 12 4 2 13 4 3 14 4 9 15 4 10 16 5 5 17 5 7 18 5 8 19 5 11 In this example you groups of (up to) four. For the first assignment you have 11 students (IDs 1 through 11) in 3 groups. After that assignment the group compositions change: Students 1, 4 and 6 drop out. The remaining two students of group 3 move to groups 1 and 2. Student 10 doesn't like it in group 1 so he asks group 2 if one of them wants to switch places with him. Student 11 agrees and they switch places. Later they hand in their submissions for the second assignment. The DB table "assign_submission" would then no longer have a column "groupid" which refers to the "groups" table but an "assignsubmissiongroupid" column that refers to the new "assign_submission_groups" table. I haven't looked at the PHP code yet, so can't say how much would need to be changed there to make it work. Would something like this be an okay solution? Am I missing something? Edit: The group info (name etc.) stored in the new table wouldn't be updated if you change the group info after the assignment. This might cause confusion, possibly. But a) I'm not sure most people would even want the group names in old submissions "updated" and b) even so it's still better than unintentionally changing student's grades (and not noticing it!).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Isn't that what groupings are for?  The grouping should just be changed for the second assignment. The problem with your suggestion is what if you want the student to get the grade for the second group?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Emma, I've already explained in the post before Tim's that groupings might be used but you would have to create completely new groups for each assignment. Let's assume a teacher is willing to go this extra step. In our case usually the students choose themselves who they want to work with. So they choose the group. As Moodle core doesn't offer this you have to use a plugin like groupchoice. So in addition to the teacher having to create new groups and do the grouping again (I'm talking about courses with several hundreds of people and a large number of groups accordingly) he has to create a new activity groupchoice. Then the students have to choose a new group although most of them will keep the group members they already worked with. This is osmething our students have already been complaining about in the past so we changed that with our current system which is not Moodle. So, the teacher has to make sure that the group choice activity expires before the next assignment starts. That's already complicated as usually with weekly assignments the deadline of the first assignment ends with the publication of the next assignment. So you have to find space for doing the groupchoice and have to make sure that really all the students have chosen their group before the assigment starts. And I'm still talking about several hundred students here. You have to make sure that the groupchoice has been done before the assignment starts as it is not possible to be in no group or more than one group with group solutions. In both cases a student doensn't hand in a solution for a special group but for a mysterious standard group the teacher has never seen before. In this standard group there are all the students that have more than one group or no group. If a student creates a solution for this standard group he hands in a soluton for other people without even knowing it. If students have not chosen a new group in time (and you know how students are) the teacher has to put in extra time and manual work to put them into groups. This is the result of my tests. Maybe I oversaw an easier solution but doing all this work will be very complicated for teachers that have far less time to spend on learning to understand Moodle than I do. That's the problem I see here. About the second thing that you mention: If student X works in group A for assignment 1 he should get the grade for that solution. If he changes to group B for assignment 2, why should he get the grade of that group for assignment 1? He didn't work with that group and their solution at the time of deadline. What if group B gets a weaker grade than group A for assignment 1? Then the student would complain, and rightfully in my view. What would be your scenario where it would make sense? That's what I tried to find out but couldn't so far. Best regards and thanks for your answers! Harald

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: That makes sense. But, I think the problem is that whatever solution is found has to take care of all scenarios.  What if assignments overlap and students start jumping back and forth between groups.  How is Moodle meant to know where that student's grade comes from for each assignment?  Hence groupings...not the easiest way, I know, but I cannot think of a better way to be sure that student gets the correct grade without locking down the flexibility that is available now.  You cannot use the assignment due date because some courses do not have due dates.  You could say they get the grade for whatever group they were a member of on the day of submission but what if they have already switched?  Or what if the group is allowed to resubmit later and the member has moved groups?  So many scenarios where your proposal does not work... I am not disagreeing with you that teachers need an easier way, I just have not figured out how to make it work...I wish you luck in finding something that will!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Emma I just tested again to verify what I said. Indeed you don't have to re-do all the groups in your course but all groups where members change. (In case you let the students choose their groups through a plugin like groupchoice this still means you have to do all the groups again, I guess.) So, if S1 ist part of Group A for an assignment and wants to join Group B for the next assignment, then the teacher has to create a new Group C with S1 and the members of Group B. And he has to create a new group D for the remaining members of Group A. Because for the new grouping you cannot re-use the old group A (and neither you can re-use Group B). Another Group E that remains stable from the first to the next assignment can remain as is but has to become part of the new grouping of course. The groupings in this scenario are Grouping 1 (Groups A, B, E) for Assignment 1 and Grouping 2 (C, D, E) for Assignment 2. So, basically it works with groupings but still to me it seems rather complicated and difficult to explain to users. Best regards Harald

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group submissions when changing groups
ResponsesInList.Text: I use groups a lot (actually for a way different purpose but that besides the point).  I tell my teachers that Moodle gives you the option to create groups for assignments - because students are not necessarily in the same group for each assignment, they should create groups with a naming convention something like this:  Assign1-GroupA, Assign1-GroupB, Assign2-GroupA, Assign2-GroupB and then place them in Groupings named Assign1, Assign2.  Does it make it easier no, but it helps them to understand how it works...that the grouping is specific to the assignment and the group naming makes it easier to understand and quickly find when they are looking at a long list of groups...it also helps it make sense for the students who do not know about groupings but will hopefully now understand why they are in different groups...

ResponsesInList.Title: Weights in marking guide
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello I am defining a marking guide in which my each criterion has some weight. I want to grade all criterion out of 10 but finally some criterion will weigh double than the other to make the total grade in that particular assignment. How to do this? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weights in marking guide
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't think you can other than just making them out of different amounts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weights in marking guide
ResponsesInList.Text: You cannot do you want with all criteria set to 10. If you want a criteria to be weighted double that of the others, then give it twice as much Maximum score. For example, let's say I have three criteria and I want #3 to be weighted double that of #1 and #2. I can set the Maximum score for #1 and #2 to be 10. Then I set the Maximum score for #3 to be 20. For the assignment I set the Grade to Type > Point and the Maximum grade to 100. When you grade a student the three criteria scores will be scaled as a percentage of the 100 point maximum for the activity. Use the same priciple for any number of criteria and keep the assignment grade set to 100. So, it is like Emma says, make them out to different amounts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Re-submitting assignment without deleting the old submission
ResponsesInList.Text: The feature is there. Assignment setup > Submission Settings > Attempts reopened to manually, then Maximum attempts to some value. I usually set 3 as that's our resit policy. Now when you grade the assessment, there is an option at the bottom of the grading screen to allow another attempt. Choose Yes and save. To view different attempts as a grader, there is now a new "View a different attempt" link at the bottom of the grading screen. It'll also show you the attempt number. All of the attachments, feedback, etc for each attempt are isolated from each other which is great for keeping evidence of improvement. The learner sees the feedback on their assessment screen, which does, unfortunately make for a very long scroll (this is fixable if you know how to theme moodle). When the learner goes to submit extra attempts, they can choose to use the old submission as a template, copying the existing attachments, text, etc or submit from scratch. The previous attempts remain untouched. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, just ran into the exact same problem here with .jpg and .png files not displaying using unoconv.  PDF and .DOC(X) work fine.  Also using Moodle 3.3. Looking for an answer...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unoconv not converting image files (jpg, png, etc) or text files for the Moodle 3.3 PDF feedback tool
ResponsesInList.Text: I found myself in a similar situation with .jpg files but .png files haven't been a issue for me.  Look at the code in $CFG-> dirroot /files/converter/unoconv/classes/converter.php, there's a function called supports that is called that passes file types to is_format_supported to make sure unoconv can handle the conversion. What I noticed was that in the case of jpg, it was picking it up as jpe.  What ends up happening is a little bit down the line, unoconv --show is called and the list of supported filetypes it outputs is then used to see if the conversion is possible.  This list doesn't include .jpe so it ends up believing the conversion isn't possible and leaves it alone. The quickest and dirtiest way to fix that is to insert a if statement above "return self::is_format_supported($from) && self::is_format_supported($to);" in public static function supports where if $from equals jpe then make $from equal jpg.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic Grading of Assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Bit of a work-around using a module for something it's not meant for, but this a way you could achieve it: Try using Quiz instead as this allows for automatic marking. Use whatever Scale you want to use. Deselect everything under Review options. Change total marks to "1" Add an Essay question, which will be unmarked. Set Mark to "0" Set Response format to "No online text" Set both Allow attachments and Require attachments to "1" (or however many files they need to upload). Add a multiple choice question, which can be any question you want to add (for example a "I haven't plagiarised" statement). This question is marked, which will add the points to your Gradebook. Set Mark to "1" Set One or multiple answers to "Multiple answers allowed Deselect "Shuffle choices" Add two answers and set the Grade to "50%" for each (one answer doesn't work for a multiple choice question). The multiple choice question will be automatically marked. Quick example:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: assignment: download feedback and annotated PDFs for all students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kris, I have also replied to your within our UCL Moodle Users forum, but am posting my reply on here too for the benefit of others outside UCL. You can download the annotated PDF file, however, on our current UCL Moodle theme, this column is obstructed by the blocks on the right. In the new theme coming over summer you will be able to hide the blocks with one click and make the page full-screen, so this won't be an issue any more. Hopefully other Moodle installations won't have the same issue with the blocks covering the columns, like we do. For those who can't see all the Assignment columns because the blocks are covering them, if you zoom out (Ctrl--) you can see the 'Annotate PDF' column. If you click on the first link for each student the online marked PDF file with its annotations will open. There doesn't seem to be a way to download these in bulk from Moodle, but you can use a browser plugin to do this pretty easily. Chrono Download Manager looks like a popular option for Chrome Browser. You can filter by document (on the second tab) and then filter again by PDF file. I think it will also download any PDFs that students have submitted (i.e. the non-annotated files), but hopefully these are easy to sort by filename, once downloaded. I hope others find this useful too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Change identifier for offline grading worksheets
ResponsesInList.Text: (using Moodle 3.4.2) Is there a way to change the Identifier for offline grading worksheets? The Moodle User ID that currently acts as identifier / first column in the grading worksheets is useless to our teachers, and we would very much like to exchange that for the Moodle logon name.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change identifier for offline grading worksheets
ResponsesInList.Text: No there isn't. You potentially run into issues with Blind Marking, where presenting that sort of identifiable information breaks the blindness, and since Moodle need to support all of the different modes, an institution-agnostic identifier is better. However if you go in to the Site Policies configuration you can select fields from the User profile to be used as "Identity fields" ( Show user identity configuration option), which are then included in various places where a user's identity is needed (username isn't an option however, and this is probably good as it's 1/2 the information you need to start hacking credentials) ID Number is a good one to select if it is filled with student's Registration / Matriculation number from your Student Record. These fields then also appear (in addition to the Moodle identifier) in the Offline grading worksheet. Just don't mix up the values (e.g. when sorting the sheet) as it will still use the Moodle identifier as the key for re-uploading the data. (Note this is *sitewide* and may leak information that you don't want everyone to have...) M

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change identifier for offline grading worksheets

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All, I wanted to get some input around how existing educators are using different assignments to develop soft skills. What kind of assignments do you use? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Soft Skill Development
ResponsesInList.Text: I used to teach two Computer Applications courses, one introductory beginner course and one advanced. Each course covered a variety of software applications for presentations, word processing, databases, spreadsheets, desktop publishing, vector graphics drawing, audio recording, video recording, and a few others. Usually assignments were projects and students would turn in most of their projects via Moodle Assignment. Audio and video projects were submitted via the Pcast plugin. The beginners course students would finish the year by creating a portfolio of all their work using eXe. Each assignment had step-by-step directions using Book resources, and students worked at their own pace with a deadline. Students who beat the deadline got to do "fun" stuff bonus work. Advanced students, using what they learned the year before, would create a monthly school newspaper, and a portfolio of their work for the year, again using eXe. They also worked on adding to a narration script about school events each week. At the end of the year, using their script and videos made throughout the year, they each made a video broadcast of the school highlights for the year. As a final step, they added close captions to the video. The softskills you mention were very important to the advanced students in being able to produce the newspaper, their scripts, and their videos.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Online Text Second Submission Error message
ResponsesInList.Text: I understand that there are two possible behaviours for the Save button in Moodle assignments. A course designer can require that students push a special 'Submit' button before their work goes to be marked.  If that option is not set, then the Save button acts as a Submit button - the work is sent for marking.     This option can be set one way or the other for any assignment.  So what applies for one assignment may not apply for another. Your advice to use the Save button is helpful only for where a Submit button is also supplied.  You are probably witnessing cases where the students have actually been submitting when they hit "Save".  Moodle settings can also control how many times a student can submit. Depending on your site, you may not need to advocate the Save button.  I believe that the editor program you use when you type online text in Moodle can be quite smart, and more or less save things for you as you go.  As I've been writing this in a similar box, a message came up which said "Draft saved."  I'm writing in a discussion forum, not in Moodle itself, but the tool I think is the same (or can be).  Many of these things are 'plug-in's - administrators can decide what will manage it. Talk to them, because this isn't a matter I'm confident about. If such a thing is implemented at your site, it may not be necessary to advise students to Save. It will be safe to do so if there is also a Submit button. I'd avoid doing so if Save is the only button they can see. Maybe you can talk to some local teachers/admins to see what policy if any operates at your school. It would probably be best if it were consistent. If you have input to course design, another idea might be to use more than one assignment - so submissions address smaller pieces of work, and the  stakes are not so high.  Again, the Quiz module allows you to set 'essay questions' where each question is like an online assignment of the type you describe.  The Quiz module automatically saves progress as you complete one question and move to the next.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PDF Corrupted & Not Found After Migration
ResponsesInList.Text: First screen shot looks like a browser doesn't know what to do with a .pdf file it's supposed to be downloading - not displaying.  One can see in the header of that file a "PDF 1.4" designation. What browser?  And have you checked browser settings for what to do with a PDF file?  Unless you have Adobe, typically Mac browsers will default to opening PDF's in Preview. The second, might be related to unoconv ... a feature introduced in 3.1.   In setting of the Moodle, do you have /usr/bin/unoconv in the path box for unoconv?   Try removing that path and save. Then go back to an assignment submission and attempt grading again. You might have to turn on debugging for a bit to see if Moodle will give any more information on the second. ﻿ Was the moodledata directory transferred in a binary mode or an ascii mode? You say all the  PDF's are corrupted?  Or just the ones you've checked out? Might have to query the DB using the "humanly recognizable" name of a file to find it's contenthash value and then manually copy out of moodledata/filedir/ a file that you think is corrupted. The example provide shows it was a PDF in an assignment submission and the humanly recognizable name was "Hasher Alam Task.pdf" select contenthash from `mdl_files` where (`component` like "%assignsubmission%" and `filename` like "%Hasher Alam Task.pdf%") Should show the contenthash ... i.e. location of the file. something like: 25b7f1f30b49ae98e313e12885e4e8f5b8859549 then navigate /moodledata/filedir/25/b7/ to see if there is a file by the contenthash name. Copy that file in filedir out to your web root ... on CentOS web root is /var/www/html/ typically. From moodledata in a shell for example: cp ./filedir/25/b7/25b7f1f30b49ae98e313e12885e4e8f5b8859549 /var/www/html/test.pdf Then use browser going directly to: http://site/test.pdf How does your browser behave?   Should prompt to download or launch with either Adobe or Preview, I would think. Don't forget to remove the test.pdf file after testing. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to find the assignment that needs grading (Moodle 3.4)
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two potentially confusing things, I think: You need to press the uncoloured button, "View all submissions" (even though you want to view only a selection).  (But I think you've done this.) There are drop boxes both above and below the student listing that comes up.  You need to go below the listing to find the Options section.  It's got an arrow next to it, which shows it's a collapsible section.  If the arrow's pointing down, you'll see some options, which include Filter. Set Filter to Requires Grading . You can still use the big blue Grade button against each individual student, but if doing so I use the breadcrumb menu to take me back to the next filtered student.  The filtering doesn't seem to apply to the next/previous navigation on the full (single-student-view) grading page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Call for an experienced Moodler: Push to Lock submissions after Grading: Avoid loss of evidence  (Moodle 3.4 and earlier)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Can someone do some advocacy for me?  Post this or something similar on the Tracker.  [Footnote 1] Project: Moodle (MDL) Issue Type: Improvement Applies to : 3.4 (and as far back as you care to go) Summary: Assignment: High teacher vigilance required to
avoid loss of evidence when students edit submissions after grading rather than start a new
attempt. EXPECTED: When a teacher awards a grade for work, the state
of the work at that time will be preserved.  With “Attempts reopened
automatically until pass “ implemented, a non-pass grade will permit the
student to resubmit in a new attempt-space for a new grade, but the history of
effort-grade pairings will not be affected. WHAT HAPPENS: Teachers are often unaware that they must manually lock students'
work from further edit, or implement workaround restrictions such as a cut-off
date (which has side-effects for local practice).  Without this control,
students encouraged to resubmit will instead edit work already awarded a
non-pass grade.  This issue was previously raised as MDL-37817 ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-37817), but
received a 'Will not fix' in anticipation of the new assignment resubmission
system.  The issue persists, despite implementation of the assignment
resubmission system  in Moodle 2.5 ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-36804). The problem was excellently described by Gabriel Fernandez Borsot in discussion
forum https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=279147 . While this is not technically a bug, the Moodle behaviour is not in
accordance with normal teaching practice nor with the expectations of a
practitioner with data management experience. STEPS TO REPRODUCE: 1. Set up an assignment with following settings: Availability Due Date [tick: Enable] Cut-off Date[Enable not ticked] Submission types File only (to maximally illustrate problem) [Note 2] Maximum number of uploaded files: 1 (to maximally illustrate problem) Submission settings Require students click submit button: No Maximum attempts: Unlimited Grade Type: Scale [Note 1] Scale: Further Evidence Required/Meets Requirements[Note 1] Grading method: Simple direct grading Grade category: Uncategorised Grade to pass: 2 [Note 1] (Others: No) Activity Completion Completion tracking: Show activity as complete when conditions are met Require grade: Student must receive a grade to complete this activity (ticked) 2. Have a student submit an assignment.  One file will be submitted
on hitting Save. 3. Mark it with less than the pass grade (in the example, Further Evidence
Required [Note 1]).  In feedback, advise student to resubmit. 4. (As a busy/naive teacher), do nothing with respect
to locking of submissions. 5. Have student resubmit.  The student will be
presented with chance to edit the existing submission (not to
resubmit).  The student will need to delete the one file already submitted
in order to replace it with another file.  The student will have
been inadvertently led by the teacher to removal of the evidence
upon which the initial grade and feedback was provided. [Note 1] A point based scale would probably do to reproduce the problem.  The
scale used here communicates the expectation of resubmission normalcy that may
often apply. [Note 2]  It is not necessary to limit the submission artefacts as
outlined above.  Indeed, by welcoming multiple submission types, a greater
mess can be created, where old and new activities are mixed together and
not matchable to the existing feedback artefacts. [Note 3] Implementing Cut-off date is an
unsatisfactory workaround.  Early submitters are entitled to early
feedback and early resubmission if student and teacher have the time and
energy.  Teachers in this scenario would still have to manually
'lock' the submission. I believe much of the 'lock submission' rationale stems from
workaround thinking that predated the assignment resubmission initiative in Moodle 2.5.  In any case, the principle that evidence should be matched
with feedback ought not to be a matter that is left to chance, as
currently.  Teachers will expect that the state of student work at
the time of grading is preserved, without additional administrative action. ...................... [Footnote 1]  I was disappointed to find after a *long* composition that my post to the Tracker was disallowed because I hadn't established enough reputation.  I needed to show I'd supported some similar issues: "Dear
Moodler, before creating a new issue you need to demonstrate that you have
searched among the existing issues to see if it's already been filed. Please
find a similar issue from among the open issues and either start watching it or
vote for it."  I did this but it hasn't recognised me yet.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Call for an experienced Moodler: Push to Lock submissions after Grading: Avoid loss of evidence  (Moodle 3.4 and earlier)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, Could you carefully re-check exactly what happens, as I believe there is an issue, but it is not exactly as you have described. With 'Attempts reopened automatically until pass', if the student receives less than a pass mark then they start on a new resubmission. They no longer have the opportunity to edit the existing submission and it is kept in  the history (exactly as you are wanting). However, there is definitely a problem when they receive more than the pass mark - at that point no resubmission is created and, unless the submission has been locked, they are free to edit the submission. Maybe there should be an extra option alongside 'Attempts reopened automatically until pass' called 'Attempts reopened automatically until pass, then locked' - which would lock the submission as soon as a pass mark is reached?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When student quits the course, does his assignement material  remain ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Please clarify: "when drops the uni..., he is automatically quits the moodle" ... That sounds like students are authenticating via the student information system or LDAP and the students no longer attending the univ  have had their accounts on the SIS or LDAP disabled. The student account might still exist in the Moodle, but cannot login because their credentials in LDAP have been changed/hidden/blocked from being used to authenticate. If there is some automated setup where the students no longer have access to the authentication server then they are also 'removed' from Moodle, then the removal of the student could erase all of their work. Student work is not kept in one table/folder in the sea of files in moodledata/filedir/ ... depends upon class and mods/ activities .   Assignments have a set of tables for all courses ... not each course ... as do forums, as do other things like blogs, etc. So what to do to archive?    At the close of the academic session, before the student is removed from Moodle, make a full backup of the course - that includes students and their work/grades/ teacher comments, etc... Download or put that full backup somewhere on LAN/WAN or download for restoring. OR, hide that course .... make a no user backup of the course, restore the no user backup for use the next academic session. OR, once you have a full backup downloaded, reset the course removing all students work and account.   That leaves the teacher and all resources/activities, etc. in the course and the course visible and ready for new students. If the student accounts have been alterted, not even admin level users can see the students any more. They are, however, in an obscured. form in the mdl_user table. Am sure Emma may have yet another idea ... ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi everyone, I've been searching for a solution to the following problem: in one of our Moodle courses, an assignment has been set up to be graded with a rubric. One of my colleagues has modified the rubric slightly after grading of the submissions had started and now we can't proceed anymore, as there is an error message that I can't seem to solve: 
```text
The rubric definition was changed after this student had been graded. The student can not see this rubric until you check the rubric and update the grade.
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joost, If I remember correctly, you will have to regrade the students that were already graded. When the teacher modified the rubric, there should have been a warning about needing to do so.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joost, Once the rubric is changed, the order of grading doesn't matter, just as long as the previously graded students are regraded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...
ResponsesInList.Text: So, just to get this clear: all 70+ students have to be regraded in order for the rubric to be unlocked again?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.3 Rubric definition was changed...
ResponsesInList.Text: Right. The previously graded students will not see the new rubric until they have been regraded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Downloading file assignment submissions (what is the number after the name)

In /assign/locallib.php is the following line: $this->get_uniqueid_for_user($userid)) Why a random number is generated I'm not sure as it provides no meaningful information to an instructor who downloads multiple files that have been uploaded. I think it has something to do with anonymous grading...? At any rate, I've modified it to give me the Moodle userid but am going to change it to give me the idnumber as that is the student id for students on our campus and will be most useful. Regards Jason

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Downloading file assignment submissions (what is the number after the name)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jason, If I recall correctly I think the number relates to the identifier that is generated for a user in an activity under blind marking. The Moodle ID number isn't used as it would identify the user, so for every activity each user gets a new participant ID. It means that you can re- upload the files and Moodle can tie the file back up to the destination user without leaking user information. Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing feedback for earlier attempt - URL incorrect for button (Moodle 3.1)

I have changed this to call each value in the array rather than use 'http_build_query' to build part of the URL, this keeps the same information but does not include the unwanted ascii codes and works as intended.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "reopened" confusion
ResponsesInList.Text: Reopening assignments allows a student to make a new attempt at an assignment after it has been graded (either at the teacher's discretion or until they have reached a passing grade). If 'manual' was selected, then the teacher would have had to have specifically selected 'yes' to reopen the assignment after each student was graded (the setting does not automatically switch everyone to a resubmission). Once a student has been granted a resubmission, there isn't, as far as I am aware, an option to 'take back' that resubmission (I thought there was such a feature when it was originally written, but I can't spot it now). If each student logs in and clicks 'Add a new attempt based on previous submission', then clicks 'Save changes', then the submission should be back to the original state and the 'bulk download' feature should work again.

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignment showing incorrect group members
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have created different assignments which should only be visible to students who belong to a certain group created by myself. The wording next to the participants seems correct, but next to the assignment on the course page it says 0 of 99 participants (total users enrolled on the course) for all my assignments which is not correct (it should say “0 of 4 participants” or “0 of 3 participants” depending on the individual group. Is this an expected behaviour? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment showing incorrect group members
ResponsesInList.Text: This is expected behaviour. The restrict access conditions are considered temporary and not part of the calculation of the "participants" for an assignment. E.g. if an assignment is not available until someone has completed the previous section - the participants list should NOT show 0 people and then slowly start showing more and more people as students complete the previous section - it will always show the full list of students that will eventually have access. I realise that groups is more of a "permanent" restriction - but it's considered the same way. In addition it's expensive to compute all the access restrictions for all the students in a course at the same time.

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignment Penalties
ResponsesInList.Text: So this was a thing back in March 2015(!) and had some conversation at the 2017 UK Moodle Moot too. Basically we've been looking at allowing a penalty to be semi-automatically be applied to student submissions in mod_assign. The idea being that instead of having to have 3 assignment submissions for each piece of work (1st attempt & 2 re-attempts), that you would then have to do some fancy foot work in the gradebook to sort out, you would just use the Assignment Attempt's function to allow 3 attempts. When you configure the activity with attempts you get a new control that says what penalty you'd like applied to each attempt. So attempt 1 would be 0 (but you could start it differently if you wanted, attempt 2 10%, attempt 3: 100% MDL-50395-AttemptPenalty.png" alt="" width="1200" height="372" class="img-responsive atto_image_button_text-bottom" />Once set up the marking screen gets a small tweak to display the penalty that would be applied. And more importantly allows the marker to decide if they want a different penalty to be applied (see semi- automated). MDL-50395-GradingWithPenalty.png" alt="grading penalty" width="650" height="552" class="img-responsive atto_image_button_text-bottom" /> Once the grader hits the save option for the grading selected penalty & the "real" Grade out of 100 is saved to the assignment as the students "raw" grade. However what is "persisted" as the final grade is the raw grade * penalty. This means that you can find out how much the student actually attained, versus what they were "awarded" (subtle but important difference) Anyway I've put a (hopefully) working build of this on github (against Moodle 3.5) https://github.com/mhughes2k/moodle/tree/MDL-50395-Attempt-Penalties And the tracker issue is here https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-50395 I'm hoping this could re-boot some discussion and some community interest...I know it's been a perennial issue for us, so presumably similar issues exist at other places! Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Traffic light grade scale or rubric?

ResponsesInList.Title: unoconv replacement for versions prior to 3.3
ResponsesInList.Text: We run Moodle version 3.1.x and have no plans to upgrade before Summer 2018. To get around all the unoconv conversion issues we wrote our own google converter script. The script is a drop in replacement for unoconv. I have attached the script in case it is useful for someone else. Requirements: python (should be installed already if you are using unconv) Google Service Key (json) for a project that has google drive api enabled ( https://console.developers.google.com/flows/enableapi?apiid=drive ) Installation: Put the script files into a folder (e.g. /usr/local/bin/converter) pip install --upgrade google-api-python-client Put the service key from google in this folder, rename the file to privatekey.json Set appropriate permissions on convert and converter.py (same as unoconv, your apache user will need to be able to execute this) Change your unoconv path in moodle to the convert script (/usr/local/bin/converter/convert in this example) Hope this helps someone. Regards,

ResponsesInList.Title: Group assignments with adjustments to individuals' marks
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi all, This is my first post - sorry if it's a duplicate, or if I end up missing any information that's usually expected. I'm teaching a course that includes group assignments, but where I want to be able to adjust the marks that individuals within a group get to account for varying levels of contribution. Our planned marking scheme is: For group assignments, we’ll first mark the
entire group’s submission out of 50 using a rubric with point ranges. So, for example,
group 1 might end up with a mark of 30/50. We then assign each individual within the group an individual adjustment mark in
recognition of how much they contributed relative to the rest of the group.
This has an intended range of -12 to +12. So, say, if Sue (a member of group 1)
contributed little to the project relative to her group-mates, she might get an
individual adjustment mark of -6, and end up with a final mark of 30-6 -=
24/50*. The problem: How can I implement this kind of marking
structure in moodle? I’ve tried a bunch of stuff in a sandbox site I have, but having
a marking criterion/category that can accept negative marks without unwanted
side effects is really tricky. I can add an "individual adjustment" criterion to a marking guide or rubric, and that accepts either positive or negative marks... but entering a maximum mark of 12 for this then has the unintended side effect of increasing the total that the assignment is marked out of from 50 to 62. Adding an individual adjustment mark as a separate grading item doesn't work either, because grading items can't accept negative marks. The only real solution I’ve found so far is to use
the marking guide to mark the group submissions, then have the markers decide
the individual adjustment marks, calculate the final mark for each student
themselves (group mark +- individual adjustment), and then manually override the group
submission mark with each student’s final mark in the gradebook. This works but
is clunky and has a lot of potential for human error, so really isn’t ideal. Does anyone have any thoughts about how
this might be solvable? What would really be ideal is the capacity to add an "extra credit" type criterion to the marking guide that doesn't affect the total the assignment is marked out of, and that can accept positive or negative marks. But I don't think that's possible. I don't know the version of Moodle I'm using I'm afraid - my university uses a customised version called Stream, and I can't work out how to get the version number. *In the unlikely case of the combination of a group score plus an
individual adjustment resulting in a mark higher than the intended
maximum of 50, the final mark would remain at 50.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group assignments with adjustments to individuals' marks
ResponsesInList.Text: Why can't you make them two different assignment activities ? The first with the submission and the group rubric and the second with the individual contribution rubric. Set the second to "no submission". Put both grade items into a category in the gradebook and sum the two to equal 50. It's not perfect, but it would preserve that group grade since you don't need to override anything. If you set the individual grade activity to visible groups, then graders can filter by groups as they grade it and have the group submission activity open in another browser window for reference. So, you'll get one grade for each group in the first assignment, then one grade per person in the second.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CAN YOU AUTOMATICALLY SEND A FEEDBACK FILE
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dusty. Could you use the activity completion and restrict access settings to make the feedback file available? Set the assignment activity completion to "Student must submit to this activity to complete it". Then put the feedback file in as a resource in Moodle. Set that file to restrict access to students who complete the activity (submit it). You could even keep it hidden until students meet the restriction (it's greyed out by default). It will automatically show up for students, but won't be "sent" to them--they'd have to click on it. I'd also indent the resource in the topic block so it appears subordinate to the activity. I can't think of any other way to do what you want automatically. Maybe someone else can.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student Feedback Notification Email Without Grade
ResponsesInList.Text: Alright, for those who may have a similar issue, I was able to work around this by using the "Use Marking Workflow" option in the "Grade" section of the assignment settings. After uploading the feedback files, the email notifications can be sent to the students by selecting all users in the "View all submission" page, and then choose the "Set marking workflow state" from the "With selected" drop-down. Next, choose "Released', and then "Yes" to notify students. The email notifications for the feedback will then be sent, even without any grades entered.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have one user who is unable to upload anything above 90KB on any assignment on any course. All of these assignments have a limit of 56MB. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Version 3.1 - Single user cannot upload anything above 90 KB
ResponsesInList.Text: First off, these things do not just happen, so what's changed? Find that out and it might answer your question. There are three areas where filesizes can be limited, the Server, depending on the server, so that can be altered in the iis .ini file in windows Server, the httpd.config file in Apache to set the file sizes to a particular size. You will need to discuss these changes with your Systems Admin people to get these changed. The second place to change is the php.ini file. the values of max_file_size, max_post_size and max_time_out need to be increased to suit your need. There should only be one useable PHP instance on your server so there it will be. But again, you may need to check with your Systems admins to get this checked. You can look at the PHP.ini file values by going to Site Admin > Server > PHP info, unless the System Admin have turned it off. The last place is inside Moodle, there is a site wide setting in Site Admin > Courses > Course Default Settings    and see what the Site Maximum upload size is. There is also a limit placed in all courses so in Course > Edit Settings > Files and Uploads. That should cover it all. AFAIK , Moodle has never had an issue with differentiating User uploads, so is there something the Users have done to limit their own uploads? Never heard of any such thing, but anything is possible, I suppose. Don't know about uploading from a phone though....mmmmmmmm

ResponsesInList.Title: Improvement on Assignment module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I write to propose a proposal I put in Moodle Tracker . Case: NDL-59414 ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-59414 ) and wish to get more responses to support for this development by voting and suggesting how it could be put into moodle. Current Situation The assignment module allow use of rubrics for marking. This can effectively control variances of marker's mark and also to provide feedback to students. The module allows students to predetermine the level of expectation from the teacher. Problem/Limitation There is a limitation of the rubrics. It provides the user to "copy" an existing rubric. However, it does not allow us to merge multiple rubrics.  It is often after a few delivery of the same course, we will have different rubrics because different assignment given to students. With this limitation, we have to "type" new rubrics even the decided rubrics is a combination of readily rubrics. The Proposed Changes 1. To allow a collection of rubrics that administrator can set that the teacher can copy and merge as one. 2. To allow the teacher to select rubrics from own as well as administrator, merge as one 3. To allow changes made to the newly "merged" or "created" rubrics. Please help to vote for these improvement so teachers using rubrics can be more effective in their designs. thank you Jack

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notifying Specific Users of Assignment Submissions

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to view Assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Sounds like maybe a permissions issue?  Do the users have different roles?   Can you still view them on the direct logins?  Can you post screenshots?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to view Assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Emma, thank you for your response. This does not look like a permissions issue because its the same id. So for example: Colleague 1: is able to view in direct login, not able to view through remote desktop login (with same user credentials) Colleague 2: is able to view in both logins Both colleagues have the same designer role. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issues with PDF files in the grading interface
ResponsesInList.Text: This thread is a few months old but adding my fix here in case anyone finds this via Google like I did: Was running into the ghostscript 'Rangecheck' crash during the document conversions task, I'm guessing on only about 1 in 1000 conversions or so but that was frequent enough for it to become a major pain point for us. Our server was running gs version 8.7 (Version installed by yum from epel repos on CentOS 6.8). Downloading and compiling version 9.21 from the ghostscript git , and replacing v8.7 with v9.21, fixed the issue. If you're on Fedora/RHEL-flavored Linux and compiling from source scares you, this script will do the heavy lifting: #!/bin/bash yum install git git clone --branch gs921 git://git.ghostscript.com/ghostpdl.git cd ghostpdl ./autogen.sh ./configure make make install mv /usr/bin/gs /usr/bin/gs.87 mv /usr/bin/local/gs /usr/bin/gs exit 0

Ok, let's take this slowly .... what is the output of: ps aux |grep libreoffice In your case soffice, I guess. Here's an example ... note there is only ONE process ... there are not multples. [root@moodle ktask]# ps aux |grep libreoffice root      1953  0.0  0.0 103332   852 pts/0    S+   22:13   0:00 grep libreoffice root      7954  0.0  0.5 1043232 88892 ?       Sl   Apr06   0:01 /usr/lib64/libreoffice/program/soffice.bin --headless --invisible --nocrashreport --nodefault --nologo --nofirststartwizard --norestore --accept=socket,host=127.0.0.1,port=2002,tcpNoDelay=1;urp;StarOffice.ComponentContext What does your listener setup look like ... here's the one on the CentOS 6 server am using: See the bolded line?  And for others reading ... yeah, it's running as root. Note this line (below) is commented out but it was the line I used when trouble shooting things.  The -vvv gives more verbose output ... it's where one might see that the listener had to be launched by unoconv ... it could not find a listener to talk to.   When that happened, it also didn't kill itself when done and eventually clogged things up.   Had to kill -9 PID all but the first soffice.bin process to regain some semblance of 'control' #cmd="/usr/bin/unoconv -vvv --listener &" Add that line to yours ... commenting out the normal line ... and then watch the process via terminal ... forget the GUI for now. [root@moodle init.d]# cat unoconvd #!/bin/sh ### BEGIN INIT INFO # Provides: # Required-Start:    $remote_fs $syslog # Required-Stop:     $remote_fs $syslog # Default-Start:     2 3 4 5 # Default-Stop:      0 1 6 # Short-Description: Start daemon at boot time # Description:       Enable service provided by daemon. ### END INIT INFO #UNO_PATH=/opt/libreoffice5.2/program unoconv --listener dir="/opt/openoffice4/program" #cmd="/usr/bin/unoconv -vvv --listener &" cmd="/usr/bin/unoconv --listener" user="root" name=`basename $0` pid_file="/var/run/$name.pid" stdout_log="/var/log/$name.log" stderr_log="/var/log/$name.err" get_pid() { cat "$pid_file" } is_running() { [ -f "$pid_file" ] && ps `get_pid` > /dev/null 2>&1 } case "$1" in start) if is_running; then echo "Already started" else echo "Starting $name" cd "$dir" if [ -z "$user" ]; then sudo $cmd >> "$stdout_log" 2>> "$stderr_log" & else sudo -u "$user" $cmd >> "$stdout_log" 2>> "$stderr_log" & fi echo $! > "$pid_file" if ! is_running; then echo "Unable to start, see $stdout_log and $stderr_log" exit 1 fi fi ;; stop) if is_running; then echo -n "Stopping $name.." kill `get_pid` killall soffice.bin for i in {1..10} do if ! is_running; then break fi echo -n "." sleep 1 done echo if is_running; then echo "Not stopped; may still be shutting down or shutdown may have failed" exit 1 else echo "Stopped" if [ -f "$pid_file" ]; then rm "$pid_file" fi fi else echo "Not running" fi ;; restart) $0 stop if is_running; then echo "Unable to stop, will not attempt to start" exit 1 fi $0 start ;; status) if is_running; then echo "Running" else echo "Stopped" exit 1 fi ;; *) echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|restart|status}" exit 1 ;; esac exit 0 What does yours look like? Can you start/stop/check on status? From: https://docs.moodle.org/31/en/Installing_unoconv#Ubuntu_16.04_LTS it says: Potential problems: On some systems the apache user home directory is set to a non existent folder. This can cause unoconv to fail. There are 2 solutions to this - one is to make a (writable) home directory for the apache user (like /home/www-data). The other is to run a unoconv listener (described below) as another user other than the apache user (someone with a valid, writable home directory). On the above link/page there's more info that might worth your time to read. AND this: Run a unoconv listener Unoconv utilises a client/server process when converting documents. By default, when there is no running server process - each time unoconv runs it will start a server process, send its request and shut down the server process when the request is complete. The drawback of this mode is that if 2 requests are submitted simultaneously - this can cause the first request to shutdown the server process when the second request is still in progress - and the second conversion request fails. A more robust way to configure unoconv is to start a server process at boot time, and/or run a script to monitor it and restart it if it crashes. To start a unoconv listener at boot time - you need a start up script. Different operating systems and Linux distributions use different startup scripts - but here are some examples of startup scripts for different systems. Here's the link to Ubuntu listener service: https://docs.moodle.org/31/en/mod/assign/feedback/editpdf/testunoconv/upstart Hopefully, the info above might lead to the resolution ... from what you've shared, it looks like the listener you've got configured isn't for Ubuntu. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to grade assignment after upgrade to Moodle 3.2.2+ (Build: 20170331)
ResponsesInList.Text: Did you try those commands shared earlier? unoconv setup is really old tech ... client/server ... again, to repeat ... it is NOT a daemon like apache or mysql ... a true server that can get multiple request and handle them. unoconv listener is setup to prevent lock up ... if you read that pages linked to previously it explains that.   And from what you've described, that's exactly what's happening to your server. Unoconv listener gets a job sends it to libreoffice (you see it as soffice.bin) which does the actual conversion. Converted files get passed back or saved locatons where Moodle code can see them.   After unoconv and libreoffice does the conversion they do not stay running ... but listen again for the next request.  So it's wash, rinse, dry, repeat ... wash, rinse, dry, repeat. (very boring life unoconv has). Why?  Dunno ... you've hinted that there might have been some update recently ... yep, that could be a factor or the actual cause.   Here again ... both Al and I don't have direct access to your server and can only ask questions .. point to docs ... other blogs ... make educated guesses! ;) If it's still not resolved ... strongly suggest removing the path to unoconv ... you can always put it back again ... that will allow teachers to grade ... just can use Annotated stuff. Later, when teachers are all caught up you might consider asking teachers if there is any up-coming assignments students will have to turn in .. certain date, etc.  ... so you can work out a schedule to revisit the issue.   If you do it that way, post something to the community forum on front page of your Moodle that informs students/teachers ... or ... reserve Sat. Sun. as time to work with it. OR get the new person hired PDQ!!!! 'spirit of sharing'. Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: I apologize ahead of time as this is probably not what you want to hear. I've played with unoconv a lot over the past two months in CentOS 6 and 7, and have come to the conclusion, that if you cannot get unoconv to work in Moodle, you do not have your server set up correctly. Even when I was able to get unoconv to work in a Linux terminal window, but not in Moodle, the problem was still the server setup. I finally got it working when I did all of the following: made sure I had the latest unoconv version 0.7 right from github setup a listener made sure the listener was running if/after system reboots installed latest version of python installed latest version of PHP 7 installed latest database - since I was doing this for testing, I installed both Mariadb and Postgresql installed latest version of Libre Office on the server made sure my firewall was not blocking pythons use of port 2002 checked all the entries in SELinux Troubleshooter and made sure that I fixed all the problems - there were multiple different ones for httpd - two of which affected unoconv The server I set up last week has multiple Moodle sites, some using MariDB and some using Postgre SQL , Unoconv works in all of them. I think the most important items that prevented me from getting unoconv to work before was not enabling port 2002 and not having httpd set to allow it to setattr access on the moodle data folders.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Submissions have draft status even though Require Submit Button is NO
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nancy. I use Moodle 2.6 and this sometime happens to us. If you set the assignment settings to "Require student to click submit button -- YES" then a submit button will appear for the students when they upload their work.  If students upload their work and FORGET to click the submit button, it wll display as a Draft on the teacher's end until the student goes back to the assignment and clicks that submit button. However, If you se the assignment settings to "Require student to click submit button -- NO" then there will be no submit button for the students. They simply upload an assignment and it automatically is submitted. If a student decides to update the file, then when they upload a new file and clicks save, then the assignment will re-submit for a new grade (though the old grade will still be visible until a new grade is entered). In the second scenario, drafts will occur if a student starts to upload an assignment, but no save it, or clicks on the upload a file, but never actually upload a file.... or at other times, they just come in as drafts. We had three kids' assignments come in as drafts this morning. We just had them goin, and re-save the assigment, then the appeared correctly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unoconv and PDF annotation issue on Moodle 3.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Probably should refrain from commenting, but ... that's not my nature. Think about this a minute ... the latest 3.2 of Moodle ...   to get Search requires an Apache extension ... Solr which requires the installation of JRE. (is there a solr extension for IIS?) There is also the issue you are having now with Unoconv (will admit that many seem to have issues with this regardless of platform, but ...).   Unoconv is really a python script that interfaces into headless libreoffice. ( BTW , from what I've read about office suites lately, OpenOffice seems to have stagnated but not so with LibreOffice). None of the above is native to Windows. Note that unoconv is 'faceless' (being a script) as is the process used to do doc conversions ... libreoffice in a headless mode), the JRE/solr thing does have a web based interface into it's config which probably should NOT be accessible cept to those who admin the server/service. In working with the MySQL DB most often is recommended PHPMyAdmin ... a php based app.  Ok, running MSSQL ... is there a php based or any based web app for remotely admin? Just maintaining (updates and upgrading) a Moodle site via FTP is, IMHO , antiquated ... Moodle has yet a way to update or upgrade a Moodle from within Moodle Admin itself (Worpress, Joomla, and other very popular open sourced web based apps do).   By far the easiest way to maintain (acquire updates and/or upgrades) is via git .   Git is also not native to Windows. And a real bottom question ... what does a GUI interface into a server that runs software that for the most part is 'faceless', really do for the server Admin? Now in defense of Windows ... Microsoft is coming around ... no longer the 300 pound gorilla they used to be.   They are developing/have developed a Linux of their own ... to help with the Guest OS's on Azure (will never release that to the public).   There's additional software one can install now that enables the server admin to run bash shell scripts .... etc.   BUT, is all that compatible with the version of Windows you are running right now (this is not to mention the licensing fees [Microsoft Tax]). In certain areas, don't think one can beat a Windows server ... LDAP comes to mind here. But for open sourced apps such as a Moodle? Analogy (poor one at that) ... if I had a Mercedes don't think I'd be taking it to the local Joe's Mechanic shop unless there were some mechanics that had Mercedes training/equipment/parts, etc. My 2 'sense' ... nope, spelled it right! ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unoconv and PDF annotation issue on Moodle 3.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Kinda hijacking this discussion but may as well Am learning a little more nearly every week about cli on Linux ... have to in some cases ... CentOS 7 is out now. (Debian is same).   Most commands one uses in Linux are in every Linux - bash shell is bash shell.  And all of them are now beginning to take LSB (Linux Standards Base) at little more seriously ... which is a good thing! With Moodle marching forward often, there's that as well. This to say ... the 'learning' never ends.  Isn't teaching the same way? .... a little more about Webmin ... Back when I had 40 school servers to admin, CLI only was taking a long time when a security update (0 day) was available.   That's when I decided to 'get a life' and seek a way to do some things on all 40 at once.    Solution Webmin. Still use it today in situation where there are 5 Rackspace hosted CentOS 6 boxen.  One of those is designated 'Webmin Central' ... the other 4 have a webmin of their own but I don't have to access each individual server for some things.   Each server, has a bash shell script that checks versions ... MySQL, PHP, Apache, Moodle ... that script is called 'mversions'.   From Central, I can create a 'custom command' which executes that /usr/local/bin/mversions on ALL servers. I have several 'custom commands' like that on 'Central'. One of which is an update to Moodle ... all servers are 'git' installed and maintained.  So there's a 'custom command' to 'Update Moodles'.   One button click on Central executes the 'update' script on the local host Webmin, then goes to the  other linked Webmin servers and excutes that servers 'update' bash shell script.   Nice thing about that ... the script is called the same, but if there is a need to do something different on one, only that servers 'update' script need be changed.    What used to take a little less than an hour per server, now takes 30 minutes at the most. In order to use Webmin efficiently, a good understanding of the OS (the apps) and bash shell scripting is needed.  So your 'comfort' at CLI comes in real handy. Should point out how significant is using Webmin to git update or upgrade Moodles really is.   Have done some research and even attempted some programming in PHP for using git to update or upgrade Moodles.   Difficult to do.   Webmin, however, uses Perl (that's perhaps the 'first P' in ' LAMP ' - Perl/Python/PHP - and in that order) and can call git just like one was the root user logged on via ssh. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email Notification
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a way to get only selected people to receive emails for assignment submissions.  Here is the scenario: You have two roles, Teacher, and TA.  You only want the TA to receive notifications about the submitted assignment.  Both roles must have the mod/assignment:grade capability. In the course create two groups, EmailGroup and NoEmailGroup.  Enroll add all of the students and the TA to the EmailGroup and the Teacher to the NoEmailGroup. Now edit the assignment.  Go under Common module settings and set "Group mode" to "Seperate groups." Emails will now only go to the people in the EmailGroup with th mod/assignment:grade capability assuming the student submitting the assignment is also in that group.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email Notification
ResponsesInList.Text: Marc, I can think of two cases, and the solution to each one of them would be: CASE 1: There is only one teacher in the course and you want that teacher, only in that course not to receive notifications, for that you can do this: Go to the "course administration" block of the course in question Expand "Users", click on "Permissions" On the top left corner of the screen, under "Advance role override", select "Teacher" Under "Filter" type the word 'notification' Change to "Prevent" or "Prohibit" these capabilities: Receive grader submission notifications, Receive email notification, Get a notification message when an attempt is submitted, etc. You get the idea... Click the "Save changes button" Repeat steps 4-6, but this time under "Filter"  type the word 'email'.  Look for the items that you want prohibited or disabled and enact them. CASE 2:  There is more than 1 teacher in the course and you want to disable notifications for only one (or just for some) of two or more teachers, for that you can do this: Create a new profile in the system (based off of the "Teacher" role) called "Teacher - No Notifications" or something similar Prohibit or prevent the same capabilities that you did in case 1 Remove the "Teacher" role and assign the newly created role to those teachers who do not want to receive notifications. Hope this helps.  Have a blessed afternoon. Sam Villamizar

ResponsesInList.Text: I just wanted to add that you could also use CASE 2 for all instances, instead of having two methods. -sv

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic Grade for Submission
ResponsesInList.Text: I see what you are saying Steve. I will share my experience with this conversation with our teachers, just for what it is worth We required that our teachers add a zero so that an accurate grade for that item missing is calculated.  In an extreme example, If it is the last day of the semester a student has one assignment turned in, earned 100%, but didn't turn anything else in, what is sent to our SIS is 100% - A. Parents are happy, student is happy, but in reality they are failing since they haven't turned anything else in for the rest of the class. Adding a zero communicates to all parties with access (student, parents, etc) that the items were not completed. (this could go in to a whole other gradebook conversation, but that is for another forum What the teacher accepts and grades after a late assignment is submitted (full, partial, or zero credit), we leave up to individual teachers discretion. Philosophically we have many teachers who believe that adding zeros, even if they were to allow full credit later, is actually demotivational to high school students and doesn't communicate the right message to student, that being, all work needs to be completed to meet the objectives of the course. Many students will see a zero and think  "well, missed that guess I move on." IMO it connects more with educational teaching philosophy and institutional policy. That said, I would like to see Moodle be able to support all grading philosophies and policies

ResponsesInList.Text: If you happen to use Moodlerooms, you can send out alerts to students as you described.  There is a tool called the personalized learning designer.  You can set up notifications to be automatically sent out at specified times.  I don't think Moodle core has this functionality.  This is an add-on unique to Moodlerooms.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic Grade for Submission
ResponsesInList.Text: If you go to the full view of the "categories and items" page, there is a setting titled "aggregate only non-empty grades."  If you un-check the box corresponding to that setting, Moodle will then assume that a blank cell in the grade book equates to a zero.  Be careful, though, because this applies to all assignments.  If a student is excused on an assignment, he/she will receive a zero for it if it's left blank in the grade book.  So, while the system is capable of saving you time entering in zeros, you should also use it with caution or else it might end up costing you more time in the end.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to disable or make invisible the coursepage's assignment link once the assignment has been submitted?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Find all student assignment submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: I've got the desired result although it takes a while to execute: SELECT distinct(mdl_files.contenthash) as contenthash, mdl_files.filename FROM mdl_log INNER JOIN mdl_course ON mdl_log.course = mdl_course.id INNER JOIN mdl_resource ON mdl_log.info = mdl_resource.id INNER JOIN mdl_context ON mdl_log.cmid = mdl_context.instanceid INNER JOIN mdl_files ON mdl_context.id = mdl_files.contextid WHERE (mdl_files.userid='2115' and mdl_files.component='assignsubmission_file' and mdl_files.source IS NOT NULL) group by mdl_files.contenthash This I will use to make a batch file to copy and rename all the files into one folder. Hopefully it might help someone else in the future

ResponsesInList.Title: Unable to set passing grade as completion requirement in 3.1? Only A (any) grade.
ResponsesInList.Text: We have recently upgraded from 2.7 to 3.1 We have completion data set up in all our courses that all assignments have a particular grade to pass. This is set at the activity level and the completion data for the course is set to show those activities that are required to pass the course. In 2.7, we could set the minimum grade to pass and an activity was not considered complete until this grade was achieved. In 3.1, we can still set the passing grade in the Grade Book Settings. BUT, we cannot tell the activity that a PASSING grade is required. Moodle thinks any grade is ok to set that activity as complete (even if the passing grade is not met). So our course completion data is now saying that students have completed the course when in fact they have not as they do not have the right grade for an assignment. The icons for pass/fail are working correctly. So moodle knows there is a minimum grade to change the icon, BUT it ignores it for completion data. This is what moodle is expecting now or is this a bug? Does anyone else have the same issue? If this is what moodle is expecting, then it's a useless function for us and we now have no way but to manually check thousands of courses for passing. It seems ridiculous if the passing grade option is not there for completion data.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to set passing grade as completion requirement in 3.1? Only A (any) grade.
ResponsesInList.Text: Further to this, the following seems to be happening (we have 2 attempts to get a passing grade set):- Student submits and passes all work - course completion is triggered as complete - this is expected and correct. Student submits all work, but assignment is reopened (after grading) for second attempt to receive passing grade (not yet a passing grade is assigned) - course completion is triggered as complete - this should not happen as the student has another attempt at an assessment. Course is not yet complete but moodle signals it is. Student submits all work, but fails two attempts at an assignment (as per our activity settings, 2 attempts allowed) - course completion is triggered as complete - this is expected and correct. The student has no more attempts so the course is complete (albeit failed). So it seems that this might be a bug? Moodle is not considering the impact of reopened attempts as part of its completion workflow. It should ignore reopened attempts and not  mark course as complete until all the attempts are exhausted or all activities set receive a passing grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Accidental group assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, Using Moodle 2.9, and I've had two incidents today where a teacher has set "Students submit in groups" to "yes" in an assignment. The group was set to "default group", so every single student in the subject became a group member. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2.4  ASSIGNMENT- how to upload multiple feedback files in zip
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, it is possible to upload a zip file with feedback for multiple students. The key is to be sure you have the naming convention sorted. Or risk giving the wrong student the wrong feedback! So most likely you will be using a word-merge or other means of generating the feedback automatically. Make sure your assignment has Feedback types of both Offline grading Sheet and Feedback files 'View All Submissions' and then Grading Action - Download Grading Worksheet. This csv file will have Column A - Participant Number. This number is unique to the student AND the assignment, e.g. Participant 401 ,  And Column B - Full name, e.g. Joe Bloggs . Use this spreadsheet file to create the following naming convention for your feedback files. e.g. " Joe Bloggs_401_assignsubmission_file_.pdf ". As far as I can tell the underscores are important! Zip your renamed feedback files. 'Grading Action - Upload multiple feedback files in a zip', drag and drop your zip file in. Sit back and enjoy a well earned break. On trialling I think you may be better off putting each feedback file in its own folder per student e.g. A folder called ' Joe Bloggs_401_assignsubmission_file_ ' with a feedback file such as 'JoesFeedback.pdf ', but I have not tested this enough to be sure.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2.4  ASSIGNMENT- how to upload multiple feedback files in zip
ResponsesInList.Text: Further edit- Rename your file to "Joe Bloggs_401_assignsubmission_file_JoesFeedback.pdf " causes a rename in the file the student sees to JoesFeedback.pdf .

ResponsesInList.Title: Revert submission to draft vs. Allow another attempt

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Revert submission to draft vs. Allow another attempt
ResponsesInList.Text: 'Revert submission to draft' is basically an 'undo' for students who have incorrectly submitted an assignment - it allows them to go back and change the files before submitting again. 'Allow another attempt' saves the submission and the feedback into the submission history and allows them to create a new submission (optionally based on their original submission), which will have its own feedback associated with it.

I took on the case and using the xhprof/moodle profile tool I identified that there was a PDF Submission / PDF Feedback module being used on the mod assignment which was the source of the problem. Removal of this 'pdf' directory in both cases resulted in immediate performance improvement from 60 secs down to 3 secs. I then installed the latest version of both from https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=assignsubmission_pdf & https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=assignfeedback_pdf and all is still well. I suspect this problem for us was due to the module not being updated when we updated from Moodle 2.5 to 2.6. Not sure whether it will help anyone else but thought I'd share nonetheless. Cheers, Kim
