ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Integration beta 2 release!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Okay, we got it working in Win32. It would seem that in the win32 builds of cURL/PHP that by default there is not certificate specified where as in the linux distributions has a default certificate name and path. We ran the script to test the curl ssl connections on both Win32 and Linux. We were surprised to get a very different result on each platform. curl_test.php '; print_r(curl_getinfo($ch)); echo ''; echo 'Errors: ' . curl_errno($ch) . ' ' . curl_error($ch) . '

'; curl_close ($ch); echo $result . 'EOF'; ?> The following screenshots show the different errors Linux At the bottom of the above image you will see that both the path and the file name to the certificate are specified. It's an easy fix in Linux, just get your CA cert bundle and move it into the the above path and change it's filename to ca-certificates.crt and bingo! Turn it in works correctly. Win32 You should notice that this error is very different (and kind of scary!) and somewhat miss leading. After checking the PHP source code for the php_curl.dll it has no default certificate path or filename specified for the Win32 builds. So it appears that on win32 systems you must set your CA certs path and filename using the php curl_setopt command ie: curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_CAINFO, "c:/php/ca-certificates.crt"); Once this was set in the curl_test.php code that we were using to test the win32 platform we got this result Woo Hoo!!! It we now have a secure ssl connection using cURL in Win32! Next step we need to modify two files in moodle to enable the turnitin intergration to use ssl in win32 turnitinlib.php - add the highlighted line (making sure you point the path to your CA cert bundle) After this we were still having not much success connecting so we had to hunt a little further, at which point we found that we also needed to modify the following file filelib.php - add the highlighted line (making sure you point the path to your CA cert bundle) We are not really sure if we stuck the code in the correct places but it works, we now have a fully functioning Win32 moodle server using the turnitin integration That being said it might pay to get this code added to the administration management interface so people can set the path to their CA cert bundle via a gui rather than have to edit the php file. Linux users can just drop the file into the correct path. CREDITS: This fix was not discovered by me but rather my work mate Rob who spent the last couple of days pulling his hair out trying to find the differences between cURL in linux and windows.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Integration beta 2 release!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Can I suggest that you abstract the two curl_setopt() calls to the config.php file? This way you can reuse the code on multiple platforms without having to edit the filelib.php and turnitinlib.php files every time you want to deploy it somewhere new. It would then look something like this in both the above files: 
```text
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_CAINFO, $CFG->CApath);
```
 and like this in the config.php: 
```text
$CFG->CApath = "C:/php/ca-certificates.crt";
```

Hi Dan, I had some minor issues doing a straight upgrade from the beta 2 to 1.0, but it was relatively easy to work around. What I had to do was find and remove entries in mdl_capabilities that were related to the TII plugin before I could successfully upgrade. Here was the query I ran before doing the upgrade in Moodle: 
```text
DELETE 


FROM
 
`mdl_capabilities`


WHERE
 
`name`
 
LIKE
 
'%moodle/turnitin:%'
```
 After that, it upgraded seamlessly. You might want to put a check into your db upgrade scripts to see if the values exist in mdl_capabilities before doing an INSERT statement, and change it to an UPDATE statement if they do.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin Release V1.0 for Moodle 1.9.2+
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan and Michael, I'll do my best to try and explain how it works. The reason when you are in native Turnitin and you are viewing a match to another student paper, and you are given a link where you can open that paper in a new window and see the content of the paper as well as all the metadata such as the author, title, when it was submitted, etc. is because that paper was submitted to an assignment and a class of which you were the instructor of as well, and so theoretically, you had access to all of that information anyway. It is a bit different through our Moodle integration (at least the one produced by Turnitin, not sure if it's the same with Dan's patch implementation - it depends on how he handles the multiple instructor issue), in that for each course in Moodle, we create a separate "pseudo" instructor in Turnitin because courses in Turnitin can only have one instructor, but in Moodle, they can have multiple instructors. That way, any time an instructor in Moodle interacts with the Turnitin plugin, then to Turnitin they all look like that single "pseudo" instructor. This is relevant because when you have a match in an originality report to another paper that is in another class in which you are an instructor for in Moodle, Turnitin cannot readily determine that because to the Turnitin system, it looks like 2 different instructors. Thus, it tries to email you the content of the paper along with some of the other metadata (institution name, paper title, class, when it was uploaded and percentage match - but you are right - it does not show the student name. As far as I know, but I'm not the expert on it here at Turnitin, it is done this way because or privacy issues and intellectual property issues, but don't take my word for it. The best way to get the exact reason is to submit the question to our HelpDesk ( www.turnitin.com/help/helpdesk ), and they should be able to give you a complete explanation. I hope this helps. Thanks, Dave

Note: with some of the older code I wrote, there was a check to see if the user was a student or an "instructor" when returning the report which was failing and was always logging in as the instructor - make sure you're using the latest version of the code available from the modules and plugins database.

This then prevents the download of the file as the symbols are interpreted by the browser according to their web meaning rather than as part of the file name of the submission. Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: User-defined scale shows up as percenatage
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We created a user-defined scale (Satisfactory/Excellent) for our assignments.  In defining the scale, I ordered these in such a way that Satisfactory would end up as the default in the drop-drown box while grading.  We did not include an "unsatisfactory," since the assignment is marked complete based on if it has been graded. Unfortunately, we're finding that users who got an "Excellent" also see a "0%" as their grade (when they look at their grades, which include both ones using this scale and numerically scored quizzes), whereas if they got "Satisfactory," they see "100%." I'm wondering if anyone has any suggestions, knowledge, or experience on how best to correct this problem....both in terms of making it work (e.g., is there any way to have a user-defined scale that doesn't show up also as a percentage?) and fixing student's scores in the database so that they're right once the problem has been corrected in the design. My guess is perhaps the "user-defined scale" concept really isn't completely ready for production-use if one wants it not to show a percentage, and that we should stick with numerical grades only and then do a database query that will change people's grades to the appropriate one once we use numerical grades (?).  Or is there a way that user-defined scales can actually work? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User-defined scale shows up as percenatage
ResponsesInList.Text: Nevermind...I should have read the documentation a little more carefully.  So we've fixed this by assigning a new scale which works better with how percentages are assigned.  Apparently any scales items are put into the database as 1,2,3, etc. and then shown on a percentage scale mapping 1 to 0 and the highest number to 100.  We've replaced the scale and updated the various database tables so everyone's score is correct for the new system. My one pet peeve is that the highest possible score is always the default in the dropdown box.  That's why we had originally created it so that "Satisfactory" was on top...we wanted that to be the default, so the grader would need to specifically change it to grade as "Excellent," but could just press the save button if the assignment should get "Satisfactory." It would be nice if the person setting up a given assignment could specify what the dropdown box defaults to.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: video as an assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Basically what Mary just said ... But I want to elaborate a little. I t would help to know what version of Moodle you are using, and how long the videos are, to answer your question. In Moodle 2.3 the assignment changed and so did some of your options. But simply put, you can offer your students the option to upload a file, as the assignment submission. If you are uploading videos (ie not shooting them from a webcam) then MP4 is  probably the best format. That is because it plays back on most devices and is well supported by online video players. But asking your students to convert their own files might be tricky. So it will probably depend on how you are asking them to record their videos. File size depends on your server , the distance from your students to the server, and the length of the videos, and how they are recording them. But in general small is good. When shooting from a webcam, I aim to keep file sizes no greater than 1.5M per minute. Actually I worked with an organisation earlier this year who needed very long video files uploaded as assignment submissions. We made a Youtube assignment submission type. The plan is to release that back to the community. This would clear up the need to worry about file formats or file size.

ResponsesInList.Title: Multiple Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: This has been asked in various ways before but I was wondering if this would be more achievable with the changes to Assignments in 2.3 We have an occasional requirement where a student submits an Assignment, the lecturer grades and gives feedback then returns to the student who may make amendments and then resubmit. At the moment, the way the assignment works the student would delete the first attempt and replace with a new version. Then when the lecturer regraded the first set of feedback would be overwritten too. For me an option rather like the quizzes allow multiple attempts would be ideal here which would mean that after allowing a resubmission it would be a different attempt and the old one (with corresponding feedback/score) is locked away somewhere. This would provide a record of number of resubmissions and evidence of feedback and versions for audit purposes. Is this more feasible to achieve via a plug-in or extension following the changes for 2.3?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, This is a pre-release version of the Assign 2.3 plugins we are developing at ULPGC. Here the "History" plugin. This plugin will allow the student to store current submission in an historic record and return submission status to draft, so being able to submit again. The plugin settings control when the student will see the "resubmission" button. Currently "grading" and "submit & grading" are behaving more or less in the same way. The understanding is that a student can re-submit ONLY after having submitted and have been graded by the teacher. Only after grading  the student can involve in a new submission. The submission is controlled by dates/submission status as normal (no re-submission if the due date is  past). No resubmission if the submission status is "submitted" In order to be able to send new files/text, the student has to use the "Save to History" button that appears in his submission review page. This "Save to History" button saves files & text for current submission, empty the current submission of files and/or online text and return current submission status to draft.. This plugin only knows about files submitted by the "file" plugin and text submitted by "onlinetext" plugin. Teacher feedback loaded either as feedback "comments" or feedback "file" are also stored. There is a table where student or teacher can review previous attempts at this Assignment by an student, saved as the History for the assignment. The history record contains the files & text submitted, submission timestamp, feedback files & text,  grade and grader and marking timestamp. Please, feel free to experiment with the plugin and to request any changes or further refinements. At this stage there are some open topics with the plugin that we will settle as moodle 2.3 will stabilize. Some issues depend on topics that remain open currently in Assign 2.3 core developent. For instance, Assignment Team Based Submissions and Assignment Submission Date Extensions . Particularly, depending on how date extension would be implemented we would need to change the control or re-submission capability for students in one or other way. At this moment this code is in a "just works" state. Code could be simplified, cleaned or refactored. We expect comments, suggestions and  criticism for improving it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: We created a plugin that filled this need in Moodle 1.9, but I'm quite surprised (disappointed ) that Moodle 2.3 does have a simple ways of handling Assignment resubmissions. This is a VERY basic need. The approach described by Enrique sounds interesting (thank for taking that on!). I will definitely try it out, but our own purposes, we would need something more automated, like this: If the received grade is less than the “grade to pass” and the “allow resubmission” = yes , then save submission/grade/feedback (archive it)  and Revert submission to draft . This would require some changes to the way Moodle works, namely the following: I don’t think the new assignment module has the “allow resubmission” function (actually, I don’t recall seeing it since Moodle 1.9). If so, we’d need that back.  Better yet, add an extra toggle that would allow for conditional resubmission - only if “grade to pass” is not met, like this: http://screencast.com/t/172nIJmiWLS The “grade to pass” setting is buried in the gradebook, which makes it very time consuming to modify in courses with lots of assignments. It should also be included in the assignment settings screen like this: http://screencast.com/t/a9zUxjDP2w Any feedback on this method would be welcome. Would be good to come up with a method that could be posted as a feature request in the Moodle Tracker .  We really need this to be part of the core. For now, our team will probably add this ability to our Marking Manager plugin. As I noted above, this plugin was able to track past submissions in Moodle 1.9, as shown in screenshot 1 and screenshot 2 … and it looks like we’ll have to try and find a way of bringing it back for Moodle 2.3. Cheers, Fernando PS. Enrique, would you consider posting your code into the Moodle plugins repository?

ResponsesInList.Title: Error message when trying to download submitted assignment files | v. 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Am getting the following error message when clicking to download all assignments from a new Assignment activity: Fatal error: Maximum execution time of 30 seconds exceeded in /home/sitename/public_html/moodle/lib/filestorage/zip_archive.php on line 106 I'm now obliged I think to download all the student submissions separately, and there are hundreds of them. Can anyone suggest what's going on? Kind thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error message when trying to download submitted assignment files | v. 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Francois, If I am not mistaken, it means your php max_execution_time is set for 30 seconds. Since you say there are hundreds of submissions, php is running out of time before it can complete making the zip file to download all submissions at one time. If you use groups like I do, you can try to download one group at a time. If not using groups, you will need to change the php_max_execution_time in the php.ini file to a greater amount of seconds. (I am using 45 seconds but have a fairly fast cpu and never download more than 70 submissions at a time.) You will also need to restart the web server to put the change into effect. Hope this helps, AL

ResponsesInList.Title: Assignment changes for 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, NetSpot has received a number of feature requests for the assignment module in Moodle and in order to make these changes and contribute them back to Moodle core, we have agreed to perform the redevelopment work Martin has planned for the assignment module in Moodle 2.3. The main part of the work is developing a new assignment module (mod_assign) that combines all of the functionality of the previous 4 assignment subtypes. There will be an upgrade path from the old assignment module to the new one and the old one will not be removed for at least one major moodle release (but will be disabled so that new assignments use the new module). There are a number of other features we will be working on once the core redevelopment is complete and the specifications are being developed here: http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Assignment We welcome your feedback either in this forum or on the wiki page linked above. Regards, Damyon Wiese

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment changes for 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Assorted comments. 1. Re: the presets thing. No other bit of UI in Moodle works that way. The requirement you are trying to implement is a good one, but I think you need to find a better way to do it. 2. Well, with the new wiki in 2.0 (and new workshop), the module went on being called wiki, and successful upgraded from previous versions. Why not keep the name mod_assignment in the same way? (On the other hand, forumng installs along-side forum. It does not upgrade old instances during install, instead, there is an option that you can use later to convert any forum to a forumng.) If you have to go for another name, I would choose mod_assign, or mod_assignmentng (like forumng). You are not allowed digits like 2 in internal plugin names. It will be easier to comment more once you have more of the proposed design.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment changes for 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim Thanks for the comments, 1. our reasoning for the presets thing is that we want to ease the transition for people who are used to the old assignment type. I think it provides a good balance between the requirements of advanced users and beginners but I am keen to hear some more opinions on this (Martin?). 2. this is how it was suggested by Martin and some of the reasons I see for this are: * you won't have people trying to install subtypes into the new assignment module (because it has a different name) * it gives maintainers of the existing assignment subtypes a window to upgrade their plugins * it gives a longer period to test the upgrade code and iron out any wrinkles Regards, Damyon

You will be able to disable the new assignment and re-enable the old one if that is your preference. > 2 options - which one... Otherwise you could target the existing module - the downside being that it will stop recieving updates and new features and will be removed from core Moodle eventually (which means it won't even receive security updates). Or: you could do both - ie target the existing module and write upgrade code to manage the conversion to the new module. > I'm taking a look at https://github.com/netspotau/moodle-mod_assign to get a feel for working with it. Great - but this is more of a prototype. We will write up the design docs and get agreement and then do a fair bit of restructuring of that repo soon - especially around the area of custom subtypes. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment changes for 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Damyon and everyone, Yesterday we had a very useful online meeting with the Electronic Assignment Management (EAM) consortium where we discussed the new Assignment changes and how they overlap with Lightwork and how we can work together. Following on from that meeting I thought it would be useful to share the Lightwork team's high level vision of how we see the new Assignment module and Lightwork working together to enhance and improve Moodle. It would be great to have feedback both from those at the meeting and the rest of the community to ensure that our visions are aligned. The functionality of managing and allocating assignment submissions to markers was one of the topics that was discussed and since this is a key feature already implemented by Lightwork, I'll use it in the following scenario to explain our vision for assignment marking in the Moodle assignment module. In Moodle ======= 1) An assignment is created 2) The teachers (marking managers and markers) can access it and view the list of students who can submit assignments. 3) The marking manager could choose to create a rubric on which the marking would be based. The rubric would be published for the students to view. 4) The marking manager could choose to allocate students to markers for marking. This could be done manually or via an algorithm. 5) Students commence submitting assignments (if a rubric is being used then this would normally follow on from rubric publication) 6) Markers begin marking the submissions of the students that have been assigned to them 7) Markers finish marking and submit their marking to the manager for review 8) The marking manager releases the marking back to the students via gradebook Lightwork ========= Any of the teachers (marking managers or markers) may choose to use Lightwork to perform all or some of steps 2-4 and 6-8 described above. They may wish to use Lightwork instead of the Moodle web interface because: a) They wish to work offline b) They wish to take advantage of Lightwork's ability to manage locally, all the files and students assigned to them for marking. c) They wish to easily create and manage their student feedback and annotations d) They wish to take advantage of Lightwork's ability to generate feedback PDF documents based on a rubric I believe that the key to achieving all of the above is to incorporate Lightwork's marking management database tables and logic into the new assignment module. Please let me know what you all think and whether our visions are aligned. Cheers, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Team assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, As we discussed, I have set up our Lightwork Moodle 2.1 development site with the Team assignment type so that you can see how it could fit our needs for Team assignment in the new assignment module. The site can be accessed at http://lightwork-dev.massey.ac.nz . The course is "301 Social Environment" where I have created "Social Env team assignment 1". There are currently 4 teams: Team 1 - This has 2 student members. Membership is now closed because they have submitted the final submission for marking. Team 2 - This has 2 student members. Membership is now closed because they have submitted the final submission for marking. Team 3 - This has 2 student members. Nothing has been submitted yet Team 4 - This has 2 student members. Nothing has been submitted yet In order to test this I would suggest logging in as another student. Select the help icons for an explanation of the various actions. You can use any of the following student logins (they all have password "password"): jbarry, abashir, cbates, jbeader, jbears, gbell, abellman, rboyd, ycao, jcarter, mchoa Once you login and access the team assignment as one of the above students you could: 1) Create your own team 2) Join one of the existing teams (where membership is still open) 3) After joining a team (you can only join one) you could submit an assignment for marking You could also test team assignment as a teacher. The teacher login is cchadwic with password "password". After opening the assignment you will see that you can view and mark the submissions: 1) By team - where you give a single mark to the whole team 2) By team members - where you give individual marks to team members If you wish to experiment further you could also create a new team assignment. Please remember that this version of team assignment has been ported from the Moodle 1.9 version and so there are still a few bugs that need to be addressed. Note also that the current version is designed to allow students to create the teams. Due to popular demand we also plan a modification to allow teachers to create teams and have more control over membership. Looking forward to your feedback, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Team assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for sharing that Paul. The work you have done is fantastic and certainly meets a need. Some comments from a purely non-technical 'user' perspective... Whilst setting up a 'team' assignment where students not only allocate themselves to teams, but also create the teams, can reject members and can close the teams themselves may be used, some more common occurances at our institution are where the teacher/lecturer assigns students to a 'team' either manually or randomly, or the team membership is already known, or the number of teams is known...ie: teachers manually allocate students to X number of teams (X as set by teacher) system randomly allocates students to X number of teams (X as set by teacher) teacher creates X number of teams and students have to self-register into teams....maybe by a given date - and then membership is closed either on a set date or by the teacher teacher 'asks' the system to create teams with Y number of students in each team I am slightly concerned that the teams assignment doesn't use the existing groups and groupings feature within Moodle. I realise that this has been discussed but I must admit to not fully appreciating the shortcomings of the groups/groupings that has required creation of 'team tables'. From a user perspective I would expect to create my teams using the groups interface and expect a fairly high support overhead for institutions if this is otherwise. The workflow as i see it from a user perspective is that the teams could be created using the 'autocreate groups' feature in groups/groupings that already has built in options for number of groups/members per group, group/member count, allocation method, naming scheme, grouping name. Then the assignment would have a setting that flagged it as a 'team assignment' which would allow one submission per team and would utilise the grading features that your demo displays - ie. the ability to grade as a team or as individual members. Some thought needs to be put in to submission permissions - I note in the demo that as a member of a team I can upload a file and submit and once I have done so no other members can submit and the team membership is closed. This model assumes that all team members agree with the submission - I think this needs to be more explicit and all students in the group need to say "yes - ready" – makes all students accountable (no comeback to say work submitted wasn’t what they agreed on). In practice I wonder how often an assignment will be late as a result of one student not having gone in and clicked "ready for submission" - so should the teacher be able to see the work as soon as it is uploaded (as is the case now) as well as which students of the group have declared that the work is ready for marking. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Team assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Grette, Thanks for your feedback. An important aspect of our team assignment type is to free the teacher from the administrative aspect of creating and managing teams and to empower the students to do this. However, as you and others have pointed out, this doesn't suit all learning environments and there needs to be additional functionality so that teachers can control this. Your suggestions on team creation and submission permissions all look good. We've also had a secondary school asking about ways to prevent students from maliciously removing other students from teams and so there is definitely a requirement to make improvements in this area. As far as using the Moodle groups and groupings feature, I am quite happy to revisit this area. When we built the team assignment, an important requirement was to have a minimal support overhead. This meant that we avoided making any changes to existing Moodle tables as per the recommended Moodle design strategy for building new assignment types. I had a brief look at the work done by Royal Roads Uni at MDL-27250 . They use the Groups and groupings feature but also made changes to existing Moodle tables assignment and assignment_submissions. However, I think that the design of the new team assignment will be very much influenced by the design decision taken at http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Assignment_Subtypes_Combined . We will need to understand exactly how the new team assignment can fit in with the approach chosen here. Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Team assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Paul, As Emma mentioned, we do use Groups and Groupings for a lot of our courses where there is the need to split the students into 'sections' with different instructors, all within the same course.  The course material is the same for both sections so to avoid having to duplicate the course material, we use the Groups and Groupings to define who sees what and share the materials/ activities . We define two Groupings and assign predefined groups to them: All Sections- Individuals: Section A; Section B All Sections - Teams: Team A1, Team A2; Team B1, Team B2 This allows us to choose in the Group Mode for an activity, whether the assignment is for individuals or teams. Once this framework is set up, we can run the entire course selecting activities as we require and the teams are already set.  So to have to redefine teams at the assignment level might be counterproductive. In order for this to work for our model, we need the groupings to separate the sections of our course.  I don't know how those will work with the new 'team assignment' assignment type. Will you be able to assign a Grouping to a team assignment?  Could the Grouping override the team assignment teams?  Could this be an option?  Or would that defeat the purpose of creating the team assignment functionality? Shelley

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Download all submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Anis I have come across the same issue. Has the assignment closed for submissions? Are the students' submissions still in "Draft" state? The solutions I found: The teacher needs to enable "Send for marking" button in the assignment. Then students must click "send for marking" to finalise their drafts. OR The teacher needs to enable "Due date" and "Prevent late submissions" Without these options enabled, the submissions sit forever in a draft state and cannot be downloaded in bulk. The cause of this is: "If assignment is open and submission is not finalized then don't add it to zip.", from MDL-30121 This is not made clear in the interface, and may count as a bug in the assignment module.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle assignment with Turnitin plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Update on my status: I have managed to solve the SSL problem after finding this in a moodle forum discussion To work around this: You need to be running minimum PHP 5.3.7 ( http://uk3.php.net/manual/en/curl.configuration.php ) Download a certificate bundle from somewhere and save to somewhere on the server that the webserver will be able to access. I saved mine into the Moodle installation directory but maybe the moodledata folder might eb a better location. I used the bundle provided at http://curl.haxx.se/docs/caextract.html Create a new entry in your php.ini file called curl.cainfo and set its value to the path of your downloaded certificate bundle. eg curl.cainfo = D:\iiswebsites\moodle\cacert.pem Create a reminder for yourself to update the certificate bundle on a semi-regular basis as this config will stop working if some of the CA certificates in the bundle expire or new CA certs are issues and you don't have them in the bundle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle assignment with Turnitin plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: The Turnitin API has a hissy fit if you try to create an assignment with a start date in the past - so the integration code won't allow creation with a date in the past. AFAIK they are improving this with their new api so the new version of the plugin that Turnitin are developing may not have this issue. The due date is usually a bit more manageable - the code checks to make sure the date is greater than the time the assignment was created via cron + 10min and if not extends the due date to 1yr from now (probably a bigger extension than is needed!) If you had set a later due date by a couple of hours or days it would probably have used that date. the code that manages dates is slightly better in the latest code in my git repo compared to the zip that is available in the plugins db.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle assignment with Turnitin plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: when a student uploads a file it triggers an event. when cron runs it sees that event and if turnitin is enabled for that assignment it will add a record to the plagiarism_turnitin_files table for that file and will submit the file to turnitin. If you have previously installed another plagiarism plugin like crot/urkund/compilatio/moss that go into the /plagiarism directory but you have deleted the files there may be an event handler in your database that is holding up the event from being handled by Turnitin. The handlers in the table look for the code that created the handler (eg crot/urkund/compilatio) and if it can't find the code it causes that event type to "hang" completely in your database. the fix is either to restore the deleted files in which case it will see that the assignment hasn't been configured to use that plugin and clear or you will need to manually remove the invalid handlers from the handlers table. The latest turnitin code will show an error on the turnitin settings page if there are any invalid handlers in the db. IF the students submitted the files before you enabled turnitin inside the assignment - those files will not be sent to Turnitin - only files uploaded after turnitin was enabled in the assignment will be sent.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can teacher publish the students' assignment after grade?
ResponsesInList.Text: You can try the database activity with a simple add entry form consisting of a file upload field. The database should be set to require approval. As long as an entry is not approved only the author (and the teacher) can see it. Then if the teacher wants to publish an entry he/she can approve the entry and everyone will be able to see it. The main drawback of this activity for this purpose is the settings for due date (availability) which don't work and even if they worked they are too simplified (for some reason graded activities do not share common availability settings). So the teacher will have to work around that. hth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can teacher publish the students' assignment after grade?
ResponsesInList.Text: How about simply using a Forum? Teacher creates a Forum called 'Shared example assignments' or something similar and then uploads example files as attachments to posts that she wants to share with the class. If you make the Forum type 'Single simple discussion' then students can respond to each Assignment you upload. Hope this helps. mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can teacher publish the students' assignment after grade?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suggestions for assignment method
ResponsesInList.Text: You could probably use something like the Database module for this. The module allows you to create a form with various field types. So you could design the form a rubric with a menu field for each competency with options 1-5 for the scale. Then, in each session the associate creates an entry for each attending student and fill out the rubric. These records can then be reviewed by their designated students and associates. You can also add to each record comments and rating that can go to the gradebook if needed. If something like that could work for you, you should probably use the Dataform instead of the Database as the Dataform offers many more options for adding and browsing these records. hth

ResponsesInList.Text:
In the assignment lib.php in v.1.9 I placed it in the function below. (between the //// megill tags).  I haven't installed it in v.2.0 but figure it will be the same or simiar: /** * Returns a link with info about the state of the assignment submissions * * This is used by view_header to put this link at the top right of the page. * For teachers it gives the number of submitted assignments with a link * For students it gives the time of their submission. * This will be suitable for most assignment types. * @param bool $allgroup print all groups info if user can access all groups, suitable for index.php * @return string */ function submittedlink($allgroups=false) { global $USER; $submitted = ''; $ context = get_context_instance(CONTEXT_MODULE,$this->cm->id); if (has_capability('mod/assignment:grade', $context)) { if ($allgroups and has_capability('moodle/site:accessallgroups', $context)) { $group = 0; } else { $group = groups_get_activity_group($this->cm); }                                                       //echo "group-> $group"; if ($count = $this->count_real_submissions($group)) { //// megill $ungraded = $this->count_real_ungraded_submissions($group); $submitted = ''. get_string('viewsubmissions', 'assignment', $count).'
('.get_string('submissionsnotgraded', 'music', $ungraded).')'; //// end megill } else { $submitted = ''. get_string('noattempts', 'assignment').''; } } else { if (!empty($USER->id)) { if ($submission = $this->get_submission($USER->id)) { if ($submission->timemodified) { if ($submission->timemodified <= $this->assignment->timedue || empty($this->assignment->timedue)) { $submitted = ''.userdate($submission->timemodified).''; } else { $submitted = ''.userdate($submission->timemodified).''; } } } } } return $submitted; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to hide list of assignments in Course Overview block
ResponsesInList.Text: A little bit of further research at our end suggests that the behaviour of the course overview block is as follows: Assignments are removed from this block only when there is no due date, regardless of whether the assignment is complete or not. Hence, any assignment - completed or not - with no due date set/enabled will not appear in the course overview block. However, any assignment - completed or not - with a due date set/enabled remains listed. It would seem therefore that the logic in the block_course_overview.php module is not correct.  Or maybe this is be design...? James.

ResponsesInList.Title: Resetting Turnitin - Moodle direct
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, A quick question because I can't see it in any of the Turnitin documentation. There are 3 options in the reset area for Turnitin. The last is quite obvious (leave alone), but can anyone explain what each of the first 2 do? The first one (Copy) says Create Duplicates, New Turnitin. I assume this creates a new instance of the assignment and has no previous assignments set against it. The second one (Replace) says Replace Assignment Parts, Reuse Turnitin Class. What parts does it mean? Does this mean that last years students/class will still be associated with the assignment? What I want to do, is removed last years assignments and still keep the same assignment setup to go for this year from scratch. Is that possible or do I have to create a duplicate? Thanks in advance

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resetting Turnitin - Moodle direct
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi William, Those 2 options: (Copy) says Create Duplicates, New Turnitin.... This one looks at the current course to find which Turntin class it links to and creates a new class in Turnitin to link to, then for each Moodle Direct activity, creates a new version of each Turnitin assignment in the newly created class with the exact same assignment options. (This is generally the one most folk will choose). It is not destructive and will keep copies of the previous class and assignments containing submissions in Turnitin but will create new activities linked to brand new empty replicas of the Turnitin assignments (Replace) Replace Assignment Parts, Reuse Turnitin Class This one is similar to the above but instead of creating a brand new class it will reuse the previously linked class and create brand new replicas of the assignments in it rather than use a new class. Downside to this method is you keep the previous Turnitin cohort of students. This option is pretty specific to certain use cases and is generally not used very often. Option 3 as you say, leaves the class and assignment linkage the same and basically does nothing to the Moodle Direct activities. Hope that helps. Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resetting Turnitin - Moodle direct
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Paul. I think I'll go with Option 1.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'Grade' settings
ResponsesInList.Text: Christina, If I understand you correctly, you have everything in place so that when you create an assignment, your scale is there but you are wanting to save the time and trouble of changing from the default scale of 100, over to your Solent scale, not to mention, preventing the possibility of forgetting to change to the Solent scale. If this is correct, I can think of two ways of doing it. One is to get a programmer to go in and modify/patch Moodle core code to change the grade scale to show your new scale by default. If you do so, then each time you upgrade Moodle you would need to re-patch it. The second and much easier one to me, is that if you have one assignment set up to do what you want, make it a template and hide it from students by closing its eye. Have one copy available for each teacher in their course. Teach the teacher to duplicate the template when they need to create a new assignment with the Solent scale. Then edit the new copy to set its name and due dates and turn its eye back on so students can see it. I give very similar, spur-of-the-moment online writing assignments throughout the year with the same scoring rubric and the second way is how I do it. Makes it very easy and quick to create a new assignment while stuents are waiting to get started. In fact while testing to make sure the duplicated course was an exact duplicate in M2.3.1 like it was in M1.9.x, I made five duplicates with new names and dates in less than a minute. HTH, AL

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'Grade' settings
ResponsesInList.Text: This is actually quite simple given a few factors I'd want to ascertain first: Is this a systemwide change whereby everyone will be happy that the default grade for assignments has been changed from 100 to your scale? Do you have someone reasonably capable of editing one line of code in Moodle to initiate this change you desire? Is the scale public or published (can't recall which terminology is used but it must be available to all courses). If the answers to all questions are yes then you can certainly accomplish this by editing the line in MOODLEROOT/course/moodleform_mod.php, function standard_grading_coursemodule_elements() that reads as follows: $mform->setDefault( 'grade' , 100 ); (my system around line 711) You would replace the value, '100' wiith the scaleid associated with your Solent scale.  You can detemine the scaleid for your Solent scale by going into Settings->Grades->Scales from any course and clicking to edit the Solent scale.  Your url will now contain a parameter of 'id=<SOLENT SCALE ID>.  IMPORTANT HERE: the value you replace 100 with must be this id except it must be negative, i.e. if I saw: MOODLEROOT/grade/edit/scale/edit.php?courseid=82&id=112 on my url address line I would replace the '100' in moodleform_mod.php with '-112'. A caveat mentioned by one of the earlier posters is the need to change this each time.  That's true,  though it doesn't represent much of an effort, the base assignment code hasn't changed much (there's been a plan in the works to bring the grading over into the core grading libraries for about five years) and Moodle is better when it works like you need it to so I strongly advocate getting to know your system and jumping in with both feet.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment:- Import grades bug?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, The normal workflow for grades is that the grade is set in the activity which pushes it into the gradebook. The grades in the gradebook can then be edited for example to scale the marks - in this case the student will see the grade that is assigned in the gradebook and the overridden flag will be set to 1. If you edit a grade in the gradebook and remove the overridden flag - normally the gradebook will reset the grade to whatever it is in the activity (your solution bypasses this step). In your example I think that it would be a bit confusing for staff because - a grade would be assigned in the gradebook - but if the teacher edited that grade in the assignment - the default would not be the current grade (it would be 0) - so if they just hit edit and save without changing anything - the student grade would be reset to 0 (in the assignment and the gradebook). Regards, Damyon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Deleting Assignment Submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: This is not perfect but worked for me to "delete" a student's uploaded file.  The student can edit the file here to make changes and resubmit. Click on this and you will have the following options: Download Rename Move Delete Press delete. You will get a warning message and press Yes.  File has been deleted. This is where I get stuck as it won't let you get out of this area as there must be a file there - if you press cancel the file comes back but you/student can upload a new file. ( I'll check my settings as I probably haven't got something set in the course settings to allow this - reading the assignment info says there is a setting to allow the student to delete submissions). So the student must have a replacement file to upload at this stage.  Press save changes. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to add new functionality to the home page ???
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Pavel, In Moodle it is very easy for a user to be both a student and a teacher on different courses as these roles can be applied on a course by course basis rather than for the entire site. However, once a user is a teacher on a particular course they will have the rights of a teacher and see all the teacher resources/options even if they are also a student - if they want to be able to see what a student sees there is a 'Switch Role to...' option In terms of different functionality, well it depends exactly what you want. You can set permissions for roles to say what you want teachers/students to be able to do and, certainly in Moodle2, you have the ability to assign roles for just about every resource/activity/block etc so that they only appear to users with the roles that are allowed to see that. HTH Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A very basic question on assignments and course backups
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm beginning to think, Nick, that an unstated aspect of your question is the wish for something like a portfolio. So, maybe the question is "For whom are you saving the assignments?" Here's an idea for groups. In 2012, you create a group called YR10-12. When the next year starts, you add the members of YR10-12 to a group called YR11-13, but don't remove them from YR10-12. Inside one course, a student's assignments belong to the student regardless of groups. They don't disappear, though it might be possible (I've never tried this) to make assignments inaccessible by removing them from the group. In any event, by using two groups, you prevent yr10 from seeing yr 11 assignments before they are in yr11.

There is a neat procedure for this: -          Script “mdl_assignment_submissions” table as “create to” in SQL Server Management Studio, -          Change the name of the table (in script), change data type to NVarchar(max) where appropriate, -          Run script (this will create new table), -          Copy the content of “mdl_assignment_submissions” to your new table (remember to convert ntext fields!), -          Rename table “mdl_assignment_submissions” to something else, -          Rename your newly created table to “mdl_assignment_submissions”. It worked for me. Hope moodle.org will soon be equipped with SQL Server testing environment ;) Thanks again! Regards, Lukasz  Cz.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: huge problem with Assignment module on Moodle 2.2.2+ (Build: 20120315) - Error reading from database
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Lucasz; I imagine you thought you had to do your "neat procedure" because you tried to use the designer to change the data type and it would not let  you. However, you probably don't need to do what you did.  I believe you *can* indeed change the data type in situ (without renaming the table.  You just need to use SQL rather than the Designer, like this: alter table mdl_assignment_submissions alter column data2 nvarchar ( max ) ... I am letting you know this in case you have this problem with other ntext columns; I hope it works for you.  If not, what version of SQL Server are you working in? One reason *not* to do the rename is that there can be problems with SQL Server metadata after objects are re-named.  It is not very usual, and it may be fixed for all objects by now, but I don't like to do it. Regarding this: >>Hope moodle.org will soon be equipped with SQL Server testing environment ;) I don't think that moodle.org itself is the problem. Various individual developers, cooperating in moodle development, aren't always careful to test in a SQL Server environment and they don't apologize for this.  I am not even sure that they should. They do the best they can; using SQL Server is a "minority" platform, and we have to cooperate by finding the problems. The most we can hope for is that, when we find the problems, they don't say it's not important to fix because it's "only" SQL Server. So I suggest you log a bug, based on what you saw, and ask for a fix.  Report the number of the bug back in this thread so that people with similar environments can find it and vote for it.  That's how things get done. OK?  You will find the bug tracker on the menu of this site, under Development, http://tracker.moodle.org/secure/Dashboard.jspa Here is an example of a bug regarding SQL Server, which I reported -- and which you could vote for -- I hope you do! http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-29873 Regards, >L<

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: huge problem with Assignment module on Moodle 2.2.2+ (Build: 20120315) - Error reading from database
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Trevor.  My problem is that the tracker fixes the one case whereas the obsolete ntext data fields are pervasive in Moodle (in fact, it seems as though every time my users ask me to install a new module, there are new ones). In a test environment, I've taken the plunge and done something to convert all of them at once, in two easy steps, in SQL Mgmt Studio, as follows: 1.  with your context set to your moodle db, run the following statement, which scripts out the necessary lines (and doesn't actually affect anything) select distinct object_name ( object_id ) as tablename , columns . name as columnname , 'alter table [' + object_name ( object_id ) + '] alter column [' + columns . name + '] nvarchar(max); ' as statement from sys . columns join sys . types on columns . system_type_id = types . system_type_id and types . name = 'ntext' order by 1 -- the order by clause is just to make it easy to read, -- as are the "tablename" and "columnname" columns. -- You'll use the "statement" column next. 2. Copy the  "statement" column contents into a new query window,  where it will be a series of executable lines like this: alter table [mdl_upgrade_log] alter column [backtrace] nvarchar ( max ); alter table [mdl_upgrade_log] alter column [details] nvarchar ( max ); -- etc... in my installation about 300 lines. and execute it.  Afterwards, if you run step #1 again, you will see there are no ntext columns left. So far, I've experienced no ill effects from the mass conversion and don't expect to. I'm going to give it a little more time (this test installation is in active use) and then I will probably run it in production. I do expect to have to run the same procedure again, obviously for many fewer columns, every time I install new features, to take care of any ntext columns that have been added. HTH somebody, >L<

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: huge problem with Assignment module on Moodle 2.2.2+ (Build: 20120315) - Error reading from database
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for the info and scripts above Lisa. I didn't realise this problem was back until today (had heaps of issues with 1.9+).  Under 1.9 I had modified /lib/adodb/drivers/adodb-mssql.inc.php /lib/xmldb/classes/generators/mssql.class.php to use nvarchar(max) instead of ntext. I also used a similar script to yours above to loop through the database and convert all problem fields over to nvarchar(max) (don't recall if I wrote this or got it from someone else): select o.name as table_name, c.name as column_name, ( 'alter table [' + o.name + '] ' + 'alter column [' + c.name +'] ' + case when c.system_type_id = TYPE_ID('text') then 'varchar(max)' else 'nvarchar(max)' end + ' ' + case when c.is_nullable = 1 then 'null' else 'not null' end + ';' + char(10) + 'update [' + o.name + '] set [' + c.name + '] = [' + c.name + '];' + char(10) +char(13) ) [sql] into #tmp from sys.columns c left join sys.objects o on (c.object_id = o.object_id) where o.type = 'U' and o.is_ms_shipped = 0 and c.system_type_id = TYPE_ID('ntext') or c.system_type_id = TYPE_ID('text') while exists(select null from #tmp) begin set nocount on declare @sql nvarchar(max) select top 1 @sql = [sql] from #tmp set nocount off exec sp_executesql @sql set nocount on delete from #tmp where [sql] = @sql end drop table #tmp Cheers Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: huge problem with Assignment module on Moodle 2.2.2+ (Build: 20120315) - Error reading from database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, The technique you're using there is good for many things -- in fact I am using it extensively right now to script collation changes etc while I move a bunch of databases from one server to another -- but I don't use it for changing datatypes in externally-specified tables, such as Moodle's.  I want a record of every column I've changed, in case I have some other issues later. With my simple two-step method, I can save off the script I've created and archive it, and I do this every time I have to run it again after adding a module. You can go ahead and do it in one step with a loop, sure, but in the future I'd suggest you add one of the following: * -- put a PRINT statement in your loop and save off the messages; or * -- select * from #tmp and save/archive that result before you drop table #tmp. Make sense? >>Under 1.9 I had modified /lib/adodb/drivers/adodb-ms sql .inc.php /lib/xmldb/classes/generators/mssql.class.php to use nvarchar(max) instead of ntext. Thanks for this.  I'm basically a database person, but I will try to get up the nerve to do this too <g>.  I assume it's possible to do it in 2.x too. Good luck! >L<

ResponsesInList.Title: Assign a student to a course
ResponsesInList.Text: We have Moodle 1.9.9+ Build 20100901. We have a dozen courses. When we set a new user with "student" designation, it appears Moodle default setting is that this user can see all courses in the system. We do not wish Moodle to function that way. In simple non-geek language, how do we define that a one student can only access a one course, or certain courses that we wish the student to access - but not all of them ? So in layman's language ... if we wish to have Student A to access only Course Number 1 (but not all 12 of them) - then how do we do that trick ? And once he has completed Course 1 ; then how do we assign him to say Course Number 5 Regards Allen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign a student to a course
ResponsesInList.Text: To assign a student to just one course you need either to go into that course and then in the administration block click "assign roles"and choose "student" and manually move him in. To stop him accessing any other course you need to put enrolment keys on the other courses - you can do this via the course settings from the admininstration block again. Alternatively, once you have put enrolment keys on all your courses you can TELL the student what the enrolment key is for his course and he can enrol himself. You could do this for once he has completed course number 1 -you could give him the key for course number 5 for instance. The other way if you have a lot of students is you can enrol them straight into the course you want them in via csv file -Take a look here http://docs.moodle.org/19/en/Upload_users

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assign a student to a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Just following Mary to make sure you did not designate the new user with the system-wide role of "student." That's the usual situation in which a student can "see" all courses. Do you mean the student can enter all the courses without being enrolled? If so, then you have a site-wide role. If you do not have the user in a site-wide role, then once you enroll the student in a course, the student should not be able to see all the other courses. The student will still be able to click the all courses button on the site's front page , but, assuming you are not using enrollment-keyless self-enrollment, not be able to enter those classrooms.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No users were found with permissions to submit this assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle 2.2 and hit this same problem while trying to grade an offline assignment. But I have found both the problem and the solution: All assignments have some "Optional settings" like: the number of submissions shown per page or the options to show all submissions, only submitted assignments, or only already graded assignments. I thought these settings to be local to each assignment, but they are global. I selected "Show: Submitted" in an "Advanced uploading of files" kind of assignment and forgot about it. Obviously, "Offline activities " ever have submitted assigments, so they show the (quite criptic) "No users were found with permissions to submit this assignment" message, without (BIG BUG!!) the corresponding "Optional Settings" box to change them. Solution to the problem: open any assignment with submitted works, go to grading, and change the optional setting to "Show: All". Et voilà!

ResponsesInList.Title: Advantage of using assignment upload instead of emailing a document
ResponsesInList.Text: What is the advantage for a teacher in using the ' upload a file' or the 'advanced uploading of files' assignment module to collect a paper from a student versus just having them email the assignment? I know a teacher that has had them email assignments and has had no trouble with that method, and is a little leery of trying to use Moodle to do the same job. I've already mentioned to this person that the student will have definite confirmation that the document did indeed get uploaded and that there will be a time-stamp, but they say the emails give time stamps as well. Any other advantages you can think of? Thank you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advantage of using assignment upload instead of emailing a document
ResponsesInList.Text: Off the top of my head: sure, the emails give timestamps, but the teacher has to figure out some custom way of extracting that information from the email repository to visually identify who in the class has submitted an assignment, who has not.  This identification and other aspects of class management should be a lot easier within Moodle. The upload activity can be immediately connected to a mark, and the mark can be seen in the context of all marks, like any other Moodle activity.  There's some manual housekeeping involved if the submission is managed in email instead. The time period during which the activity is open for student submissions can be controlled according to the needs of the curriculum. A teacher can do the same thing manually in email, sure, but (a) it's more trouble and (b) the time period isn't published/visible to all students within the course context. All the points I've raised (and more that others who are more knowledgeable Moodle users could raise, and I hope will raise, in this thread) *can* be answered by doing some sort of custom integration between an email repository or even your teacher's email client (if absolutely necessary) and Moodle or whatever other application handles your gradebook, courseware, etc.  But it's unnecessarily painful. Please note: I'm not an educator.  I'm an integration specialist (officially a DBA).  That's why I'm weighing in on this thread. Even though I know it's possible to connect all the dots if needed, I am *still* saying: it's not a great idea to require integration custom work when you can get this type of functionality with no work at all. HTH , >L<

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advantage of using assignment upload instead of emailing a document
ResponsesInList.Text: From my perspective as a teacher, the "mark can be seen in context with all the other marks" aspect that Lisa names has been one of the most valuable reasons I would choose using the assignment module over email.  It is a super huge timesaver for me to be able to copy/paste some of the same pointers to students in their feedback.  This also gives me a place to see patterns of feedback that might be better addressed in a large group forum post if I find many are making the same types of errors. Finally, the assignment module also nicely locates all of your directions and feedback in one place for the student who might not be as organized as the teacher who is able to organize her/his email in a way that easily manages assignment intake. There are more reasons, but these come to mind first.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advantage of using assignment upload instead of emailing a document
ResponsesInList.Text: I run an entirely online writing program for gifted kids. We use Moodle and email as two different formats of the same courses. The virtue of Moodle is that assignments don't go astray, land in the spam bucket, or just vaporize. Recordkeeping is immensely easier. The gradebook can be as simple or complicated as you wish. We use a simple system of [no grade] = not yet turned in, 0 = unacceptable or late, 1 = worked turned in & critique has been posted. Messaging keeps a record of anything everyone says. Emails go out, but the record remains in the classroom. So, when Johnny makes a promise, it's there for everyone to see. If you need to substitute or replace an instructor, all that has happened is there to be seen. In a purely email course, you would have to find and forward immense numbers of messages. With advanced uploading, any changed or additional files are all in one place. With email only, you may start working on an assignment only to discover 40 emails down that there's another version, or that a missing piece has been sent separately. We find Moodle's main classroom page a blessing. Students start at the top and "fall" down the page till the course ends. We rarely get "what's my assignment? where do I find it?" If you need to make changes to an assignment, you don't have to rely on an email to all your students actually arriving in all your students' in boxes. You make the change in one place where it can't be lost or vaporized. So, why does my program have both an email and a Moodle format for one course? Because the email format doesn't use forums for workshops. Web-based work takes more time because of the social aspect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I'd appreciate feedback on our proposed method of incorporating the Lightwork rubrics into Moodle and the new Moodle 2.3 assignment module. See also docs.moodle.org/dev/Lightwork. Moodle currently supports one type of rubric called "rubric" which is defined in mdl_grading_definitions and its associated grading form tables. Lightwork supports 2 rubric types, a rubric that is equivalent to the Moodle rubric and a rubric without explicit quality levels that allows the teacher to specify a mark out of a maximum allowed for each criterion. I'll call these rubrics Rubric type 1 and Rubric type 2 respectively. The current Moodle rubric will be used in Lightwork as the type 1 rubric which means it will be possible to define it, edit it and grade with it either through the Moodle interface or in Lightwork. We propose creating a new grading definition for Lightwork's type 2 rubric. This means that there will be an additional grading method that can be chosen in the grading method dropdown in the assignment editing page. Currently, "Rubric" is the only rubric option available. Teachers will now have an additional rubric definition to choose from, the type 2 rubric. This rubric definition provides a more traditional rubric which in Lightwork we call an "analytical rubric". However, subsequent research has revealed this name to be misleading and we would need to come up with different terminology to define the 2 rubric types in Moodle. The Lightwork rubrics have additional features that are not currently supported in the Moodle rubric such as the ability to define a bank of "frequently used comments" that can be subsequently selected from and added by the teacher as feedback in the rubric instance displayed to the user. We'd like to extend Moodle's functionality to provide this feature.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Paul, I think this sounds like a pretty reasonable approach. I am not good with naming things though so I can't help much there

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Paul, Your proposal sounds like a good one. My understanding of the advanced grading methods in Moodle 2.2 is that by marking a particuar performance standard against a criteria a marker can apply a set point value (a true rubric). Whereas what some markers are asking me for may be more appropriately described as a 'marking guide'. They wish to indicate where a piece of work sits in terms of the performance standard, but then have the flexibility to determine the point value that is applied either; within a particular range according to the performance standard selected, against each criteria seperately with no reference programatically to the performance standard selected, or to the marking guide as a whole. I think that sounds like what you have described as the analytic rubric? I would be supportive of extending the functionality of the Advanced Grading Method in Moodle to incoproate these features. I am not able to comment about whether this could be done for 2.3 given that the Advanced Grading Method is a sepereate Moodle module to the Assignment module and therefore not included in the re-factor for 2.3. A question for Moodle HQ perhaps?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Grette, Yes, what you are describing and calling a 'marking guide' is the equivalent to the new grading definition that we propose to add. We are submitting this feature as part of the changes that are required to incorporate Lightwork into Moodle 2.3 as described at docs.moodle.org/dev/Lightwork.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Grette, I like your suggestion of 'marking guide'! What you describe is what we are doing in our Lightwork 'analytic rubric' (a name, as Paul says, we are not quite happy with). Thanks, Eva

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal for incorporating Lightwork rubrics into Moodle 2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: The first version of the marking guide is now available. It allows definition of a marking guide and grading using the marking guide (there is no student interface yet for seeing the detailed marking comments and marks). We have prepared a testing plan, see http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Lightwork#Marking_guide_-_Screenshot_and_Testing . You can either test within our sample Moodle installation (links and usercodes are provided in the testing plan) or within you own environments. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Export to PDF
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the previous poster had a good idea, about using GoogleDocs for the items that you want to handle this way. They can "Download as PDF", etc. However, if you don't like that... When a student wants to download or save "any work produced in Moodle", I'm going to start by assuming you mean anything produced by that student as text. When the student does this, they're editing/typing into a little text widget, right? The text editor you see in Moodle is a plugin, configurable, so this behavior is different in different installations, but it's going to behave pretty much the same way throughout your site. Taking my own installation as an example: my editors are TinyMCE HTML editor and the plain text editor.  Even when editing rich HTML, I can select within the editing area, copy and paste to a text file; I will illustrate with an attached screen shot.  As you'll see, when I paste into the text file, I get readable plain text, not HTML markup.  Obviously, from the plain text editor, it shouldn't be *more* difficult. So, all they have to do is have the ability to open a text file and they can have a saved file record of what they've done.  Would this suit you? As another idea, most browsers have some idea of "Save Page As" and will save the entire page down to an HTML file, which would include the student's input on this page.  That would include any rich formatting, if you were interested in doing so, and still would not require a word processor -- which I gather is something you are trying to avoid? Caveats: * -- these suggestions would probably be more difficult on a mobile device, but so would the student's ability to create long text input (or manipulate *any* files) * -- you haven't really specified what type of assignments or activities you are talking about, so these ideas might not work 100% for "any work". >L<

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Export to PDF
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ralph, I understand what you are saying about cut/paste.  OTOH I don't know any other sequence of actions - in any environment or application - that would be simpler for them. Whether it's "export to PDF" or "save as PDF", or "press that button", regardless of the actual set of actions they take to get there, I believe that "save in a pdf an assignment (or any text entered online) for later print out. " is going to be problemmatic for them: where did they put the file that they saved? Are you envisioning this file going into the moodle repository somewhere, so that it's available on-line during the in-person seminar?  If that's the case, then why not just forget the whole problem and review the document in-situ (or have the person holding the seminar do it that way)? IOW, why the need for a separate PDF file at all? Sorry if these thoughts don't seem germane.  I'm willing to take your assessment of your users' capabilities at face value, but then I think you should re-think the whole workflow, not just this one action, if possible. From this statement, I am not sure if I have confused you about something else: >> I going to look into TinyMCE HTML plugins.  There might be something we can use. I think you mean to say "I am going to look into editor plugins", to see if one behaves the way you want.  I really doubt it, FWIW.  And here: >>I am suprised no one has thought about this yet as a Moodle plug in. Well, if it went after the contents of an editor window, it wouldn't be a Moodle plug in, that's for sure.  Tiny MCE, and the other editor plugins, aren't specific to Moodle.  They're freestanding. The reason I think there isn't one that will do what you want is that it would have to interact with its environment in a way that would hard to write cross platform and cross browser. I do think there is a possible other solution to your problem, however; why not just remove the requirement from the student, extract the data directly from the database , and make it available from there during the in-person seminar?  To tell you how this might be done, I have to know more about that full workflow, but it might be better.   Tell me who needs the PDF, who does the printing out, and where and when, etc, what do you envision? >L< PS. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add Turn It In Basic or Direct
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd reccomend you avoid the Turnitin Basic plugin if you can - it has a few issues that cause problems. The Turnitin basic plugin  stores all assignments/files externally on Turnitin.coms servers - you don't get a local copy of the file, and it doesn't provide access to the full range of Turnitin services. It also has a few bugs/design flaws that can make it difficult to support long term. If given the choice - Turnitin support will usually reccommend Turnitin Direct over Turnitin Basic too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing assignment types ("Upload a single file" => "Advanced uploading of files")
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everybody, I've found that you can easily update the assignments by running this SQL command. Suppose you have a course whose url is: http://myschool.edu/course/view.php?id=223 Then the course ID is 223. You can update all of the assignments with this SQL command: UPDATE `mdl_assignment` SET `assignmenttype` = 'upload', `var1` = '3' WHERE `course` = 223 AND `assignmenttype` = 'uploadsingle'; That will give the maximum of 3 uploads per assignment. To change that, change the value of `var1` in that command. Because we often have this problem, I'm eventually going to write a script that you can put into your Administrative Menu in Moodle to change them and select specific assignments and a nicer way of selecting courses. We're just in a massive hurry to fix all of our courses before the spring semester starts in 8 days, and I figured I'd post that mySQL command to give some of you a quick start. I'll update you all once the semester begins and my workload dies down to put something together.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Patch for Downloading assignment files as one Zip file.
ResponsesInList.Text: you may also need to alter the function get_submissions in your moodle install \moodle\mod\assignment\lib.php to this: function get_submissions($sort='', $dir='DESC') { /// Return all assignment submissions by ENROLLED students (even empty) global $CFG; if ($sort == "lastname" or $sort == "firstname") { $sort = "u.$sort $dir"; } else if (empty($sort)) { $sort = "a.timemodified DESC"; } else { $sort = "a.$sort $dir"; } $select = "s.course = '".$this->assignment->course."' AND"; $site = get_site(); if ($this->assignment->course == $site->id) { $select = ''; } return get_records_ sql ("SELECT a.* FROM {$CFG->prefix}assignment_submissions a, {$CFG->prefix}user_students s, {$CFG->prefix}user u, {$CFG->prefix}user_teachers t WHERE (a.userid = s.userid OR a.userid = t.userid) AND u.id = a.userid AND $select a.assignment = '".$this->assignment->id."' ORDER BY $sort"); } NOTE: - this will then include all teachers responses in the download as well as the students. Dan

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Julian- Could I get you to post a diff version? What you do is diff -c old/assignment new/assignment > assignment-1zip.diff where old is the directory with the original version and new is the patched version. This will create a context diff file. What I want to do is use the unix patch utility to apply this "patch". See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patch_(Unix ) for background. What patch does is to look at the output of diff and apply this as a "difference". This is a long time technique in the unix community to send patches in discussion forums (originally in network news). As long as your original files are in sync, using diffs works fine. The advantage of this approach is easier management of patches using diff. For example, you can create a "backup" of the original with the patch -b option. This will work with a whole directory tree where multiple files are being changed. Where I'm going with this is the patch could be listed in the Moodle Modules and plugins. I'm working in 1.8.1 (on about May 5th), which is what you said you have. I tried to create my own diff -c, but there were quite a few files that are missing.
