ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Patch for Downloading assignment files - by groups
ResponsesInList.Text: I've had a go at doing this because we are reducing the turnaround time for feedback and need to speed up the process of uploading marked scripts. I had to make some changes to your download code to achieve a directory structure that suited our needs. I have attached the patch and this is the help file explaining how it works: Bulk upload feedback In order to use this feature, you must first download all submissions using the button 'Bulk download all submissions'. The download will be a zip file which, when extracted, will be of the format: [course shortname]_[assignment name]_[assno] [lastname]_[firstname]_[userid] filename.ext [lastname]_[firstname]_[userid] filename.ext ... do_not_edit.txt eg: EDM116_PRD1_2009_10_Discuss_Life_42 Doughty_Amanda_1029 myassignment.docx Hughes_Mike_6057 myattempt.xls ... do_not_edit.txt You can edit the downloaded files or add extra files to the [lastname]_[firstname]_[userid] directories. But DO NOT rename or add directories. When all feedback is complete, zip up the [course shortname]_[assignment name]_[assno] folder and upload it using this form. The uploaded files will not overwrite the student files. They will be renamed and saved in a sub directory for each user (within the file structure courseid/moddata/assignment): assignmentid userid responses filename_feedback.ext filename.ext userid responses filename_feedback.ext extrafile_feedback.ext filename.ext ... eg: 42 1029 responses myassignment_feedback.docx myassignment.docx 6057 responses myattempt_feedback.xls notes_feedback.txt myattempt.xls ... IMPORTANT - Do not edit or delete the 'do_not_edit.txt' file. This is used to verify that you are uploading the correct zip file for the current course and assignment. Also note that each time you use this feature, any feedback files will be overwritten, unless you rename them. eg: 1. bulk download files as above example 2. edit myassignment.docx 3. bulk upload the files This results in a new file .../responses/myassignment_feedback.docx repeat steps 1 - 3 File .../responses/myassignment_feedback.docx is overwritten with the uploaded file. Now try 1. bulk download files as above 2. rename myassignment.docx as myassignment2.docx and edit it 3. bulk upload the files This results in a new file .../responses/myassignment2_feedback.docx, whilst .../responses/myassignment_feedback.docx is preserved. Once feedback is released. the student will see all files that reside in their corresponding responses directory. So in this example student abbf999 will see: myassignment_feedback.docx myassignment_feedback2.docx Is it any good?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems with TurnItIn Assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: This sounds like what happens when you delete a user in Moodle. The user's email is replaced in the database with some hash string it seems. The way to fix it would be to go into the Moodle Direct admin config pages and click the unlink users link. That list should contain the users that have emails that have become garbled. Unlink the users in that list that look like they have nonsense email addresses. The way Moodle Direct ties users in Moodle to their Turnitin counterparts is by email address initially and then by Turnitin user ID. When you unlink the users using the above mentioned tool it will delete the reference the plugin has that ties the user in Moodle by moodle user ID to the user in Turnitin by Turnitin User ID. When the users entry is removed from that 'unlink users' list the next time that user connects via the API to turnitin the entries are remade based on the email stored against that user in Moodle. The latest release of the plug in has more details in the unlink users form that older versions so if you find that the garbled email addresses aren't displayed in the list to unlink, upgrade to a newer version of the plug in.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't delete turnitin assignments from Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: my guess is that you're using the old Turnitin Basic assignment type. That plugin had some bugs with the early release that made it hard to delete the assignments - you will need to get the latest version of the code (login to turnitin as admin to get it from the admin interface) and upgrade your site to use the latest code. Unfortunately that version of the plugin can also leave some assignments in a "broken" state - run this sql on your db(replacing mdl_ with whatever db prefix is being used): SELECT m.* FROM mdl_course_modules m WHERE m.module=1 AND id NOT IN(SELECT m.id FROM mdl_course_modules m, mdl_assignment a WHERE m.module=1 and a.id=m.instance); It should bring up a list of "broken" entries for Turnitin assignments in the course_modules table - check each one of these records and if it relates to a "broken" assignment - delete it from the db.(If it doesn't return any results - that's great!)

ResponsesInList.Title: "Multiplicator"? can any one explain this?
ResponsesInList.Text: Let me get you started and you can pick it up from here: In mathematical group theory , the Schur multiplier or Schur multiplicator is the second homology group H 2 ( G , Z ) of agroup G . It was introduced by Issai Schur ( 1904 ) in his work on projective representations . The Schur multiplier M( G ) of a finite group G is a finite abelian group whose exponent divides the order of G . If a Sylow p -subgroup of G is cyclic for some p , then order of M( G ) is not divisible by p . In particular, if all Sylow p -subgroups of G are cyclic, then M( G ) is trivial. For instance, the Schur multiplier of the nonabelian group of order 6 is the trivial group since every Sylow subgroup is cyclic. The Schur multiplier of the elementary abelian group of order 16 is an elementary abelian group of order 64, showing that the multiplier  can be strictly larger than the group itself. The Schur multiplier of the quaternion group is trivial, but the Schur multiplier of dihedral 2-groups has order 2. The Schur multipliers of the finite simple groups are given at the list of finite simple groups . The covering groups of the alternating and symmetric groups are of considerable recent interest. Schur's original motivation for studying the multiplier was to classify projective representations of a group, and the modern formulation of his definition is the second cohomology  group H 2 ( G , C × ). A projective representation is much like a group representation except that instead of a homomorphism into the general linear group GL( n , C ), one takes a homomorphism into the projective general linear group PGL( n , C ). In other words, a projective representation is a representation modulo the center . (-:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2 upload button for assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: My team has monkeyed with this one, too, and gotten quite frustrated over it. Gavin seems to have the problem licked, but I found his description a bit confusing and missed the point. Here is another -- maybe for some 'simpler' -- explanation: THE TRICK: Whoever wishes to be able to see the upload button must actually be enrolled in the course. (As administrators/managers/teachers initially populating the site with courses, Moodle 2.0 does not recognize us as being 'enrolled' in the courses we are setting up!) HOW TO: From anywhere in a course go to Settings>Course Administration>Users>Enrolled Users. Click on the "Enrol users" button. (Whoever chose that spelling?!) Use the search block to locate whomever (like your own admin name) and select the role from the dropdown. Click on Finish enrolling. Use the outlined plus sign to add more roles (I generallly assign administator both student and manager roles). Voila!! When you return to the course assignment you will now see the "Upload file" button, even if you "switch role to" -- as long as you are logged in as an enrollee and assume a role assigned for that course!

ResponsesInList.Title: Bulk download
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there any way to do a bulk download of the files the students submitted and after correcting them to do a bulk upload of the corrected files? Thanks, Moshe

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk download
ResponsesInList.Text: In your files there is a folder labeled mod data that has a subfolder labeled assignments.  Within that folder is a list of allthe assignements for the course but there are only identified by numbers so you will need tofind the number assigned for that particular assisgnement.  Once identified, open the folder and use select all button at bottom of page to select all the folderss (each one contains one student's submitted work).  Then in box for selected files choose create zip file.  Once the zip file is created you can download it to your desktop, unzip it (DO NOT CHANGE NAME OF ANYTHING).  Grade the extracted files, saving each without changing any names ( you will want to record the grades as you go-I use a spreadsheet with each student's name and id number).  Once you finish grading all, zip the graded files back and upload that zip file to the same folder you got original from and unzip it.  That should now make thestudents see your markup when they go back and click on the assignment.  You definitleyshould try these steps before doing a lot of grading.  Perhaps make a sample assignement and have one group of students submit their work and then go thru the described steps to make sure it works for you. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Keeping Versions? Advanced Uploading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Advanced uploading allows up to 20 files to be submitted by students. >Update assignment > Advanced uploading > Allow deleting Maximum number of uploaded files Allow notes Hide description before available date Email alerts to teachers Enable Send for marking The trick to not overwriting is to alter the file name. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Competent/Not yet Competent
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jon, From the sound of it, I assume you are talking about a grading system where if a student scores a certain amount of marks their results should show as Competent/Not yet Competent in a task. You can do this by going to Administration>Grades. Then Letters>Edit Let us say, you are using Grade(%) system. The defaults are: Grade Letter 1,2,3: A+, A, A-... Grade Boundary 1,2,3: 95%, 90%,..... You can write Competent inplace of letter A+ and choose what ever % you want from the drop down and the for rest of the boundaries write Not Yet Competent in Grade Letter field. Write a formula for caluclating the course total by going to Grader Report> Turn Editing on> Course Total. Once you set up your formula results will be displayed with the set Grade Letters both for the cumulative and individual tasks, in this case its either Competent/Not Yet Competent . Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assignment Module Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mahtab, There are a number of ways to do what you want to accomplish. My suggestions would include: Use an online text assignment type and set it up so that students can resubmit. In this case you just have them answer the same questions 3 times in 3 different paragraphs Use one of the upload a file assignment types and do the same thing allowing the students to answer the question 3 different times in different paragraphs and upload the new version of the file each time. Use a private wiki and have the students just edit a wiki page 3 times  covering the same question each time. The most complex of the options is to create a database activity with a separate field for each answer. Then students just go in at the beginning, middle and end of the course and type the appropriate answer in the corrrect field. There are other options as well but these to me are the four best ways to go about solving the problem. Because I like the database module so much and because of the ease of use once it is put together I would probably use a database activity. It also easily allows you the teacher to make comments as well. Good Luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enable Send for Marking - Can it be defaulted to no?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John This can be changed via the setup_elements function in mod/assignment/type/ upload /assignment.class.php find: $mform->addElement('select', 'var4', get_string('trackdrafts', 'assignment'), $ynoptions); $mform->addHelpButton('var4', 'trackdrafts', 'assignment'); $mform->setDefault('var4', 1); and change the '1' in the setDefault line to a '0', like this: $mform->addElement('select', 'var4', get_string('trackdrafts', 'assignment'), $ynoptions); $mform->addHelpButton('var4', 'trackdrafts', 'assignment'); $mform->setDefault('var4', 0) ; Do remember that this is altering the core code of Moodle so when you should keep track of this change and do it again after an upgrade I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Last Year's Assignments in This Year's Course - How to Fix It?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dhruva It sounds like you removed last year's students and just continued to use the same teaching space for this year - perhaps?  The other student's submissions are still in the Moodle database but the removed students just don't show in the gradebook or assignment submissions screen so you can't see them!  When this student was added again he shows in these areas along with all of his content. There are two options that I can see for you: You could use a new shell for each time the course is taught (we do this at out University).  You can use the Course Import feature to copy the relevant resources/ activities from the old course into the new shell - this copies the activities etc but no user data. Alternatively you could use the Reset Course feature which allows you to select which data you'd like removed.  I highly recommend you backup the course first before you do this - actually probably before you remove students next time so their data is included! ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Last Year's Assignments in This Year's Course - How to Fix It?
ResponsesInList.Text: Our procedure is to make a "template" course with the forum introductions, etc. and to backup with no user data, then restore each term, which gives a new course each term. If your forums also have actual discussion threads already started (a prompt of some sort) by a person, your template is backed up and restored with user data included. To make a template now that you've begun, reset the course, which wipes almost everything, then drag & drop or copy & paste your forum material into the template.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Convert single file upload to Adanced file upload (easily)
ResponsesInList.Text: Brian I've found a way that involves modifying the database entry for the assignment. In the table mdl_assignment, you need to find the row (use the description field contents to help) then edit the assignmenttype field value to become "uploadsingle" to "upload" - find a techy or database type if you need help accessing your database that underpins moodle. To show ALL assignments id, description and type fields... SELECT id,assignmenttype,description FROM mdl_assignment; Find the value of id field where the description matches the one you want to change. When you know the id of the row to update (which I'm referring to as changeid here)... UPDATE mdl_assignment SET assignmenttype='upload' WHERE id=changeid Hope that helps, Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Timing assignment modules relative to student joining date
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 1.9.1 Hi, I am setting up a course which will be two months long with a multiple choice exam at the end.  The thing is that the course will be an ongoing course that students can sign up to on an ad-hoc basis. i.e. the start and finish time for the course is relative to the date that each student enrols. Can anyone point me towards some information about how I go about setting this up? (or let me know if it is not possible). Also, if it is possible then can I set up an assignment activity (i.e the multiple choice quiz) that is available, say, 1 week after the student enrols? Any help much appreciated! Thanks, Richard

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Timing assignment modules relative to student joining date
ResponsesInList.Text: Richard, I think that no-one has come back to you quickly on this because it is difficult to see how this can be done successfully. I'm only putting together an answer from the fragments I know about, so this is not definitive... Firstly you idea sounds great but flies in the face of way a standard assessment works; namely, a fixed start and end date - the same for everyone having the student role in that course. So it would require some rather special tweaks to make it work! Secondly, AFAIK if a student is off-rolled from a course their assignment can no longer be seen or marked [does anyone want to correct me there?] So you need a workaround... I can think of two possible solutions, neither of which is perfect as each has drawbacks. 1. You could have one assignment that is always open (so you disable the due date), though it is set so that the user gets one attempt only (I suggest that otherwise you end up with no idea of closure for the student). You write a little php code that is triggered as the user enrols for the first time... This script gives the user access to the assignment (or Quiz, or Questionnaire) course module, which access begins in one week's time (that's all available stuff, and is made possible by clicking into the module, into Assign Roles, Locally assigned roles, and noting down the contextid which you would need in order to generate a new entry into the table mdl_role_assignments where you want to set timestart to the UNIX equivalent of one week hence. Care needs to be taken with this (as obviously you are aware) because corrupting the table by writing rubbish into the database is not going to make moodle very stable! But it isn't rocket science. Now you could also put in a timeend for one week after that. But here's the rub. If the student disappears from the module (or course) after one week there is no opportunity to mark and record grades. Of course if the test is multiple choice and the correct answers therefore predetermined, then this won't matter so long as the grade is stashed away somewhere else automatically upon completion. Does the gradebook let us do this? I plead ignorance. 2. Rather messier (though the student sees exactly the same thing!) You create a course with 52 consecutive assignments (or quizzes or questionnaires) each with its own start/end date, and on enrolment to the course you give the user the student role in the next available assignment that is at least 7 days away. Now you need not fret about the start & end of the student enrolment, you use the start & end of that assignment instead. One really obvious snag is that as soon as the user has the student role in the course he sees all the assignments. But not if you have them all hidden except the current week. Or if you do another sneaky thing and create (you wont like this) 52 clone courses each with its own assignment start / end dates, and give the user the rights to the appropriate one in your script (as above). As you can see I'm suggesting that there must be some workaround (but the ephasis is on WORK, where the course creator is concerned). Perhaps someone has a MUCH better whizz than any of this... John

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Timing assignment modules relative to student joining date
ResponsesInList.Text: ...or, just maybe... 3. You clone the assessment type you want to use, and create an entirely new type which is identical in every respect, EXCEPT that it's start and end date are not taken from the usual settings alone, but by looking at the dates of the student's own enrolment. So that for the assessment to be open... now > student enrolment in this course context + 7 days AND now > assignment start date AND now < student enrolment in this course context + 14 days AND now < assignment end date (or end date is disabled) Now that would be VERY elegant! Regards, John

ResponsesInList.Title: Making Moodle Rubrics match Letter Grades???
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm trying to design an analytic grading rubric that will allow me to assess the criteria for PASSING projects. The problem I'm having is that if I have 4 levels (poor, developing, proficient, exemplary), moodle wants to translate these into 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. Well, only two of those are passing grades! Is there a way for me to offset the rubric, so the lowest score of it is translated into a 60% (or a D), instead of a 0? (I'd like for my 4 levels to correspond to an A, B, C, and D.) I also want to be able to weight the criteria differently, which I know I can do in some modules but not others, but this problem of starting the rubric at a D, instead of a 0, is driving me crazy! If you have any suggestions, I'd be so grateful. Thanks! Jesse ps I'm using 1.9. Our school will switch to 2.0 this summer.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making Moodle Rubrics match Letter Grades???
ResponsesInList.Text: This should be much easier in 2. In the meantime you can try using a gradebook grade item to shift the original assignment value to the desired range. So you create a grade item and sets its formula to take the assignment grade. Something like (consult the docs): =[ [assignment]] Then, if you set the minimum grade of the grade item to 60 and the maximum to 100, the scale values {1,2,3,4} should be shifted to {70,80,90,100}. If you also set the offset of the grade item to -10, the scales values should be shifted to {60,70,80,90} which I think is what you want to get. Then, for course grade calculation purposes you need to move the original item to some misc category which should be ignored by the course total and put the mirror grade item in its stead. Hope this works and works for you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making Moodle Rubrics match Letter Grades???
ResponsesInList.Text: I played around with this a little tonight and found that in a slightly round-about way it can be done fairly easily. However, I think if you make the scale Poor=60, developing=70, proficient=80, and exemplary=90, no one will ever make an "A" for the course (average of 90) unless every grade is exemplary. In your course click on Grades > Choose an action > Scales View > Add a new Scale. Give your new scale a name, then in the Scale box type: Poor, Developing, Proficient, Exemplary. Add a description explaining each element of your rubric then click Save Changes. In the course settings, make sure that under Grade Item Settings, you have Grade display type set to Real. Any of the selections that include percentage will show numbers that will be confusing to students. When creating your assignments be sure and select your new scale for the grade. This will give you a scale that is Poor, Developing, Proficient, Exemplary in the drop-down scoreless in the quickgrading box. They also show up when you use the normal grade window. In the formula you create for Course Total, add 5 to each assignment grade so it gets counted as 6, 7, 8, and 9. Average the assignments, then multiply by 10 and you get grades of 60, 70, 80, and 90 like you want. Example formula for three sample assignments: =average( sa1 +5, sa2 +5, sa3 +5)*10 In the Site administrations > Grades > Report Settings > User Report, you will probably want to turn off (remove the check mark) for Show Percentage. Other wise, students will probably be confused by percentage scores that will not look right to them. In other words, poor counts as 0%, developing counts as 33.3%, proficient counts as 66.7%, and exemplary counts as 100%. With Show Percentage turned off, when students look at their grades, they will see their course total above criteria words in the Grade and range columns. You as the teacher will be able to see a percentage number for the course total and the four criteria words in each assignment in the Grader Report. Hopefully, you understand this and I didn't leave anything out as I had a BSOD (blue screen of death) during the third rewrite– just as I was fixing to save. Windows 7 does not impress me so far.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, You have overridden those grades in the gradebook, therefore you can no longer update them from the assignment interface. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot grade some of the students submissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Three are 2 ways to override grades: - Enter the grades via the gradebook for an existing activity (e.g., for the assignment column). Instructor can go to the Grades > Grader report, click Turn Editing On and type grades in cells, then click Update at the bottom. - One can also Import the grades via the .csv file into the gradebook and map them to the existing assignment columns, therefore overriding the grades that way as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A way for a teacher to edit a student's file, and then upload it.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Michael.  We've been working on this issue, too.  Here is the text of some instructions I've shared with our faculty.  I have screen prints illustrating these instructions, which I can email to you if you'd like.  (The file is too big to attach here.)   Hope this helps a bit. ADD COMMENTS TO STUDENT’S ASSIGNMENT (via Moodle’s Advanced Uploading of Files type of Assignment) Using Microsoft Word, you can open a student’s assignment, track changes or insert comments, save your comments, and upload your version of the assignment back to Moodle.  The student then can view your changes and comments. IMPORTANT:  You can only track changes and insert comments in an “Advanced uploading of files” type of assignment.  (You can add comments to a student’s assignment submitted via the “Online text” type of assignment, but not track changes.) Open the Assignment and click on “View # submitted assignments.” In the student list, find the student whose work you will grade.  To open the student’s uploaded assignment, click on “Grade.”  Automatically, a “Feedback” screen will open in a new window. From this “Feedback” screen: In the lower left corner, open the student’s submitted assignment (in this case, called “Group Project 1.doc”). Save the student’s submission on your own hard drive.  Make any alteration you wish to the student’s document, using Track Changes or Insert Comment, etc. Save your version of the student’s document.  (In this case, the faculty version of the document is called “Group Project 1—FACULTY FEEDBACK.doc.”) Browse for and Upload your version of the document to the Feedback screen. Now type in comments in the text box (in this case, faculty comments begin “Dear Alter Ego, this wasn’t your best effort…”) Hit either “Save changes” to return to the assignment, or “Save and show next” to see the next student’s work. VERY IMPORTANT !! You must upload your version of the document to the Feedback screen and then type your comments in the text box.  DO NOT type your comments first, or they’ll be lost!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A way for a teacher to edit a student's file, and then upload it.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mary, Just adding a warning. Following your procedure, if an instructor spends a long time editing the .doc, Moodle may time out. The default timeout is something like 30 minutes. One way around that problem is simply to download all the students' files at the end of your step#1, work on them, and then return to your step 7. And a note to Michael, versioning control -- in the form of a recommended file naming procedure for both student and instructor -- is key to making this work. Note Mary's clearly worded examples.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Text-input assignment grading interface
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been asked if this allows grades greater than 100 points for assignments. The answer is "yes" and "no".  To change the input for the assignment setup page to allow text input is a much more intense change in order to allow for scales, no grade, etc.  So in that sense it doesn't allow you to input maximum grades greater than 100.  However... there is a common hack implemented on many sites that increases the dropdown menu for assignment grading (including maximum grade for assignment setup) to whatever the institution wants.  The "text-input assignment grading interface" makes that hack much more palatable as the instructor only uses the (VERY LONG) dropdown once, during assignment setup. The common hack for increasing the maximum grade available for assignment is: in lib/weblib.php, function print_grade_menu (around line 5600): and in lib/form/modgrade.php, function onQUickFormEvent (around line 63): set the line: for ($i= 100 ; $i>=1; $i--) { to: for ($i= 250 ; $i>=1; $i--) { (or whatever you want your maximum grade value to be for assignments)

You can delete a file by clicking on the X after its name.] If you upload a file, you MUST also insert a comment in the feedback box or the student won't be able to see your file. We don't do "grades," but please change the grade in the upper right corner above the feedback box. No grade = work not yet turned in. 0 = unacceptable or late work (not turned in yet). Follow Handbook instructions for late work. 1=student work in & critique has been posted. Save changes. For Progress and Midterm Reports, when you have uploaded/posted a report, go out to the main classroom page and click on the closed eye to open it up. Once the eye is open, the students can access your feedback by following the directions below. [If you don't see the closed eye, click on the "Turn Editing On" button on the Home page and the eye and other options will be revealed.] Send email to students and parents that your critique or report has been posted in the classroom. Be sure to instruct them how to access it and how to post a parental acknowledgment that it was read.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: URGENT!! Emails not going to teachers or students
ResponsesInList.Text: It's working! (after a bug fix). First of all, let me correct my previous statements on assignment emails: 1.  Emails to teachers are not actually generated through cron.php, but sent directly when a student uploads an assignment (or re-uploads it). 2.  Emails to students when a teacher grades (or re-grades) the assignment are sent through cron.php (actually the code is in mod/assignment/lib.php). Now to why emails to teachers were not being sent.  I think there's a "bug" in the code where emails are sent to teachers (see bug 5909 in the bug tracker). Briefly, I think the function user_group in lib/datalib.php used to return a single record using the get_record_ sql .  It now returns an array of records using get_records_sql.  I'm thinking this was done to allow a user to be a member of multiple groups. The student emails seem to be working now also. Scott

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can an instructor upload a student's file a Moodle Assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: The only way I can think of is if you have been given the permission to "log in as" another user - which under normal circumstances a regular teacher wouldn't be able to. Alternatively you might be able to upload it directly into the student's ID area of the moddata directory in your course files which holds all the students' folders of that particular assignment - but it's a bit complicate. The third alternative goes against all security measures which is to get the student to change their password and give you their log in so you can do it - then they change their password back again. But I would really not advise that. Why can they not do it themselves?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can an instructor upload a student's file a Moodle Assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume she wants to manually upload because the due date has passed for the assignment, so the student cannot upload himself. You can do this as follows: Go to the assignment page and note what the assignment number is (it's a number that varies for each assignment and is typically 4 digits long; if you're not sure which number it is, check a few other assignments and note which number in the file path is the same for all of them). Then mouse over the student and get his number as well. Now, from the class page of the moodle, go to "files" and then select "moddata" and then select the proper folder for the assignment according to the number you found above. Peruse the folders and see if the student has a folder named after his student number. If not, create it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Group Assignment, a first shot
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, We needed some way at our school to set up group assignments, i.e. one user uploads the file but all the members of his or her group "benefit" from the submission. Also, for the teacher we wanted to allow for group grading, i.e. assign the grade and give feedback only once for all the students in a group. Here is our first shot at solving this issue, with some caveats: It works under 1.5.2+ as of today (Sept 13, 2005), and has only been moderately tested. It copies files from one user file area to the file areas of his or her colleagues. A more elegant way would probably consist of having group file areas so as to have only one copy of a submission on the disk, but ... Ignores teacher submissions Does not handle grading individuals who are not part of a group The group assignment type relies on the groups defined in the course: When groups are defined in the course, the submissions are handled by using these groups. When no groups are defined in the course, the whole class is treated as a group. We have this case in projects with only few participants (3-5). When setting up the assignment, the teacher can choose whether to grade groups (all students in a group get the same grade and feedback) or to grade individuals (allows to give different grades and feedback to the members of a group). Maybe some of you might install this and try it out, comments are welcome. We plan to have it robust and usable by mid-october.

ResponsesInList.Text: You might be interested in having students book themselves into a group before starting on the assignment. I'm using activity locking (thanks to Stuart ) and a bookings-module. The assignment is locked by the booking-module. The students can't start the assignment before they have selected a group to join. In the group-booking I can set max limit for each group. In the lock I can set that the assignment won't open before the group has at least xxx members. You can set the group-booking to either show usernames (so they can select a group with their friends) or the names can be hidden (students will only see how many there are in each group). The group-bookings module will create the groups defined in the setup (comma separated list). A student can only join one group from the list, but may be member of other groups (this can mess up the display for editing groups,- possibly confuse a few mods ... haven't checked this). The bookings-mod could be changed so that students are dropped from other groups as an option - need some testing here ...

ResponsesInList.Text: I just did a little digging...the text appears to go into the database mdl_assignment_submissions table in the data1 field. The type for this field is defined as text. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: problem with player inside assignment since upgrading
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'll clarify... When I insert the code, my video will play when I go to the page. The problem occurs when I attempt to update the resource. The following is the original code pasted into the html area of a label, forum posts, assignments, etc...: <script type="text/ javascript " src="https://myhost.com/vportal/scripts/videoplayer/DmsEmbedLib.js"></script><script>document.write(dmsEmbed.getSimplePlayer("C-be993db7-af87-45ac-99e6-eca8ae448987:5","https://myhost.com/vportal/VideoPlayer.jsp?ccsid=C-be993db7-af87-45ac-99e6-eca8ae448987:5#","false",480));</script> The following is the what the code gets changed into after I click on the "update" button on the resource/activity: <script src="https://myhost.com/vportal/scripts/videoplayer/DmsEmbedLib.js" type="text/javascript"></script> <script type="text/javascript">// <![CDATA[ 

document.write(dmsEmbed.getSimplePlayer("C-be993db7-af87-45ac-99e6-eca8ae448987:5"," https://myhost.com/vportal/VideoPlayer.jsp?ccsid=C-be993db7-af87-45ac-99e6-eca8ae448987:5# ","false",480));

 // ]]></script> The change in code occurs / exists both in IE and FF. The problem exists in Moodle 1.9.7, 1.9.8, and 1.9.9 (the only ones tested). The problem exists with default installations of Moodle, and with TinyMCE (replacement for htmlarea wysiwyg editor) modified installations. As noted by Bob Puffer in the a tinymce clean port thread, when I go into my profile and choose to use standard web forms, the code does not change when I choose to update the resource. Upon closer examination of the problem code, it reveals that the code begins to be re-written with the CData tag only upon the action performed on the invoked javascript . Even more revealing is that the editor uses the // to comment out the operation being performed. In this case, the operation is document.write Knowing this, it seems to me that this could imply that there is a safety feature of the Moodle editors - when code is brought from that database and put into the control area to be edited, a filter is executed that prevents the running of a javascript action within the area. It then rewrites the information to comment out the potential threat. This would be a logical safety feature as we wouldn't want students to be able to execute remote javascript on our pages. Since the script almost always works the first time, before an edit occurs, it appears as though the problem originates from the command to bring that cell's data to the control area, or the reading of the data by the editor itself. Whatever the problem is, it can't be a simple "read" problem since the data is only being rewritten when loaded for editing. I'm open to any/all suggestions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! I've been trying to work around some grade page issues we've been having. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: (I'm going to assume you're using a recent version of Moodle 1.9.....) When you add Assignment activities to the front page of your Moodle course, Moodle adds the item to the gradebook without a delete option. You'll need to delete the Assignment from the front page first. This will not automatically remove the item from the gradebook, but it should now have a delete icon next to the item when you view the categories and items view of the gradebook. You should now be able to delete the item using that view of the gradebook.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: We're using 1.9.9 so is there a way to remove a file that has been submitted by the student without deleting the entire assignment from the grade book?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Heather, It sounds like you want to remove an actual file that was uploaded by a student but not delete the assignment from the gradebook. This is doable but there are caveats. To remove the actual file you need to go into the files area of your course using the "Files" link in the administration block. Once in the files area find the "moddata" folder and enter that folder. In the moddata folder find the "assignment" folder and click on it. Now here is where it gets fun. If you have lots of assignments there will be a number of numbered folders. You need to figure out which folder holds the files for the given assignment. I haven't found an easy way to identify this folder. Once you find the correct folder, you will go into that folder and once again you will see a number of other folders. Each of these folders contains the actual files uploaded by the students, one folder for each student. The folder numbers are actually the students ID number in the Moodle database . You can find the student id by mousing over any student name in Moodle and look at the url that takes you to their profile. It will look something like this: http://yourmoodlesite.com/moodle/user/view.php?id=7&course=20 The spot that says "id=7" is the spot you are looking for. If you find a folder with the number 7 then this is the folder for that particular student. Does this make sense? Once you are in this folder you will see the file that has been uploaded and can delete it from there. The caveat is that the student will still have a score for the assignment but now no longer have an attached file. It will still show the "Last Modified (student)" date in the column but not list any files. If you want to remove the score just change it to "No grade" and save and you should be good to go. I hope this is what you are looking for. Randy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: Exactly what I needed, thanks Randy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove uploaded file
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, I misunderstood. I thought you were talking about how to remove as assignment activity from the gradebook. The default on the advanced uploading of files assignment is to allow deleting. So the student should be able to delete the individual file that needs to be deleted. That's assuming that the assignment has not been submitted for marking. If it has been submitted, the instructor has the option in the detailed grade view (click the Grade or Update button for the student in question) to release the assignment back to the student. If the instructor has admin rights on the course, s/he can log in as the student to delete the file. For the upload a single file assignment, there is no allow deleting option that I'm aware of. If you set allow updating to yes, then the student should be able to overwrite the 'bad' file with a new one.

ResponsesInList.Title: Group assignments - help!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all I posted this up on the Groups board, but maybe it's better suited to here as it directly links to Assignments. Hope you can help! Hi everyone Yesterday I spoke to a group of core tutors about some changes that we want to make to our Moodle site. A bit of background.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group assignments - help!
ResponsesInList.Text: If you want students taking the same course from a number of different teachers to have the same program of study then using what I call cohesive Moodle course is the wayto go.  All teachers use the same resources (though they may add their own also if it accomplishes the same learning outcome) and give the same tests etc.  This has the added advantage of producing data about student outcome in the course allowing it to be used in evaluating teachers (though I would not necessarily focus on that).  To get teachers to accept this model will require some up front training and discussion of benefit to students.  I have taught in this model for a number of years and like the collaboration process that it requires.  With all of the free online resources for working collaboratively it should not be a problem for teachers at different geographic locations to work as a team.  Two heads are better than one and when uploading etc the individual teacher does not have to do all the work. Warning though-teachers will likely balk at the idea initially so it may need to be presented as a requirement to get it started. Hope this helps, Kathy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Group assignments - help!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Dan, If I understand you correctly, this information might help. While we don't run a national system here, we have and do use groups extensively with quite a lot of success. Mostly found in the general math and English classes, our teachers run multiple sections of say Algebra 1 or English Lit 1. The sections (or Periods since the sections are taught at different periods during the day) are ALL the exact same curriculum and so teachers don't want to setup 7 courses (one for each section or period)... the answer is Groups. We ran this way last year and our teachers reported no problems with either students seeing other class work or teacher having issues managing the courses. The only issue that was initially raised was a question of pacing. That is, one class (or section or period) getting ahead of another class. This is only an issue if the teacher did not want to "expose" the next topic until a specific assignment was complete or date had passed. Hope that helped...

ResponsesInList.Title: Second marker
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi folks, I have been asked by one of our academic departments if it is possible to provide a second marker facility for assignments on Moodle. Is anyone aware of such a system, or have any ideas how this might be implemented? As I understand it, the request would require those performing the marking to be unable to view the other markers marks until they has marked an assignment. Presumably it would have to be a course setting to determine the number of markers as (for example) it might be that one lecturer and one of (possibly many) tutors would mark each assignment so there might be far more people with edit rights on the course than those required to mark each piece of work. I look forward to your comments Anthony Head of IT University of Buckingham

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Second marker
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, This is what we do which is largely driven by anonymous marking requirements. Submitted assignments are output to hard copy Tutor 1 Marks the assignment and completes an rtf document which has sufficient blank progiving detailed feedback to the student. Tutor 2 reviews the hardcopy and Tutor 1's comments. The rtf document is sent to the administrator who then uploads the right set of comments for each student using the "grade"option I realise that this is fiddly and involves outputting to hardcopy but we have resistance from tutors to reading and composing feedback on line.  You need to have two windows open to be able to do this and this reduces the amount of script viewable. This is probably not terribly helpful but Moodles participative approach to learning does not fit well with HE requirements for anonimity. If anyone comes up with a way of first or second marking without the student identity being disclosed it would be good to hear how they are doing it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Second marker
ResponsesInList.Text: We have to moderate work, currently we have to download the exemplars that we want to use, distribute them to staff, collect in the marks, compare discuss and then revisit any marking that we think might need updating in light of the moderation. If would be nice to have the ability to select work to be marked by a second or third member of staff and then to be able to compare the marks and comments before deciding on a final set of marks, but retaining the process for review later, keeping this process anonymous would also help, with only a nominated course leader being able to identify comments if needed. The only way I can think to do this in moodle would be to use a peer-assessment module or workshop in a staff only course, which would require a lot of setting up. The ability to reuse one of these facilities within a course would be great, could it be done with roles or groupings.

ResponsesInList.Title: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: We are currently reviewing role definitions in terms of privacy/ethical issues. One of our roles (Content Developer) has the purpose of assisting a tutor in uploading and populating a course area with resources. Normally, persons with this role would be administrative staff of our University. We have already managed to limit access to several items, such as forum postings, participants' profile info, grades etc. We even restricted them from viewing/grading/editing assignments. Testing this role: I tried accessing assignments from the 'Assignments' module. Access was restricted... good! Despite allowing role to manage general files from the File Manager (which was our intention), when I tried opening an assignment from the moddata folder, access was restricted... GREAT! Then... out of curiosity, I tried moving an assignment out of the moddata folder. Not only could I move it, but then I could also open it! - OUCH ! Furthermore, I could upload /delete assignments in/from moddata folders. In turn, data would change accordingly when viewing submitted assignments in the 'Assignments' module! - OUCH x2! So, practically, setting the ' mod/assignment:submit ' and ' mod/assignment:view ' capabilities to PROHIBIT was a redundant move, if setting moodle/course:managefiles to ALLOW. Did anybody encounter this issue? Any solutions? If not, I do believe that there is very big loophole in this, and must be addressed accordingly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Chris, I may be being too simplistic. >One of our roles (Content Developer) has the purpose of assisting a tutor in uploading and populating a course area with resources. Normally, persons with this role would be administrative staff of our University. Could you not simply remove the role/person once the course has been established? Doesn't FERPA allow institutionally connected people to see this stuff? Similar to a Registration clerk printing out a transcript.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, it is true that Content Developers could be removed when a course has been established... but most of the courses run on our Moodle server are a work-in-progress. As for FERPA, I am not so aware of this... from what I googled, I think it is some US law, which obviously does not affect us in Malta (Europe). Furthermore, from what I can understand, information can be made available to Administrative staff 'who require access to educational records in order to perform their legitimate educational duties' (cited here ). Admin staff do not require access to assignments. Apart from the above discussion, I seriously think that Moodle has a flaw in Assignment restriction. It developed the capability (in Define Role) which impedes a role from accessing assignments, but this may be easily bypassed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Correct. In the US the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act regulations (FERPA) protects student information. This is why anyone working in an Administrative position generally signs a confidentiality agreement because it IS part of our job function to often troubleshoot specific problems with any number of the assignment functions within courses offered via MOODLE. I would imagine that most countries have specific laws and rules and your code bases may require specific changes to facilitate individual needs. That's what so great about open source!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Barbara (and Ben) for your reply. THOUGH, my point is not about the policy of access/privacy, but I am trying to make moodle developers aware of a big technical flaw in moodle. You cannot set a role to have managing capability of Files section and restrict access to assignments (there is a specific capability for this) at the same time. I am sure that when the assignment capability was created, developers had in mind to also restrict assignment access from the Files section (moddata folder). Otherwise, we moddata files would not be resticted as they currently are. But the backdoor to this restiction is simply to move the files outside of moddata folder. My point is that Assignments are not protected, despite having a dedicated moodle capability for it .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, Moodle 1.9 is working as intended. The assumption is that if you trust someone enough to access all files, you trust them enough to access all the assignment files. Now that is not the best assumption to make, which is why file handling has been completely rewritten for Moodle 2.0.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, thanks for the info... so, in Moodle 2.0, file handling rights will be detatched from assignment (moddata) folder access? Thus, is this being already considered? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle 2.0, there is no moddata! The way files are stored on disc is completely changed (with the nice side effect that if the same file is uploaded twice, it is only stored on disc once). Each file also has information stored in the database , in a way that relates the file to how it is used, so "This file is Student X's assignment submission", "This file is a forum attachment", "This file is part of the feedback on this quiz question", ... (so in the previous example, if one file is uploaded twice, in different places, it is stored on disc once, but there are two entries in the file table, one for each use). Because we know exactly what each file belongs to, the access control can be precise. If a file is a forum attachment, then you can get the file only if you are allowed to see that forum post. If a file is a student's assignment, you can get the file only if you are allowed to access that student's assignment submission.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: BIG loophole in Assignment privacy
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the great news, Tim!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Indicating which lessons/activities a student has taken
ResponsesInList.Text: There's a new checklist module that might be of interest to you http://docs.moodle.org/en/Checklist_module In Moodle 2.0 there will be completion (progress) tracking which will "tick off" activities once students have completed them - either automatically or manually

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Indicating which lessons/activities a student has taken
ResponsesInList.Text: We use the Lesson activity to sequence quizzes and assignments. As the student goes through the lesson, they come to a page that links to a quiz or to an assignment. We have experimented with putting the lessons in the sections above the "fold" and the activities in sections below the fold. For example, Lesson 1 goes into Section 1, but quizzes and assignments for Lesson1 go down in section 8 or 9. In fact, you can also totally hide activities by putting them in the last section and then reducing the number of sections in classroom settings by one. You can also use Update this lesson to choose an activity to jump to when students complete their lesson.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Indicating which lessons/activities a student has taken
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, and Lesson actually remembers which page the user was on last (not for teachers and admins, though). So, what you do is link back to the first page of the lesson from your other activity. Lesson politely asks user if they wish to resume where they left off. User says yes, and they go to the Lesson page they last viewed.

ResponsesInList.Text: I have been trying to figure out the best way to set up a grade book that will allow an assignment to be in multiple categories. As a school wide plan we have agreed to assess students in the following weighted categories - ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Category 01: Work Ethic                             Weight: 10 Category 02: Collaboration                          Weight: 10 Category 03: Written Communication             Weight: 30 Category 04: Oral Communication                  Weight: 10 Category 05: Content                                 Weight: 40 So some assignments will be assessing the students in all of the categories and others in only some of the categories.  The sample list below shows how some assignments would be in one category and others are in multiple categories. Assignments                                                01      02      03      04      05 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Presentation Notes                                     0/30     /0      /0      /0      /0 Oral Presentations                                      0/75   0/50   0/25   0/25   0/25 Rough Draft-Peer Check                               0/50     /0      /0      /0      /0 Rough Draft-Content Check                            /0      /0      /0      /0    0/40 Collaboration Points-Group Division                   /0     0/50     /0      /0      /0 Is there a way to create an assignment so that it is in each of the categories and  can be assigned a different value?  And only create one assignment? I have looked at outcomes and that is the same for each time something is associated with that outcome- so that won't work. I looked at Rubrics- and that will only allow the areas to be weighted for that individual assignment and I can not look at how they are doing collectively within a category. Right now I see the only solution is to create the Oral Presentation assignment five times once in each category so that it will add to the weighted grade. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating Assignments in Multiple Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: >Right now I see the only solution is to create the Oral Presentation assignment five times once in each category so that it will add to the weighted grade. From a brief look at what you're trying to do I would have to agree that you need to create 5 iterations of the Oral Presentation each with a different grade. This might not be too difficult using the Sharing Cart though which would allow you to duplicate the assignment and then change the associated grade. Check out the Downloads -> Modules and plugins page for Sharing Cart. The latest version can only be obtained via CVS apparently but if you're stuck contact me and I can get it to you. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating Assignments in Multiple Categories
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Julia Have you looked at using Outcomes ? From Moodle Docs : Outcomes are specific descriptions of what a student is expected to be able to do or understand at the completion of an activity or course. An activity might have more than one outcome, and each may have a grade against it (usually on a scale ). Other terms for Outcomes are Competencies and Goals . In simple terms an Outcome is like any other grade except that it can be applied to multiple activities . When the activity is marked, a mark should be given for the submission itself and for the outcome." They need to be enabled at site level and each outcome appears as a separate item in the gradebook so you can provide different weightings. I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Text: Another way that you could go about this is to have a one shared course - it could be a meta course (in Moodle terms ) - for all the classes of the same year group. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turnitin moodle plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there... We had exactly the same problem where we were unable to delete the turnitin type assignment from a moodle course. It turned out that it was our proxy server blocking the connection. As our IT department were not prepared to alter how the proxy server worked (and we got very limited support from the developers), we decided to try to alter the code ourselves. We managed to get it to work by altering the following code within tiirequest.class.php (bold signifies where the changes have occured): function TIIRequest($apiCall) { $opts = array('http'=>array('request_full_uri'=>true,'proxy'=>'tcp://your.proxyserver.ac.uk:yourproxyportnumber')); $ context = stream_context_create($opts); $this->_xml_parser = xml_parser_create(); if (!($this->_fp = fopen($apiCall, "r", false, $context))) { die("could not open XML input [$apiCall]"); } $this->_data =''; while (!feof($this->_fp)) { $this->_data .= fread($this->_fp, 8192); } fclose($this->_fp); xml_parse_into_struct($this->_xml_parser, $this->_data, $this->_vals, $this->_index); xml_parser_free($this->_xml_parser); } Please note this fix will only work with php 5.1.0 or later as this is when they integrated proxy support for the fopen function. Another thing we have noticed is when using turnitin with moodle 1.9, if you have AJAX turned on (the drag and drop functionality) it seems to break the deleting which I assume will affect everybody. Best Regards - Richard Sanders Newman University College

That can usually be solved by trying the following: * Make sure that the php.ini file that your apache/Moodle instance uses has the "allow_url_fopen" option set to "On" * make sure that you have openssl installed on your Moodle server * To get PHP to use open ssl. The php.ini file needs to have the extension added: extension=php_openssl.dll Also, please make sure that your Moodle server can make outgoing https calls to our Turnitin servers. If all of that is enabled/works, and you still get the "could not open XML input" error, please let me know. Also, I think changing the assignment type is only something that can be done pre-Moodle 1.8. After 1.8, it doesn't look like it's possible to change an assignment type after it's been created. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Separate groups not showing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We have this problem too but I think I have solved it - at least for our site ! There is an error in the sql statement in lib/accesslib.php.  I have only tested it where the role assigned to the members of the groups is the same as the default role for the site.  In this case the where statement refers to ra.userid ( from the mdl_role_assignments table ) but in this case the table does not appear in the SQL statement.  Hence the sql fails, nothing is returned and so the error statement appears. I have only just put the fix into our system and am awaiting feedback from our users.  However it would be good if someone else could try it. We are on moodle version 1.9.4 In lib/accesslib.php change the get_users_by_capability function as below so that when the default role is in effect, the ra.userid is replaced by u.id : /// Groups if ($groups) { if (is_array($groups)) { $grouptest = 'gm.groupid IN (' . implode(',', $groups) . ')'; } else { $grouptest = 'gm.groupid = ' . $groups; } if ($defaultroleinteresting) { $grouptest = 'u.id IN (SELECT userid FROM ' . $CFG->prefix . 'groups_members gm WHERE ' . $grouptest . ')'; $grouptest = 'ra.userid IN (SELECT userid FROM ' . if ($useviewallgroups) { $viewallgroupsusers = get_users_by_capability($ context , 'moodle/site:accessallgroups', 'u.id, u.id', '', '', '', '', $exceptions); if ($defaultroleinteresting) { $wherecond['groups'] =  '('. $grouptest . ' OR u.id IN (' . implode(',', array_keys($viewallgroupsusers)) . '))'; } else { $wherecond['groups'] =  '('. $grouptest . ' OR ra.userid IN (' . implode(',', array_keys($viewallgroupsusers)) . '))'; } } else { $wherecond['groups'] =  '(' . $grouptest .')'; } } Any feedback most welcome

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to assign same course to different teacher with difference student in moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to use groups - in the course administration block of that course first click on assign roles and click teacher and move over the 4 teachers from the block on the right to the block on the left. They are now in the course. Then click on student and move the students from the block on the right to the block on the left. The students are now in the course as well. Then go to the course administration block and click on groups. Click "create group" - give your first class a name and then click " add group members" and move the students and their one teacher across from the block on the right to the block on the left. Now you have one group/class with their teacher. Do the same with the other classes. (In settings in your course admin block you need to have groups enabled) OR.. if this is too much hard work, you can just assign the 4 teachers to this class in the way I said above and then use a group enrolment key which you give the students to type in and they enrol themselves directly into the group. See here for how to do that

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot Grade an assignment
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chrissy, That is because you have altered the grade directly form the "Grader Report Table". This will automatically flag on the overridden box. When on, the overridden flag prevents any future attempts to automatically adjust the value of the grade. This flag is often set internally by the grade book, but can be switched on and off the flag manually. To switch on and off the overridden flag - From the "Administration" block select "Grades" make sure you are in the "Grader Report" - select "Turn editing on" - Select "Edit grade" icon, the intersection between student name and assignment name. - Uncheck the "Overridden" box - Select "Save changes" Now you should be able to choose student grade from the dropdown menu. Hope it will work for you, Hanaa.

When we need to create these assignments in whatever course, we just backup whatever we need from the Template course, restore (by adding) to the real course, then go in and change the assignment name. I realized that going into the database to change the assignment name saved even more time (a 'duh' after I thought about it), but found also that the old name still appeared when you went back to the actual Moodle course. The old name continued to appear (regardless of session or user) until I accessed the assignment (via 'edit' ) from within the course. It still saves time in that you don't have to edit, type and update each assignment, just click edit then save. I'll sure there's an SQL statement that would handle this for us, or there may be a cache or sessions settings I'm missing, but I haven't figured it out yet. (Suggestions would be welcome!) Note: I've been out of the Moodling Mode for a few months, so I'm a bit rusty - I may not be recalling the specifics of the old name/new name appearance exactly right - I'm actually thinking now it might be other database changes that seem to require accessing assignments via Moodle before they're visible to the user (like grades or other settings). Nevertheless, if you use this method and run into something similar, you might try accessing/editing in Moodle to update.

"Sharing cart" really describes what it does as it very powerful and flexible. So, don't despair. Get Sharing Cart installed (it's in the database of Modules/Blocks) and all your duplication problems will be sorted!

ResponsesInList.Text: The problem with lost colon in C:\ is related to PARAM_PATH and the line: $file = optional_param('file', '', PARAM_PATH); Therefore, this asignment type will not work on Windows server. I would suggest to assign to $file only the part without CFG-> dataroot and to join them together just before delete operation. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teachers can't see the students submitted assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: Check to make sure that no one went in and changed the names of the folders in moddata. We recently had a case like this and discovered the instructor had renamed the folder "3265" to "Homework 1". He did that after all of the submissions were made so he could later go and download the whole folder at once and know which one it was. Basically, the folder name should be the same as the assignment ID used in the database , and all of the submissions should be the number Moodle uses to identify the user in the database. It's not a user friendly naming convention, but it's not supposed to be. I hope this helps. Greg

Attached (bottom left, below) is an icon to identify these files - add this to either moodle/pics/f or moodle/yourtheme/pics/f (depending on where your icons are being pulled from), and then make a copy of it renamed ist.gif (for templates) and add that as well; then add the following lines to moodle/lib/filelib.php (the extensions array takes up lines 40-170 in this file, add the two lines below anywhere in this array; make sure that each line in this array except the last is followed by a comma): 'isf' => array ('type'=>'application/inspiration', 'icon'=>'isf.gif'), 'ist' => array ('type'=>'application/inspiration.template', 'icon'=>'ist.gif') perhaps some of you using Inspiration might find this helpful. (Do the same for any other file type you use commonly, using a 16x16pxl icon in .gif format - e.g., I've got icons set up for OmniGraffle templates & files, as well).

ResponsesInList.Title: OmniGraffle file icon
ResponsesInList.Text: Here, similarly, is an icon for OmniGraffle files (attached, bottom left); the line to be added to the extensions array in moodle/lib/filelib.php is: 'graffle' => array ('type'=>'application/graffle', 'icon'=>'graffle.gif') (again, each line except the last in the array needs to be followed by a comma)

However... we have done the opposite by removing the single upload assignment type. We saw the Advanced duplicated the Single and our staff likes the response files option.
```text
$CFG->assignment_hide_uploadsingle = true;
```

```text
$standardassignments = array('upload','online','uploadsingle','offline');
```
 I changed it to 
```text
$standardassignments = array('online','uploadsingle','offline');
```
 I have to say at this point I'm not a programmer but can 'read' code (to a certain point!). I HIGHLY recommend you make a note somewhere of this change so you know what has be done in case things go wrong! It will also need to be changed and fully tested again after a Moodle upgrade. I've altered the name of this thread in the hopes someone with more Moodle programming knowledge will come in and confirm/fix the suggestion I've made! I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Providing feedback documents to students without initial  student upload
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, Mark, we use advanced uploading with kids down to grade 2 to do exactly what you are doing. AND, what's worse, we invite their digital immigrant parents to "sign off" that they have read the file. Here are the instructions we give our instructors. We have really no trouble with this at all. How to Post Feedback Write your report (unless you plan to paste it in the feedback box). Go to Grades. Click on the name of the report (e.g., Lesson X Feedback, Midterm Report, Progress Report). Upload the file or cut and paste into box. [ FYI , right now you and the student can both upload 3 files max per assignment. You can delete a file by clicking on the X after its name.] Even if you upload a file, you MUST also insert a comment in the feedback box or the student won't be able to see your file. We don't do "grades," but you may choose to use a range of quality scale ("Novice, Apprentice, Proficient") or something similar found in the upper right corner above feedback box. Save changes. When you have uploaded/posted comments for all your students, go out to the main classroom page and click on the closed eye to open it up. Once the eye is open, the students will have access to your feedback in the classroom by following the directions below. [If you don't see the closed eye, click on the "Turn Editing On" button on the Home page and the eye and other options will be revealed.] Send email to students and parents to let them know that your feedback has been posted in the classroom. Be sure to instruct them how to access the feedback in the classroom and how to post a parental acknowledgment that the feedback was read. How Student and Parent Access Instructor Feedback Students and parents: 1. Log into the course and click on Lesson _ Feedback 2. Students: Please read the Feedback (If the instructor provides individualized feedback in the form of an attachment, be sure to click on the attachment icon on the bottom left of the page). 3. Parents: Please scroll down to the end of the Feedback page--not to the end of any attachment-- to the Notes section, click on Edit, enter your name and comments, and click on Save Changes. This Note lets the instructor know that you have read the feedback for that lesson.

ResponsesInList.Title: Turnitin integration - how is it being used with students?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan Marsden has developed a Moodle integration with Turnitin that retains student work within Moodle. The existing discussion thread focuses on beta-testing the technical issues, but I'd like to have a discussion about how the policy/education aspect of the integration are being applied. For instance - we are only just introducing Turnitin at my organisation and there is much trepidation being shown by students during the pilot phase. We are of course doing training and info sessions focusing on the key issue being adequate referencing etc, but the anxiety remains real. We are keen to let students have the option to test their Turnitin scores for an essay before final submission and the integration allows this. We see this as a healthy step in students getting to grips with what plagiarism is and appropriate referencing. But we don't want to get into a situation where a student submits work multiple times as they repeatedly "tweak" wording. So the only way we can think of implementing a limit on re-submission is to: Create a special "Turnitin draft submit" assignment module within a course. Using the advanced uploading of files assignment with deletions turned off means the teacher can control the number of repeat submissions e.g. 1 per assignment, 4 assignments within course = 4 Turnitin draft submissions. Students can see their Turnitin reports, act on them and then submit final assessment in the separate "Assignment 1 submission area". It adds some admin work for the teacher, but gives some assurance to the students. We would implement this option for first year courses and reduce/eliminate it for 2nd/3rd year ones. Is anyone else allowing students to see Turnitin results upon file upload and using this or other ways to manage it? Cheers David

ResponsesInList.Title: Multi Submit and Multi feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a member of staff who requires an assignment submission with the process.... Student submits assignment, Staff provides feedback Student resubmits improved assignment, Staff provides feedback Student resubmits assignment, staff provides feedback, repeating until a final point reached where the last submitted assignment would be the one to be marked. One of the requirements is that each submission/feedback cycle needs to be retained so that the various versions and changes can be reviewed at the end. At the moment the resubmissions override previous versions as does the feedback. Is it possible to do anything like this using anything currently available.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multi Submit and Multi feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a patch which I think does exactly what you want. In the attached ZIP file you will find two files 1) lib.php should be placed in /mod/assignment (replacing existing file). It captures all submissions and stores them in a separate folder structure. The key code from this is the line "$this->record_submission($submission); //ALAN" and the associated "function record_submission($submission)", "function copy_dir($from_file, $to_file)" and "function copy_file($from_file, $to_file)". 2) studentsubmissions.php should be placed in /course (this is a new file). If you access the URL : http://yoursite/course/studentsubmissions.php?id=X where X is the userid of any particular student you will get a history of all submissions and a history of all grades for that student. On my site I have a way of navigating to this page for each student, but that part is specific to my site and would not work for you. Before using the above code, the relevant database table will have to be created by hand with the following SQL commands... CREATE TABLE mdl_recorded_submissions ( id BIGINT(10) unsigned NOT NULL auto_increment, This code is tested and works with the 20090520 weekly build (although that part of Moodle is stable, so I think it will work with builds going back, at least, to late September). ResponsesInList.Title: Store or Archive Assignments as Evidence
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - I am Program Manager at an RTO and am using Moodle as both a learning aid and a repository of evidence of competency for Certificate courses.  We need to store evidence for 30 years as a compliance with the AQTF. Does anyone know how I can retrieve the text and uploaded files and archive them (PDF is preferred by govt.), other than going assignment by assignment, student by student? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Store or Archive Assignments as Evidence
ResponsesInList.Text: I empathize with your situation. I used to be an RTO compliance officer. The AQTF archive requirement is tricky to implement with any technology solution as no file type can be guaranteed to be in use for that period of time. As we all know, PDF didn't exist 30 years ago so, regardless of the govt's (current) preference for PDF, we have no way of knowing that it will be readable in 30 year's time from now. Even putting aside the questions of file type, there is also the storage medium to consider. CD, DVD and tape are likely to be obsolete well within that timeframe. Magnetic hard-drives have had the longest lifespan so far, but operating systems evolve inexorably, with backward compatibility more and more problematic. So whatever solution you pick you will need to keep updating and re-outputting your data to whatever the current file storage type and medium happens to be. That could turn into a logistic nightmare over time, with error and data loss highly probable. In practical terms you are unlikely to need to frequent access VET /AQTF records over 5 years old. My recommendation is keep everything within the normal Moodle data structure (or whatever electronic system you use) for records up to that period, and output them only on an as-required basis (i.e. audit or query purposes). Use normal electronic backup to protect this data - whether Moodle's own course or site backup (which can easily be automated) or whole-of- domain backup (which can also be automated). That will satisfy the AQTF requirement for the short-to-medium term. For records older than that, use one of the Moodle report outputs to print them to paper and store them physically. It sounds backward, but it's really the simplest solution and ultimately probably the cheapest. At worst, paper can always be scanned again. The 5 year figure comes from thinking about how long you are likely to be operating any kind of LMS or CMS. It's a good, practical business and data planning timeframe. Most likely, either Navitas will move on from Moodle over that time, or else Moodle will itself evolve to the point that it will need to dispense with total backward compatibility to its own earliest versions. The AQTF 30 year archive requirement is a classic case of bureaucratic regulation which is actually impossible to comply with - unless you output to paper. I know that sounds a little negative but I hope that helps. Mike Smith Brisbane, Australia
